LayoutTransform

inline LayoutTransform forZScore(
    float mean,
    float std_dev
)
Z-score normalization where output = (value - mean) / std_dev.
Parameters:

mean Data mean value
std_dev Data standard deviation

Return: Transform that applies z-score normalization
Centers data at 0, scales so ±1 = ±1 standard deviation. Useful for comparing signals with different baselines and amplitudes.



inline LayoutTransform forPeakToPeak(
    float data_min,
    float data_max,
    float target_min =-1.0f,
    float target_max =1.0f
)
Map [data_min, data_max] → [target_min, target_max].
Parameters:

data_min Minimum value in data
data_max Maximum value in data
target_min Desired minimum output (default: -1)
target_max Desired maximum output (default: 1)

Return: Transform that maps data range to target range
Peak-to-peak normalization for fitting data into a known range. Default maps to [-1, 1].



inline LayoutTransform forStdDevRange(
    float mean,
    float std_dev,
    float num_std_devs =3.0f
)
±N standard deviations from mean map to ±1
Parameters:

mean Data mean value
std_dev Data standard deviation
num_std_devs Number of standard deviations that map to ±1 (default: 3)

Return: Transform that maps ±N std_devs to ±1
Common for neural data visualization where 3 std_devs → full display range. Data at mean maps to 0, data at mean ± N*std_dev maps to ±1.



inline LayoutTransform forUnitRange(
    float target_min =-1.0f,
    float target_max =1.0f
)
Map [0, 1] input range to arbitrary output range.
Parameters:

target_min Desired minimum output (default: -1)
target_max Desired maximum output (default: 1)

Return: Transform that maps [0,1] to [target_min, target_max]
For data that’s already normalized to [0, 1].



inline LayoutTransform forPercentileRange(
    float low_value,
    float high_value,
    float target_min =-1.0f,
    float target_max =1.0f
)
Percentile-based normalization.
Parameters:

low_value Value at low percentile (e.g., 5th percentile)
high_value Value at high percentile (e.g., 95th percentile)
target_min Desired minimum output (default: -1)
target_max Desired maximum output (default: 1)

Return: Transform that maps percentile range to target range
Maps [low_percentile_value, high_percentile_value] to [-1, 1]. Useful for robust normalization that ignores outliers.



inline LayoutTransform forCentered(
    float center,
    float gain =1.0f
)
Center data at specified value, with optional gain.
Parameters:

center Value that maps to 0
gain Scale factor (default: 1)

Return: Transform that centers at specified value
Output = (value - center) * gain



inline LayoutTransform manual(
    float gain,
    float offset
)
Manual gain and offset specification.
Parameters:

gain Scale factor
offset Translation

Return: Transform with specified gain and offset
For full user control: output = value * gain + offset

Mapper for raster plots (PSTH/spike raster style visualization).
Transforms event data with relative time positioning. Unlike TimeSeriesMapper which uses absolute time for X coordinates, RasterMapper computes X as the relative offset from a reference event.
This mapper is used for:

PSTH raster plots: events aligned to stimulus/behavior
Multi-trial visualizations: each trial in a separate row
Event-centered analysis: spikes aligned to action potentials

Key difference from TimeSeriesMapper:

X = (event_time - reference_time), not absolute time
Y = row_index (from RowLayoutStrategy), not stacked position

std::vector< float > gatherAndExecutePipeline(
    DataTypeVariant const & source,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline const & pipeline
)
Gather source data over intervals and execute a pipeline on each gathered view, returning one float per interval.
Parameters:

source Source data wrapped in a DataTypeVariant
intervals DigitalIntervalSeries defining the row intervals
pipeline TransformPipeline to execute on each gathered view. Should end with a range reduction that collapses the gathered data to a single scalar.

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the source type does not satisfy HasDataTraits or if extractSingleFloat() fails on the pipeline output

Return: std::vector with one element per interval
For each interval i the function:

Creates a GatherResult view/copy of the source data within [intervals[i].start, intervals[i].end].
Executes pipeline steps on that gathered view (T → DataTypeVariant), including JSON-loaded container steps.
Applies the terminal range reduction to the step output.

If the source data and intervals use different TimeFrames, GatherResult converts interval boundaries to the source coordinate system when each view is created.
Dispatch is fully type-erased: the function visits the DataTypeVariant and uses GatherResult::create() + executePipeline() for each concrete contained type that supports gather.

Called after executing a range-reduction pipeline on one gathered interval view. The pipeline’s output should be a single-element AnalogTimeSeries (when the reduction produces a scalar) or a RaggedAnalogTimeSeries (for ragged intermediate results).

std::vector< float > gatherAndExecutePipeline(
    DataTypeVariant const & source,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline const & pipeline
)
Gather source data over intervals and execute a pipeline on each gathered view, returning one float per interval.
Parameters:

source Source data wrapped in a DataTypeVariant
intervals DigitalIntervalSeries defining the row intervals
pipeline TransformPipeline to execute on each gathered view. Should end with a range reduction that collapses the gathered data to a single scalar.

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the source type does not satisfy HasDataTraits or if extractSingleFloat() fails on the pipeline output

Return: std::vector with one element per interval
For each interval i the function:

Creates a GatherResult view/copy of the source data within [intervals[i].start, intervals[i].end].
Executes pipeline steps on that gathered view (T → DataTypeVariant), including JSON-loaded container steps.
Applies the terminal range reduction to the step output.

If the source data and intervals use different TimeFrames, GatherResult converts interval boundaries to the source coordinate system when each view is created.
Dispatch is fully type-erased: the function visits the DataTypeVariant and uses GatherResult::create() + executePipeline() for each concrete contained type that supports gather.

Mapper for spatial data (SpatialOverlay-style visualization).
Transforms spatial data (PointData, LineData) directly to world-space coordinates. Unlike TimeSeriesMapper, X and Y coordinates come directly from the data’s spatial coordinates, not from time conversion.

Scatter plots: displaying point clouds
Any visualization where X/Y are spatial, not temporal

All methods return ranges for zero-copy single-traversal consumption.

title: CorePlotting::SpatialMapper
CorePlotting::SpatialMapper
text:
Mapper for spatial data (SpatialOverlay-style visualization).
Transforms spatial data (PointData, LineData) directly to world-space coordinates. Unlike TimeSeriesMapper, X and Y coordinates come directly from the data’s spatial coordinates, not from time conversion.
This mapper is used for:

SpatialOverlay: displaying points, lines, masks over video frames
Scatter plots: displaying point clouds
Any visualization where X/Y are spatial, not temporal

All methods return ranges for zero-copy single-traversal consumption.

Priority (most restrictive wins):

Model FixedBatch{N>1} → min=N, max=N, forced_by_recurrent=false

)

params Post-encoder slot configuration from state or session.

Modules that collapse spatial dimensions (per [PostEncoderModuleRegistry](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1PostEncoderModuleRegistry.md) metadata, i.e. [B,C,H,W] →[B,C]) restrict output decoders to [FeatureVectorDecoderParams](/api_generated/Classes/structdl_1_1FeatureVectorDecoderParams.md) only. module_key``"none" permits every decoder variant.

Enumerator
Value
Description




Inferno

Dark-to-bright, perceptually uniform (default for heatmaps).


Viridis

Blue-green-yellow, perceptually uniform (default for spectrograms).


Magma

Dark-to-pink, perceptually uniform.


Plasma

Blue-to-yellow, perceptually uniform.


Coolwarm

Diverging blue-white-red (for z-scores).


Grayscale

Simple black-to-white.


Hot

Black-red-yellow-white (high contrast).



Available colormap presets.
Perceptually uniform sequential colormaps (Inferno, Viridis, Magma, Plasma) are from the matplotlib collection and are designed for accurate perception of magnitude differences. Coolwarm is a diverging colormap centered at white, suitable for signed data (e.g., z-scores).

A colormap is a function from [0, 1] → RGBA.

A lookup table of RGB values (alpha is always 1.0).

lut 256-entry RGB lookup table

    ColormapPreset preset
)
Get a ColormapFunction for the given preset.
Parameters:

preset Colormap preset to use

Return: Callable that maps [0,1] → glm::vec4 (RGBA, alpha=1)

    ColormapFunction const & cmap,
    float value,
    float vmin,
    float vmax
)
Map a scalar value through a colormap with explicit range.
Parameters:

cmap Colormap function
value Scalar value to map
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

Return: RGBA color
Normalises value to [0,1] using (value - vmin) / (vmax - vmin), clamps the result, and evaluates the colormap.

    float vmin,
    float vmax
)

cmap Colormap function
values Flat array of scalar values (row-major if matrix)
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

std::vector< glm::vec4 > mapMatrix(
    ColormapFunction const & cmap,
    std::span< double const > values,
    std::size_t num_rows,
    std::size_t num_cols,
    float vmin,
    float vmax
)
Map a row-major matrix of scalar values to RGBA colors.
Parameters:

cmap Colormap function
values Flat row-major matrix of values (size = num_rows × num_cols)
num_rows Number of rows
num_cols Number of columns
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

Return: Vector of RGBA colors, size = num_rows × num_cols
Convenience wrapper around mapValues() — the matrix is treated as a flat array. The row/column parameters are provided for documentation clarity and future validation.






std::size_t LUT_SIZE = 256;
Number of entries in a colormap lookup table.

cmap Colormap function
value Scalar value to map
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

Return: RGBA color

    ColormapFunction const & cmap,
    std::span< double const > values,
    float vmin,
    float vmax
)

Parameters:

cmap Colormap function
values Flat array of scalar values (row-major if matrix)
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

Return: Vector of RGBA colors, same length as values



std::vector< glm::vec4 > mapMatrix(
    ColormapFunction const & cmap,
    std::span< double const > values,
    std::size_t num_rows,
    std::size_t num_cols,
    float vmin,
    float vmax
)
Map a row-major matrix of scalar values to RGBA colors.
Parameters:

cmap Colormap function
values Flat row-major matrix of values (size = num_rows × num_cols)
num_rows Number of rows
num_cols Number of columns
vmin Minimum of the data range
vmax Maximum of the data range

Return: Vector of RGBA colors, size = num_rows × num_cols
Convenience wrapper around mapValues() — the matrix is treated as a flat array. The row/column parameters are provided for documentation clarity and future validation.

inline CorePlotting::LayoutTransform composeAnalogYTransform(
    CorePlotting::SeriesLayout const & layout,
    float data_mean,
    float std_dev,
    float intrinsic_scale,
    float user_scale_factor,
    float user_vertical_offset,
    float global_y_scale,
    float margin_factor =0.8f
)
Compose Y transform for analog series rendering.
Parameters:

margin_factor Fraction of allocated lane height used for data (0..1]

Follows the pattern from CorePlotting/DESIGN.md:

Data normalization (z-score style: maps ±3σ to ±1)
User adjustments (intrinsic scale, user scale, vertical offset)
Layout positioning (from LayoutEngine)
Global scaling (from ViewState) - applied to amplitude only, NOT position

IMPORTANT: Global Y scale scales the data amplitude within each lane, but does NOT move the lane center. This is achieved by applying global scaling to the gain component only, after composing data normalization with layout positioning.

    CorePlotting::SeriesLayout const & layout,
    float margin_factor,
    float global_y_scale
)
Compose Y transform for event series (stacked mode).

    float viewport_y_min,
    float viewport_y_max,
    float margin_factor
)
Compose Y transform for event series (full canvas mode).



inline float computeEventGlyphSize(
    CorePlotting::LayoutTransform const & composed_event_y_transform,
    float lane_half_height,
    float event_height,
    float margin_factor,
    float fallback_line_thickness
)
Compute glyph size for event ticks from explicit world-space event height.
The rendered tick world height is: glyph_size * composed_event_y_transform.gain
We derive glyph_size from an explicit event_height target (clamped to lane height), so event sizing remains predictable and controllable by state.



inline CorePlotting::LayoutTransform composeIntervalYTransform(
    CorePlotting::SeriesLayout const & layout,
    float margin_factor,
    float global_y_scale
)
Compose Y transform for interval series.
Note: Intervals intentionally ignore global_y_scale because:

They are already in normalized space [-1, 1] representing full height
global_y_scale is designed for scaling analog data based on std_dev
Intervals should always fill their allocated canvas space

using Neuralyzer::Plots::EstimationParams =  std::variant<BinningParams, GaussianKernelParams, CausalExponentialParams>;
Tagged union of all supported rate estimation method parameter structs.
Note: GaussianKernelParams and CausalExponentialParams are included in the variant but their implementations return empty RateEstimate (stub).
This is the single variation point for estimation method selection. Selecting a method at runtime is zero-overhead compared to a virtual base-class strategy — std::visit dispatches via a jump table.
To add a new method:

Define a new *Params struct above
Append it to this alias
Add the implementation in [EventRateEstimation.cpp](/api_generated/Files/EventRateEstimation_8cpp.md#file-eventrateestimation.cpp)

using Neuralyzer::Plots::TooltipHitTestFn = 
        std::function<std::optional<PlotTooltipHit>(QPoint screen_pos)>;
Callback that performs a hit test at a screen position.
Returns a PlotTooltipHit on success, or std::nullopt if nothing is under the cursor. This callback may perform spatial queries (QuadTree, etc.) and is only called after the dwell timer fires.

std::optional< UnitGatherContext > createUnitGatherContext(
    std::shared_ptr< DataManager > const & data_manager,
    std::string const & event_key,
    PlotAlignmentData const & alignment_data
)
Create a UnitGatherContext for a single DigitalEventSeries key.
Parameters:

data_manager DataManager containing the event and alignment series
event_key DataManager key of the [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md) to gather
alignment_data Alignment configuration (alignment key, window size, etc.)

Return: Populated [UnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1UnitGatherContext.md), or std::nullopt on failure
Calls [createAlignedGatherResult](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-createalignedgatherresult)<[DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md)> and also retrieves the source [TimeFrame](/api_generated/Classes/classTimeFrame.md). Returns std::nullopt when:

data_manager is null or event_key is empty
The gather result is empty (alignment key not found or no events in window)
The source series does not have a [TimeFrame](/api_generated/Classes/classTimeFrame.md)




std::vector< UnitGatherContext > createUnitGatherContexts(
    std::shared_ptr< DataManager > const & data_manager,
    std::vector< std::string > const & event_keys,
    PlotAlignmentData const & alignment_data
)
Create UnitGatherContexts for a batch of DigitalEventSeries keys.
Parameters:

data_manager DataManager containing the event and alignment series
event_keys DataManager keys of the [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md) to gather
alignment_data Alignment configuration shared across all units

Return: Vector of successfully gathered [UnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1UnitGatherContext.md) objects
Applies [createUnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-createunitgathercontext) to each key in event_keys with the same alignment settings. Keys for which gathering fails are silently skipped; the returned vector may therefore be shorter than event_keys.
Order is preserved: the i-th element of the result corresponds to the i-th key that succeeded.



RateEstimate estimateRate(
    GatherResult< DigitalEventSeries > const & gathered,
    TimeFrame const * time_frame,
    double window_size,
    EstimationParams const & params =BinningParams{}
)
Estimate the rate for a single unit (aggregate across trials).
Parameters:

gathered Trial-aligned views of one [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md)
time_frame TimeFrame of the source series (may be null)
window_size Total window span in time units (bins cover ±window_size/2)
params Estimation method and parameters (default: [BinningParams](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1BinningParams.md){})

Return: [RateEstimate](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimate.md) with times, values, num_trials, and metadata
Returns a [RateEstimate](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimate.md) with paired times[] (bin centers for binning) and values[] (raw event counts summed across all trials).
Uses time_frame to convert each event’s [TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md) to an absolute time before computing the relative time with respect to the per-trial alignment time from gathered.
If time_frame is null, [TimeFrameIndex::getValue()](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md#function-getvalue) is used directly as the absolute time (identity mapping).



RateEstimateWithTrials estimateRateWithTrials(
    GatherResult< DigitalEventSeries > const & gathered,
    TimeFrame const * time_frame,
    double window_size,
    EstimationParams const & params =BinningParams{}
)
Estimate rate with per-trial breakdown for a single unit.
Parameters:

gathered Trial-aligned views of one [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md)
time_frame TimeFrame of the source series (may be null)
window_size Total window span in time units
params Estimation method and parameters (default: [BinningParams](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1BinningParams.md){})

Return: [RateEstimateWithTrials](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimateWithTrials.md) with aggregate + per-trial data
Same as [estimateRate()](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate) but additionally returns per-trial rate curves in [RateEstimateWithTrials::trials](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimateWithTrials.md#variable-trials). The aggregate estimate is the trial-summed result (same as [estimateRate()](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate)), and each trial’s individual histogram is stored separately.
Use this when you need uncertainty quantification (SEM, CI, bootstrap) via the functions in [RateUncertainty.hpp](/api_generated/Files/RateUncertainty_8hpp.md#file-rateuncertainty.hpp).



std::vector< RateEstimate > estimateRates(
    std::vector< UnitGatherContext > const & units,
    double window_size,
    EstimationParams const & params =BinningParams{}
)
Estimate rates for multiple units.
Parameters:

units Per-unit gather contexts (from [createUnitGatherContexts](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-createunitgathercontexts))
window_size Total window span in time units
params Estimation method and parameters (default: [BinningParams](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1BinningParams.md){})

Return: One [RateEstimate](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimate.md) per unit, in input order
Applies [estimateRate](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate) independently to each [UnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1UnitGatherContext.md) in units. All units share the same window_size and params. The output vector is in the same order as the input and has the same length.
This is the primary entry point for [HeatmapWidget](/api_generated/Classes/classHeatmapWidget.md), which needs a units × time_bins rate matrix.

void toFiringRateHz(
    std::span< double > values,
    size_t num_trials,
    double sample_spacing,
    double time_units_per_second
)
Convert raw counts to firing rate (Hz).
Parameters:

values Value vector to modify in-place
num_trials Number of trials
sample_spacing Spacing between evaluation points (in data time units)
time_units_per_second Conversion factor (e.g. 1000.0 for milliseconds)

Formula: values[i] /= (num_trials × sample_spacing_s) where sample_spacing_s = sample_spacing / time_units_per_second

using Neuralyzer::Plots::EstimationParams =  std::variant<BinningParams, GaussianKernelParams, CausalExponentialParams>;
Tagged union of all supported rate estimation method parameter structs.
Note: GaussianKernelParams and CausalExponentialParams are included in the variant but their implementations return empty RateEstimate (stub).
This is the single variation point for estimation method selection. Selecting a method at runtime is zero-overhead compared to a virtual base-class strategy — std::visit dispatches via a jump table.
To add a new method:

Define a new *Params struct above
Append it to this alias
Add the implementation in [EventRateEstimation.cpp](/api_generated/Files/EventRateEstimation_8cpp.md#file-eventrateestimation.cpp)

        std::function<std::optional<PlotTooltipHit>(QPoint screen_pos)>;
Callback that performs a hit test at a screen position.
Returns a PlotTooltipHit on success, or std::nullopt if nothing is under the cursor. This callback may perform spatial queries (QuadTree, etc.) and is only called after the dwell timer fires.

    std::shared_ptr< DataManager > const & data_manager,

)
Create UnitGatherContexts for a batch of DigitalEventSeries keys.
Parameters:

data_manager DataManager containing the event and alignment series
event_keys DataManager keys of the [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md) to gather
alignment_data Alignment configuration shared across all units

Return: Vector of successfully gathered [UnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1UnitGatherContext.md) objects
Applies [createUnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-createunitgathercontext) to each key in event_keys with the same alignment settings. Keys for which gathering fails are silently skipped; the returned vector may therefore be shorter than event_keys.
Order is preserved: the i-th element of the result corresponds to the i-th key that succeeded.



RateEstimate estimateRate(
    GatherResult< DigitalEventSeries > const & gathered,
    TimeFrame const * time_frame,
    double window_size,
    EstimationParams const & params =BinningParams{}
)
Estimate the rate for a single unit (aggregate across trials).
Parameters:

gathered Trial-aligned views of one [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md)
time_frame TimeFrame of the source series (may be null)
window_size Total window span in time units (bins cover ±window_size/2)
params Estimation method and parameters (default: [BinningParams](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1BinningParams.md){})

Return: [RateEstimate](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimate.md) with times, values, num_trials, and metadata
Returns a [RateEstimate](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimate.md) with paired times[] (bin centers for binning) and values[] (raw event counts summed across all trials).
Uses time_frame to convert each event’s [TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md) to an absolute time before computing the relative time with respect to the per-trial alignment time from gathered.
If time_frame is null, [TimeFrameIndex::getValue()](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md#function-getvalue) is used directly as the absolute time (identity mapping).



RateEstimateWithTrials estimateRateWithTrials(
    GatherResult< DigitalEventSeries > const & gathered,
    TimeFrame const * time_frame,
    double window_size,
    EstimationParams const & params =BinningParams{}
)
Estimate rate with per-trial breakdown for a single unit.
Parameters:

gathered Trial-aligned views of one [DigitalEventSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalEventSeries.md)
time_frame TimeFrame of the source series (may be null)
window_size Total window span in time units
params Estimation method and parameters (default: [BinningParams](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1BinningParams.md){})

Return: [RateEstimateWithTrials](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimateWithTrials.md) with aggregate + per-trial data
Same as [estimateRate()](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate) but additionally returns per-trial rate curves in [RateEstimateWithTrials::trials](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1RateEstimateWithTrials.md#variable-trials). The aggregate estimate is the trial-summed result (same as [estimateRate()](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate)), and each trial’s individual histogram is stored separately.
Use this when you need uncertainty quantification (SEM, CI, bootstrap) via the functions in [RateUncertainty.hpp](/api_generated/Files/RateUncertainty_8hpp.md#file-rateuncertainty.hpp).

)

Applies [estimateRate](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer_1_1Plots.md#function-estimaterate) independently to each [UnitGatherContext](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Plots_1_1UnitGatherContext.md) in units. All units share the same window_size and params. The output vector is in the same order as the input and has the same length.

CostFunction createDynamicsAwareCostFunction(
    Eigen::MatrixXd const & H,
    Eigen::MatrixXd const & R,
    KalmanMatrixBuilder::StateIndexMap const & index_map,
    double dt,
    double beta =1.0,
    double gamma =0.25,
    double lambda_gap =0.0
)
Factory function to create a dynamics-aware transition cost with velocity and implied-acceleration penalties.
c = 0.5 r^T S^{-1} r + 0.5 log det S

beta * 0.5 (v_impl - v_pred)^T Sigma_v^{-1} (v_impl - v_pred)
gamma * 0.5 ||a_impl||^2 (simple L2 penalty) where r = z_to - H x_pred, S = H P_pred H^T + R, v_impl = (z_pos - x_pred_pos) / (k * dt), and a_impl = 2 * (z_pos - x_pred_pos) / ((k * dt)^2).

inline std::vector< MetaNode > sliceMetaNodesToSegment(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes,
    GroundTruthSegment const & segment
)
Create a trimmed copy of meta-nodes restricted to a ground-truth segment.
Parameters:

meta_nodes All meta-nodes across the full range
segment Ground truth segment specifying [start_frame, end_frame] and entities

Return: Trimmed meta-nodes for the segment. Empty if anchors are not found.
Keeps only meta-nodes that lie strictly within (start_frame, end_frame) and the two boundary meta-nodes that contain the anchors. Boundary meta-nodes are spliced so that their start/end align exactly with the anchor frames. Any other meta-node that crosses a boundary without containing the corresponding anchor is discarded.



inline Path buildFallbackPathFromTrimmed(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes_trimmed,
    int start_meta_index,
    int end_meta_index
)
Build a simple fallback path by concatenating members of start and end meta-nodes.
Assumes the input meta-nodes are already trimmed to the segment using sliceMetaNodesToSegment. If start and end refer to the same meta-node, returns its members. Otherwise, concatenates all members from the start meta-node followed by all members from the end meta-node.



inline std::vector< MetaNode > resolveOverlappingAnchorNodes(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes_trimmed,
    int start_meta_index,
    int end_meta_index
)
If the start anchor node and end anchor node overlap in time, split them into non-overlapping prefix/suffix nodes and two explicit overlap nodes.
Input is expected to be the trimmed/pruned meta-nodes for the segment produced by sliceMetaNodesToSegment(). This function inspects the meta-node at start_meta_index and end_meta_index; if their ranges overlap, returns a new vector where these two nodes are replaced by up to four nodes:

start_prefix: [start.start_frame .. overlap_start-1]
start_overlap: [overlap_start .. overlap_end] (from start node)
end_overlap: [overlap_start .. overlap_end] (from end node)
end_suffix: [overlap_end+1 .. end.end_frame] Nodes with empty ranges are omitted. All other nodes are copied unchanged.

)
Factory function to create a Mahalanobis distance-based cost function.
Parameters:

H Measurement matrix (maps state space to measurement space)
R Measurement noise covariance matrix

Return: CostFunction that computes Mahalanobis distance
This is the default cost function that computes the Mahalanobis distance between the predicted measurement (H * predicted_state) and the actual observation.



CostFunction createDynamicsAwareCostFunction(
    Eigen::MatrixXd const & H,
    Eigen::MatrixXd const & R,
    KalmanMatrixBuilder::StateIndexMap const & index_map,
    double dt,
    double beta =1.0,
    double gamma =0.25,
    double lambda_gap =0.0
)
Factory function to create a dynamics-aware transition cost with velocity and implied-acceleration penalties.
c = 0.5 r^T S^{-1} r + 0.5 log det S

beta * 0.5 (v_impl - v_pred)^T Sigma_v^{-1} (v_impl - v_pred)
gamma * 0.5 ||a_impl||^2 (simple L2 penalty) where r = z_to - H x_pred, S = H P_pred H^T + R, v_impl = (z_pos - x_pred_pos) / (k * dt), and a_impl = 2 * (z_pos - x_pred_pos) / ((k * dt)^2).

inline std::vector< MetaNode > sliceMetaNodesToSegment(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes,
    GroundTruthSegment const & segment
)
Create a trimmed copy of meta-nodes restricted to a ground-truth segment.
Parameters:

meta_nodes All meta-nodes across the full range
segment Ground truth segment specifying [start_frame, end_frame] and entities

Return: Trimmed meta-nodes for the segment. Empty if anchors are not found.
Keeps only meta-nodes that lie strictly within (start_frame, end_frame) and the two boundary meta-nodes that contain the anchors. Boundary meta-nodes are spliced so that their start/end align exactly with the anchor frames. Any other meta-node that crosses a boundary without containing the corresponding anchor is discarded.



inline Path buildFallbackPathFromTrimmed(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes_trimmed,
    int start_meta_index,
    int end_meta_index
)
Build a simple fallback path by concatenating members of start and end meta-nodes.
Assumes the input meta-nodes are already trimmed to the segment using sliceMetaNodesToSegment. If start and end refer to the same meta-node, returns its members. Otherwise, concatenates all members from the start meta-node followed by all members from the end meta-node.



inline std::vector< MetaNode > resolveOverlappingAnchorNodes(
    std::vector< MetaNode > const & meta_nodes_trimmed,
    int start_meta_index,
    int end_meta_index
)
If the start anchor node and end anchor node overlap in time, split them into non-overlapping prefix/suffix nodes and two explicit overlap nodes.
Input is expected to be the trimmed/pruned meta-nodes for the segment produced by sliceMetaNodesToSegment(). This function inspects the meta-node at start_meta_index and end_meta_index; if their ranges overlap, returns a new vector where these two nodes are replaced by up to four nodes:

start_prefix: [start.start_frame .. overlap_start-1]
start_overlap: [overlap_start .. overlap_end] (from start node)
end_overlap: [overlap_start .. overlap_end] (from end node)
end_suffix: [overlap_end+1 .. end.end_frame] Nodes with empty ranges are omitted. All other nodes are copied unchanged.

    DataManager & dm,
    DigitalIntervalSeries const & intervals,
    std::string const & time_key_str
)
Expand a DigitalIntervalSeries into individual TimeEntity IDs.

dm DataManager with a valid EntityRegistry
intervals The interval series to expand
time_key_str The TimeFrame key string (clock identity)

Return: Vector of EntityIds, sorted ascending by time value
Note: The resulting vector may contain fewer elements than the sum of interval lengths if intervals overlap.
For each interval [start, end] in intervals, registers every integer index in [start, end] as a TimeEntity. Returns the full set of EntityIds across all intervals, sorted by TimeFrameIndex value.

Retrieves all TimeEntity members of group_id whose data_key matches time_key_str, sorts by TimeFrameIndex value, and merges adjacent frames (difference == 1) into contiguous intervals.
Non-TimeEntity members and TimeEntities from other clocks are silently skipped.

std::vector< EntityId > registerTimeEntities(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & time_key_str,
    std::span< TimeFrameIndex const > frames
)
Register a set of arbitrary TimeFrameIndex values as TimeEntities.
Parameters:

dm DataManager (must have a valid EntityRegistry)
time_key_str The TimeFrame key string (clock identity)
frames Span of TimeFrameIndex values to register

Return: Vector of EntityIds, one per input frame (same order)
Each frame in frames is registered (or retrieved if already present) via DataManager::ensureTimeEntityId(). The returned vector is parallel to frames — result[i] is the EntityId for frames[i].



std::vector< EntityId > intervalsToTimeEntities(
    DataManager & dm,
    DigitalIntervalSeries const & intervals,
    std::string const & time_key_str
)
Expand a DigitalIntervalSeries into individual TimeEntity IDs.
Parameters:

dm DataManager with a valid EntityRegistry
intervals The interval series to expand
time_key_str The TimeFrame key string (clock identity)

Return: Vector of EntityIds, sorted ascending by time value
Note: The resulting vector may contain fewer elements than the sum of interval lengths if intervals overlap.
For each interval [start, end] in intervals, registers every integer index in [start, end] as a TimeEntity. Returns the full set of EntityIds across all intervals, sorted by TimeFrameIndex value.
Duplicate registrations (overlapping intervals) are handled idempotently by the underlying EntityRegistry.



std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries > timeEntitiesToIntervals(
    DataManager & dm,
    GroupId group_id,
    std::string const & time_key_str
)
Convert a group of TimeEntity IDs into a DigitalIntervalSeries.
Parameters:

dm DataManager with valid EntityRegistry and EntityGroupManager
group_id The group to read entities from
time_key_str The TimeFrame key string to filter by

Return: Shared pointer to a DigitalIntervalSeries containing the merged intervals, or nullptr if the group is empty or has no matching TimeEntities
Retrieves all TimeEntity members of group_id whose data_key matches time_key_str, sorts by TimeFrameIndex value, and merges adjacent frames (difference == 1) into contiguous intervals.
Non-TimeEntity members and TimeEntities from other clocks are silently skipped.

    arma::mat & matrix,

)

Parameters:

matrix The matrix to normalize (modified in-place)
epsilon Added to std to prevent division by zero

Return: Pair of {means, stds} vectors (one per row/feature)
Normalizes each row (feature) of a features × observations matrix to zero mean and unit standard deviation.



void applyZscoreNormalization(
    arma::mat & matrix,
    std::vector< double > const & means,
    std::vector< double > const & stds,
    double epsilon =1e-10
)
Apply previously computed z-score parameters to new data.

matrix The matrix to normalize (features × observations, modified in-place)
means Per-feature means (size must == matrix.n_rows)
stds Per-feature standard deviations (size must == matrix.n_rows)

Useful for normalizing prediction-time data with the same parameters used during training.

    TensorData const & tensor,

)

tensor The feature tensor (must be 2D, non-empty)

Postcondition:

If config.drop_nan is true, result.matrix contains no NaN or Inf values
If config.zscore_normalize is true, each row (feature) of result.matrix has mean≈0 and std≈1, and result.zscore_means / result.zscore_stds are populated for re-application to new data via applyZscoreNormalization()
result.valid_row_indices maps each matrix column back to the original tensor row index

This is the primary conversion entry point. It:

Validates the tensor is non-empty and 2D
Materializes all columns (handles lazy backends transparently)
Converts float → double
Optionally drops rows containing NaN/Inf values
Optionally z-score normalizes each column
Transposes to mlpack layout (features × observations)

config Conversion parameters

Similar to convertTensorToArma but preserves the TensorData’s natural layout where rows are observations and columns are features. Useful when you need the matrix in the same orientation as the tensor (e.g., for visualization).

AssembledLabels assembleLabelsFromIntervals(
    DigitalIntervalSeries const & intervals,
    TimeFrame const & source_time_frame,
    std::span< TimeFrameIndex const > row_times,
    LabelFromIntervals const & config ={}
)
Assemble binary labels from a DigitalIntervalSeries.
Parameters:

intervals The interval series defining the positive class
source_time_frame The TimeFrame that row_times are expressed in. This is typically the feature tensor’s TimeFrame from RowDescriptor.
row_times The time indices of each feature tensor row
config Configuration with class names (defaults: “Outside”, “Inside”)

Exceptions:

std::invalid_argument if row_times is empty

Return: Binary labels aligned with row_times (unlabeled_count always 0)
Precondition: row_times must not be empty (enforcement: exception)
For each row_time, checks if it falls inside any interval in the series. Inside → label 1, outside → label 0. Every row receives a label.



AssembledLabels assembleLabelsFromTimeEntityGroups(
    EntityGroupManager const & groups,
    EntityRegistry const & registry,
    std::span< TimeFrameIndex const > row_times,
    LabelFromTimeEntityGroups const & config
)

Return: Multi-class labels aligned with row_times
Precondition:

config.class_groups must not be empty (enforcement: exception)
row_times must not be empty (enforcement: exception)

Retrieves entities from each group, looks up their EntityDescriptor in the registry, and builds a mapping from TimeFrameIndex value → class label. Only entities matching the configured time_key and EntityKind::TimeEntity are considered.
Rows whose time value is not found in any group receive a sentinel label equal to num_classes and are counted as unlabeled.

Precondition:

config.class_groups must not be empty (enforcement: exception)

Similar to assembleLabelsFromTimeEntityGroups but matches entities by data_key rather than time_key. Accepts entities of any EntityKind (LineEntity, PointEntity, EventEntity, etc.) as long as data_key matches.

    DataManager & dm,
    MLModelRegistry const & registry,

    PipelineProgressCallback const & progress =nullptr
)
Run the full supervised classification pipeline.
Parameters:

dm DataManager containing the feature tensor, label sources, and output targets
registry Model registry containing the model factory
config Full pipeline configuration
progress Optional callback for progress reporting

Return: Complete pipeline result with metrics, outputs, and trained model
Precondition: config.conversion_config.zscore_normalize should be true for scale-sensitive classifiers (Logistic Regression, Softmax Regression). Tree-based methods (Random Forest) are scale-invariant. This is the sole mechanism for feature scaling — individual algorithms no longer scale internally. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Orchestrates:

Validate — checks feature tensor exists and is valid
Convert — TensorData → arma::mat (NaN dropping, optional z-score)
Assemble labels — from intervals, time-entity groups, or data-entity groups
Balance — optional class balancing (subsample/oversample)
Segment — (sequence models only) split into contiguous temporal sequences
Train — trains the selected model
Predict — on training data or a separate prediction tensor
Metrics — computes classification metrics on predictions
Write output — writes predictions as intervals, probabilities, and/or groups

Validate — checks feature tensor exists and is valid

class
Neuralyzer::Plots::PlotTooltipManager Manages tooltip lifecycle for plot widgets.






Shared tooltip manager for plot widgets with dwell-timer hover detection.
PlotTooltipManager encapsulates the tooltip lifecycle common to all plot widgets: dwell-timer management, stationarity detection, hit testing delegation, and content display. Widgets provide two callbacks:

A hit test function that converts a screen position to a hit result (or signals a miss).
A content provider that turns a hit result into displayable content (plain text or a rendered QPixmap for glyph-style tooltips).

The manager owns the QTimer, handles mouse-move restarts, suppresses tooltips during panning, and hides the tooltip on widget leave. Costly hit tests and content generation only run after the dwell interval elapses, so rapid mouse movement never triggers expensive computation.

text:
std::vector< double > fit_polynomial(
    std::vector< double > const & x,
    std::vector< double > const & y,
    int order
)
Fit a polynomial of the specified order to the given data.
Parameters:

x X-coordinates of the data points
y Y-coordinates of the data points
order The polynomial order to fit

Return: std::vector Polynomial coefficients (empty if fitting failed)
Precondition:

x and y have the same size (enforcement: runtime_check)
order >= 0 (enforcement: runtime_check)
x.size() > order for a successful fit; otherwise returns empty (enforcement: runtime_check)




double evaluate_polynomial_derivative(
    std::vector< double > const & coeffs,
    double x
)
Evaluate polynomial derivative at a given point.
Parameters:

coeffs The polynomial coefficients (c0, c1, … for poly c0 + c1*x + …)
x The x value at which to evaluate the derivative

Return: double The evaluated derivative value
Precondition: For a non-constant-zero derivative, coeffs.size() >= 2 (enforcement: none)
Postcondition: If coeffs is empty or size 1, returns 0.0



double evaluate_polynomial(
    std::vector< double > const & coeffs,
    double x
)
Evaluate polynomial at a given point.
Parameters:

coeffs The polynomial coefficients (c0, c1, … for c0 + c1x + c2x^2 + …)
x The x value at which to evaluate the polynomial

Return: double The evaluated polynomial value
Precondition: For a non-constant-zero result, coeffs must not be empty (enforcement: none)
Postcondition: If coeffs is empty, returns 0.0



double evaluate_polynomial_second_derivative(
    std::vector< double > const & coeffs,
    double t
)
Evaluate polynomial second derivative at a given point.
Parameters:

coeffs The polynomial coefficients (c0, c1, … for poly c0 + c1*t + …)
t The parameter value at which to evaluate the second derivative

Return: double The evaluated second derivative value
Precondition: For a non-constant-zero second derivative, coeffs.size() >= 3 (enforcement: none)
Postcondition: If coeffs.size() < 3, returns 0.0



float calculate_polynomial_angle(
    Line2D const & line,
    float position,
    float window,
    int polynomial_order,
    PlanarOrthonormalBasis2D const & basis
)
Calculate angle using a polynomial fit on samples within a sliding arc-length window.
Parameters:

line The line to evaluate
position Fractional midpoint along full line (0.0 to 1.0)
window Full width of arc-length window (0.0 to 1.0), same semantics as direct secant
polynomial_order Order of polynomial to fit
basis Orthonormal basis for angle measurement

Return: Angle in degrees in (-180, 180]
Precondition: polynomial_order >= 0 (enforcement: returns 0.0f if negative)
Samples (u in [0,1]) are taken along [t_low, t_high] via point_at_fractional_position with interpolation. Fits x(u), y(u), then uses tangent (dx/du, dy/du) at u corresponding to position. Falls back to calculate_direct_angle_secant on the same window if fitting fails.



std::vector< Point2D< float > > extract_parametric_subsegment(
    Line2D const & line,
    float start_pos,
    float end_pos,
    int polynomial_order,
    int output_points
)
Extract a subsegment of a line using parametric polynomial interpolation.
Parameters:

line The line to extract from
start_pos Start of subsegment (0.0 to 1.0), clamped internally
end_pos End of subsegment (0.0 to 1.0), clamped internally
polynomial_order Order of polynomial to fit
output_points Number of points in the output subsegment

Return: Points along the subsegment, or empty if start_pos >= end_pos or line empty
Precondition:

polynomial_order >= 0 (enforcement: runtime_check; fallback if line too small)
output_points >= 2 for polynomial path; otherwise division by zero (enforcement: none)

Fits parametric polynomials x(t) and y(t) to the line over [0,1], then evaluates at evenly spaced t in [start_pos, end_pos]. Falls back to distance-based extraction if the line has too few points or fitting fails.

#ifndef MMAP_ANALOG_CONFIG_HPP
#define MMAP_ANALOG_CONFIG_HPP

#include <cstddef>
#include <filesystem>

enum class MmapDataType {
    Float32,// 32-bit floating point (no conversion needed)
    Float64,// 64-bit floating point (double)
    Int8,   // 8-bit signed integer
    UInt8,  // 8-bit unsigned integer
    Int16,  // 16-bit signed integer
    UInt16, // 16-bit unsigned integer
    Int32,  // 32-bit signed integer
    UInt32  // 32-bit unsigned integer
};

struct MmapStorageConfig {
    std::filesystem::path file_path;               
    std::size_t header_size = 0;                   
    std::size_t offset = 0;                        
    std::size_t stride = 1;                        
    std::size_t num_samples = 0;                   
    MmapDataType data_type = MmapDataType::Float32;
    float scale_factor = 1.0f;                     
    float offset_value = 0.0f;                     
};

#endif// MMAP_ANALOG_CONFIG_HPP

Utilities for mask raster conversion, resize, and binary image processing.
Par:

Mask raster vs continuous geometry

This header operates on discrete mask rasters ([Mask2D](/api_generated/Classes/classMask2D.md) sparse pixel lists). It does not perform continuous point/line scaling; see DeepLearning channel encoders/decoders for float geometry. * Spatial convention (resize functions)
[map_dest_to_source](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-map-dest-to-source) and [resize_mask](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-resize-mask) use the pixel-center grid (align_corners=false), consistent with:

PyTorch ImageEncoder / interpolate(..., align_corners=false)
OpenCV cv2.resize sampling geometry
TensorToMask2D mask decode (DeepLearning)

Non-resize functions


[mask_to_binary_image](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-mask-to-binary-image) and [binary_image_to_mask](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-binary-image-to-mask) place or read pixels on an integer grid without resampling — no spatial convention applies beyond canvas bounds.
Integer pixel indices are treated as pixel centers at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) in continuous image space. Inverse nearest-neighbor mapping per axis:
src = clamp(lround((dest + 0.5) * source_size / dest_size - 0.5), 0, source_size - 1)
see docs/developer/DataObjects/Masks/utils/mask_utils.qmd for the pixel-center vs edge-aligned comparison table.





std::shared_ptr< MaskData > apply_binary_image_algorithm(
    MaskData const * mask_data,
    std::function< Image(Image const &)> const & binary_processor,
    std::function< void(int)> const & progress_callback =[](int) {},
    bool preserve_empty_masks =false
)
Applies a binary image processing function to mask data.
Parameters:

mask_data The input mask data to process.
binary_processor Function that takes a binary image and returns a processed binary image.
progress_callback Function for progress reporting (0–100).
preserve_empty_masks If true, empty masks are preserved in the output.

title: src/DataObjects/Masks/utils/mask_utils.hpp
text:
Utilities for mask raster conversion, resize, and binary image processing.
Par:

Mask raster vs continuous geometry

This header operates on discrete mask rasters ([Mask2D](/api_generated/Classes/classMask2D.md) sparse pixel lists). It does not perform continuous point/line scaling; see DeepLearning channel encoders/decoders for float geometry. * Spatial convention (resize functions)
[map_dest_to_source](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-map-dest-to-source) and [resize_mask](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-resize-mask) use the pixel-center grid (align_corners=false), consistent with:

PyTorch ImageEncoder / interpolate(..., align_corners=false)
OpenCV cv2.resize sampling geometry
TensorToMask2D mask decode (DeepLearning)

Non-resize functions


[mask_to_binary_image](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-mask-to-binary-image) and [binary_image_to_mask](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#function-binary-image-to-mask) place or read pixels on an integer grid without resampling — no spatial convention applies beyond canvas bounds.
Integer pixel indices are treated as pixel centers at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) in continuous image space. Inverse nearest-neighbor mapping per axis:
src = clamp(lround((dest + 0.5) * source_size / dest_size - 0.5), 0, source_size - 1)
see docs/developer/DataObjects/Masks/utils/mask_utils.qmd for the pixel-center vs edge-aligned comparison table.

Provides free functions to serialize trial-aligned event data from GatherResult into long-form tidy CSV strings.

trial_index,event_key,relative_time
0,spikes,-245.3

The metadata comment header (lines starting with #) records alignment parameters for reproducibility. Both Python (pd.read_csv(comment=‘#’)) and R (read_csv(comment=‘#’)) handle this natively.

std::shared_ptr< LineData > calculate_mask_principal_axis(
    MaskData const * mask_data,

)
Calculate the principal axis of masks at each timestamp.
Parameters:

mask_data The mask data to calculate principal axes from
params The principal axis calculation parameters

Return: A new LineData containing principal axis lines at each timestamp
For each timestamp in the mask data, calculates the principal axis (major or minor) of all mask points using eigenvalue decomposition of the covariance matrix. The resulting line passes through the centroid and extends to touch the bounding box. If multiple masks exist at the same timestamp, each mask gets its own principal axis line.

)

dataManager The DataManager to load data into

This function handles the case where JSON content is provided as a string (e.g., from a text editor) and file paths should be resolved relative to a specified base folder.

title: src/TransformsV2/utils/MultichannelTemplateRealigner.hpp
text:
High-performance modular engine for spatio-temporal template calculation and iterative waveform realignment.
Implements Expectation-Maximization (EM) template realignment matching SpikeSorter:

M-Step: Compute multichannel spatio-temporal cluster mean template T(c, τ)
E-Step: Slide each event within [-W_search, +W_search] to maximize template goodness-of-fit / cross-correlation
Iterate until shifts converge to 0.

title: src/DeepLearning/post_encoder/PostEncoderModule.hpp
text:
Abstract interface for post-encoder feature processing modules.
See:

ChannelDecoder.hpp for the final torch-to-DataManager decoding stage
PostEncoderModuleRegistry.hpp for module registration and lookup
PostEncoderPipeline.hpp for chaining multiple modules

Post-encoder modules are the tensor-to-tensor stage of the inference pipeline. They transform a backbone encoder’s spatial feature map (at::Tensor, typically [B, C, H, W]) into a more compact tensor representation still in the torch domain — for example a global descriptor [B, C] from GlobalAvgPoolModule or a point-sampled vector from SpatialPointExtractModule.
Typical pipeline position:
encoder output [B, C, H, W]
     → PostEncoderModule::apply()              // torch → torch
     → TensorToFeatureVector::decode() / …     // torch → DataManager type
     → DataManager::setData / addAtTime
Post-encoder modules are optional. When omitted, channel decoders operate directly on the raw encoder output (required for spatial decoders such as TensorToMask2D). Modules chain via PostEncoderPipeline and are instantiated through PostEncoderModuleRegistry.

text:
Design mode panel for building TensorData with lazy columns.
TensorDesigner provides an interactive column-building experience for constructing TensorData backed by LazyColumnTensorStorage. Users select a row source (intervals, events, timeframe) and add columns by configuring DataManager source keys with TransformsV2 range reductions or element transforms.

title: src/WhiskerToolbox/DataInspector_Widget/TensorData/TensorDesigner.hpp
text:
Architecture

Row configuration: Select a DigitalIntervalSeries (interval rows), DigitalEventSeries (timestamp rows), or ordinal rows
Column building: Each column is a ColumnRecipe that maps to a ColumnProviderFn closure via TensorColumnBuilders
Live preview: Columns are lazily materialized in the TensorDataView
JSON serialization: Column configurations save/load as JSON
CSV export: Export the designed tensor to CSV

TensorColumnBuilders for the builder layer
LazyColumnTensorStorage for the storage backend
TensorInspector for the inspector that hosts this panel

text:
Design
TableDesignerWidget is a pure properties widget for creating and configuring table views. It provides tools for:

Creating new tables with row selectors (intervals, events)
Adding columns with various computers (Mean, Max, etc.)
Managing computer states (enabled/disabled, custom names)
Exporting and transforming table data

Key characteristics:

Single instance only (allow_multiple = false)
Placed in Zone::Right (properties zone)
No separate view - this IS the view
No properties panel (create_properties = nullptr)

EditorRegistry for the type registration API
TableDesignerState for the shared state class
TableDesignerWidget for the widget implementation

title: src/CoreMath/non_finite_rows.cpp
text:
bool rowHasNonFinite(
    std::span< float const > values
)
Check whether any value in a contiguous row slice is non-finite.
Parameters:

values Row values to scan

Return: true if at least one element is NaN or Inf



bool hasNonFiniteRows(
    arma::fmat const & fmat
)
Check whether any row of a float matrix contains NaN or Inf.
Parameters:

fmat Matrix to check (any layout)

Return: true if at least one element is NaN or Inf
Scans in row-major order with early exit on the first non-finite element.



NonFiniteRowFilterResult filterNonFiniteRows(
    arma::mat const & obs_matrix
)
Remove rows containing NaN or Inf from an observations × features matrix.
Parameters:

obs_matrix Matrix in observations × features layout (double precision)

Return: NonFiniteRowFilterResult with clean matrix, valid indices, and drop count
Precondition: obs_matrix must not be empty
Postcondition:

result.clean_matrix has no NaN or Inf values
result.valid_row_indices.size() == result.clean_matrix.n_rows
result.rows_dropped == obs_matrix.n_rows - result.clean_matrix.n_rows

Returns the cleaned matrix together with the surviving row indices. If all rows are finite, returns the original matrix and a full index vector without copying.



bool rowHasNonFiniteAcrossColumns(
    std::vector< std::vector< float > > const & columns,
    std::size_t row
)
Check whether a row in column-major materialized storage contains NaN or Inf.
Parameters:

columns Materialized tensor columns (each column vector has one value per row)
row Row index to check

Return: true if any column value at row is non-finite
Precondition: row < columns.front().size() when columns is non-empty

std::shared_ptr< LineData > lineOutlierDetection(
    std::shared_ptr< LineData > line_data,
    LineOutlierDetectionParameters const * params
)
Detect outliers in grouped lines using Kalman filtering.
Parameters:

line_data The LineData to process
params Parameters including thresholds and Kalman settings

Return: The same LineData shared_ptr (operation is performed in-place on groups)
This function processes existing groups in the LineData, using Kalman filtering and smoothing to establish expected trajectories. Entities that deviate significantly from their group’s predicted behavior are identified as outliers and moved to a dedicated outlier group.
The algorithm:

For each group with entities in the LineData
Extract features (centroid + length) for each entity in the group
Perform forward Kalman filtering
Perform backward smoothing using Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother
Calculate Mahalanobis distance between smoothed prediction and actual measurement
Identify outliers using MAD (Median Absolute Deviation) criterion
Add outliers to a new “Outliers” group

This file provides type definitions for value projections - transforms that compute scalar values from source elements without creating intermediate element types.

title: src/TransformsV2/extension/ValueProjectionTypes.hpp
text:
Value Projection vs Element Transform
Traditional element transforms produce new element types:
EventWithId → NormalizedEvent  // New type required
Value projections produce scalars while preserving source identity:
EventWithId → float            // Just the normalized time
    └── .id() accessible from source element

title: src/TransformsV2/extension/ValueProjectionTypes.hpp
text:
Motivation
For trial-aligned analysis (raster plots, PSTH), we often need to:

Normalize event times relative to trial alignment
Draw or reduce the normalized values
Preserve access to EntityId for coloring/grouping

Creating intermediate types like NormalizedEvent causes:

Type explosion in ElementVariant
Unnecessary data duplication (EntityId copied to output)
Complex type management in pipelines

Value projections solve this by:

Computing only the derived value (e.g., normalized time)
Leaving identity info in the source element
Enabling zero-copy lazy iteration

title: src/TransformsV2/extension/ValueProjectionTypes.hpp
src/TransformsV2/extension/ValueProjectionTypes.hpp
text:
Relationship to Other Types

ViewAdaptorFn: span<In> → vector<Out> (batch, materializing)
ValueProjectionFn: In → Value (single element, computed)
ReducerFn: span<In> → Scalar (batch, terminal)

Value projections are element-level and can be used inside a reduction:
span<EventWithId> → [project each] → span<float> → [reduce] → Scalar

bindValueProjectionV2()
GatherResult.hpp for trial-aligned analysis

RangeReductionRegistry.hpp for the registry infrastructure

End-to-end supervised dimensionality reduction pipeline.
Combines feature conversion (from DimReductionPipeline) with label assembly (from ClassificationPipeline) to train a supervised projection and produce a reduced TensorData output.
The pipeline trains on labeled observations only, then transforms ALL valid rows (labeled + unlabeled) so the output tensor covers the complete dataset. This enables scatter visualization with labeled and unlabeled points side-by-side.

ScatterSourceRowType resolveSourceRowType(
    DataManager & dm,
    ScatterAxisSource const & source
)
Resolve the scatter source row type for a single axis source.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to resolve the key against
source Axis source descriptor

Return: The resolved row type
Looks up source.data_key in dm. If the key is an AnalogTimeSeries, returns [ScatterSourceRowType::AnalogTimeSeries](/api_generated/Files/SourceCompatibility_8hpp.md#enumvalue-analogtimeseries). If the key is a TensorData, returns the row type from its RowDescriptor. Otherwise returns [ScatterSourceRowType::Unknown](/api_generated/Files/SourceCompatibility_8hpp.md#enumvalue-unknown).



SourceCompatibilityResult checkSourceCompatibility(
    DataManager & dm,
    ScatterAxisSource const & x_source,
    ScatterAxisSource const & y_source
)
Check whether two scatter axis sources are row-type compatible.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to resolve keys against
x_source X-axis data source descriptor
y_source Y-axis data source descriptor

Return: A SourceCompatibilityResult with compatibility flag and diagnostic
This function resolves the row type of each source and checks the compatibility matrix documented above. For TensorData Ordinal × Ordinal pairings, compatibility additionally requires that the two tensors have the same row count.

title: src/MLCore/models/supervised/LogisticRegressionOperation.hpp
text:
MLCore-native Logistic Regression classifier (wraps mlpack::LogisticRegression).
Features:

Conforms to the evolved MLModelOperation interface (MLTaskType, numFeatures, etc.)
Naturally provides probability estimates via LogisticRegression::Classify()
Supports save/load for model persistence via binary serialization
Tracks training metadata (numClasses, numFeatures) for validation
Uses pimpl to isolate mlpack headers from consumers
Uses the MLCore::LogisticRegressionParameters (lambda, max_iterations)

Note: mlpack’s LogisticRegression is inherently a binary classifier (2 classes). For multi-class logistic regression, mlpack provides SoftmaxRegression, which could be added as a separate operation in the future.

text:
# Transformation System V2 Architecture

## Overview

This document describes the V2 transformation architecture for WhiskerToolbox. The system provides a unified, composable approach to data transformations with compile-time type safety and runtime configurability.

## Implementation Status

### ✅ Complete
- **ElementRegistry**: Compile-time typed transform registry with TypedParamExecutor
- **TransformPipeline**: Multi-step pipeline with execution fusion and view-based lazy evaluation
- **Container Transforms**: Automatic lifting (element→container) and native container-to-container transforms
- **ContainerElementMapping / TypeIndexMapper** (`DataManager/utils`): Type mapping (Mask2D ↔ MaskData, etc.)
- **Advanced Features**: Ragged outputs, multi-input transforms (binary via tuple), time-grouped transforms
- **reflect-cpp Integration**: Parameter serialization with automatic validation
- **JSON Pipeline Loading**: PipelineDescriptor, PipelineLoader with full validation
- **PipelineValueStore**: Generic key-value store for computed values with parameter bindings
- **Pre-Reductions**: Statistical computations (Mean, StdDev, Min, Max) that populate value store
- **GatherResult Integration**: Trial-aligned analysis with `buildTrialStore()` and value projections
- **RangeReductions**: Library of reductions for trial-level analysis (EventCount, FirstPositiveLatency, etc.)
- **Provenance Tracking**: `LineageRegistry`, `EntityResolver`, `LineageRecorder`
- **DataManager Integration**: `DataManagerPipelineExecutor` and `load_data_from_json_config_v2()`

### 🔄 Planned
- **UI Integration**: Pipeline Builder Widget
- **Parallel Execution**: Multi-threaded transform execution

## Core Architecture

### Type Traits Layer

Fundamental type properties are defined at `src/DataManager/TypeTraits/`. Each container type defines its own `DataTraits` nested struct:

```cpp
class MaskData : public RaggedTimeSeries<Mask2D> {
public:
    struct DataTraits : WhiskerToolbox::TypeTraits::DataTypeTraitsBase<MaskData, Mask2D> {
        static constexpr bool is_ragged = true;
        static constexpr bool is_temporal = true;
        static constexpr bool has_entity_ids = true;
    };
};

// Usage:
static_assert(is_ragged_v<MaskData>);
using ElementType = element_type_t<MaskData>;  // Mask2D


Pure functions operating on single data elements:
float calculateMaskArea(Mask2D const& mask, MaskAreaParams const& params);
Properties: stateless, type-safe, composable, testable in isolation.



Automatic Lifting: Element transforms automatically work on containers:
registry.registerTransform<Mask2D, float, MaskAreaParams>("CalculateMaskArea", calculateMaskArea);

// Automatically available at container level:
auto areas = registry.executeContainer<MaskData, AnalogTimeSeries>("CalculateMaskArea", masks, params);
Native Container Transforms: For operations requiring full context (temporal dependencies, global stats):
registry.registerContainerTransform<AnalogTimeSeries, DigitalEventSeries, ThresholdParams>(
    "AnalogEventThreshold", analogEventThreshold);



Fused Execution (Eager): Single pass, materializes final result immediately.
TransformPipeline<MaskData, AnalogTimeSeries> pipeline;
pipeline.addStep<SkeletonParams>("Skeletonize", p1);
pipeline.addStep<MaskAreaParams>("CalculateArea", p2);
auto areas = pipeline.execute(masks);  // Single pass, no intermediate allocations
View-Based Execution (Lazy): Zero intermediate allocations, pull-based.
auto view = pipeline.executeAsView(masks);
auto filtered = view | std::views::filter([](auto p) { return p.second > 10.0f; });
Dynamic Output: Runtime-determined output type via DataTypeVariant.
TransformPipeline<MaskData> pipeline;
DataTypeVariant result = pipeline.execute(masks);



For transforms requiring global statistics (e.g., Z-Score normalization), use pre-reductions to compute values and bind them to parameters:
{
  "name": "ZScoreNormalization",
  "pre_reductions": [
    {"reduction": "MeanValue", "output_key": "computed_mean"},
    {"reduction": "StdValue", "output_key": "computed_std"}
  ],
  "steps": [{
    "transform": "ZScoreNormalizeV2",
    "params": {"clamp_outliers": true},
    "param_bindings": {"mean": "computed_mean", "std_dev": "computed_std"}
  }]
}
The PipelineValueStore holds computed values, and bindings inject them into transform parameters.



For trial-level analysis, range reductions collapse entire ranges to scalars:

For trial-aligned analysis, GatherResult provides:
// Build value store for a trial
PipelineValueStore store = gather.buildTrialStore(trial_idx);
// Contains: "alignment_time", "trial_index", "trial_duration", "end_time"

// Project values across trials (V2 store-based binding)
auto factory = bindValueProjectionV2<EventWithId, float>(pipeline);
auto projections = gather.project(factory);

// Reduce and sort trials (supply ReducerFactoryV2, often wrapping executeErased)
auto latencies = gather.reduce(reducer_factory);
auto sorted_indices = gather.sortIndicesBy(reducer_factory, /*ascending=*/true);
auto reordered = gather.reorder(sorted_indices);



Track EntityID relationships through transforms:
auto resolver = data_manager.getEntityResolver();
auto source_entities = resolver.resolveToRoot("mask_areas", time_index);




v2/
├── algorithms/              # Concrete transform implementations
│   ├── MaskArea/           # Mask2D → float
│   ├── SumReduction/       # Time-grouped reduction
│   ├── LineMinPointDist/   # Binary transform (Line2D, Point2D) → float
│   ├── ZScoreNormalization/# Z-score with pre-reductions
│   ├── Temporal/           # Time normalization transforms
│   └── RangeReductions/    # Event and value range reductions
│
├── core/                   # Public API
│   ├── ElementTransform.hpp
│   ├── ElementRegistry.hpp
│   ├── TransformPipeline.hpp
│   ├── PipelineValueStore.hpp
│   ├── PipelineLoader.hpp
│   ├── DataManagerIntegration.hpp
│   └── RangeReductionRegistry.hpp
│
├── extension/              # Transform developer utilities
│   ├── ParameterBinding.hpp
│   └── ValueProjectionTypes.hpp
│
└── detail/                 # Pipeline execution internals
    ├── PipelineStep.hpp
    └── ReductionStep.hpp





Ranges (compile-time dispatch) provide: - Zero overhead when type is known - Compiler can fuse multiple transforms - Cache-friendly execution (element processed through full pipeline) - Type erasure only at boundaries for runtime configuration



Materialize: User saves to DataManager, transform requires multiple passes, data needed by multiple consumers.
Keep Lazy: Intermediate pipeline steps, single-pass consumption, memory constraints, interactive visualization.





Parameter cast: Once per pipeline (not per element)
Type dispatch: Once per pipeline (not per element)
Per-element overhead: ~2 virtual calls + 2 variant visits (input/output only)
Fusion: Multiple transforms execute in single pass (no intermediate containers)
View Mode: Pull-based execution, zero intermediate allocations





UI Integration: Pipeline Builder widget, auto-generated parameter forms
Transform Migration: Port more V1 transforms to V2
Parallel Execution: Thread pool for expensive transforms

MLCore::LARSProjectionOperation LARS-based supervised feature selection.






LARS-based supervised feature selection (LASSO / Ridge / Elastic Net).
Uses mlpack’s LARS (Least Angle Regression Stagewise) algorithm to train penalized regression models against class labels, then identifies which input features have non-zero coefficients (the “active set”). The output is the subset of input features that survived regularization.
Binary (C=2): fits a single LARS model (response = class indicator). Multi-class (C>=3): fits one-vs-all LARS models and takes the union of active feature sets across all models.
The regularization mode can be set to LASSO (L1 only), Ridge (L2 only), or Elastic Net (L1 + L2).

title: src/MLCore/models/supervised/LARSProjectionOperation.hpp
text:
Motivation
LASSO regression produces sparse coefficient vectors — features whose coefficients are shrunk to zero are not predictive and are removed. This provides an interpretable, supervised dimensionality reduction where the output features are a subset of the originals (not a linear combination), making downstream analysis easier to interpret.

title: src/MLCore/models/supervised/LARSProjectionOperation.hpp
text:
Output Convention
Output is (A × N), where A = number of active (non-zero) features. Each row corresponds to one selected input feature, preserving its original values. Column names indicate which original feature index was selected (e.g. “LARS_sel:3”, “LARS_sel:7”).

text:
Strong type wrappers for EditorState identifiers.
See:

EditorState for widget state management
OperationContext for inter-widget operations

This file provides strongly-typed wrappers around QString to prevent accidental mixing of different identifier types. Using these types instead of raw QString provides:

Compile-time safety: Can’t pass a DataKey where EditorInstanceId is expected
Self-documenting code: Function signatures clearly state what they need
Better IDE support: Autocomplete and error messages are more helpful
Refactoring safety: Type changes are caught by the compiler

title: src/DeepLearning/channel_encoding/EncoderFactory.hpp
text:
Factory for channel encoders that map DataManager geometry and images into model input tensors.
See:

DecoderFactory
EncoderDispatch

Par: Spatial scaling contract
Every encoder registered here must resize or reproject between source_image_size (original media / mask canvas) and the tensor spatial dimensions in EncoderContext::height / EncoderContext::width using the same convention as the paired channel decoders in DecoderFactory.

Target convention: pixel-center grid (align_corners=false), matching PyTorch ImageEncoder resize and OpenCV cv2.resize sampling geometry.
Continuous geometry (points, lines): map pixel centers with t = (x + 0.5) * T / I - 0.5 (and the inverse when decoding).
Discrete masks: nearest-index raster ops on that grid (not independent per-point round(x * scale) formulas).

Do not introduce ad-hoc scaling in individual encoders. Shared helpers will live under [src/DeepLearning/spatial/SpatialResize.hpp](/api_generated/Files/SpatialResize_8hpp.md#file-spatialresize.hpp) (see developer docs).

text:
ProgressCallback throttleProgressCallbackToWholePercents(
    ProgressCallback inner
)
Wraps a progress callback so the inner callback runs at most once per integer percent (0–100).
Parameters:

inner Destination callback; if empty, returns an empty function.

Return: Wrapper that forwards only when the clamped percent value changes; duplicate 100 values are collapsed to a single delivery.
Repeated calls with the same clamped percent are ignored. Useful at pipeline/UI boundaries where transforms may report progress very frequently.

Factory function for building scatter point data from two axis sources.

ScatterPointData for the result structure
ScatterAxisSource for the source descriptor

Given two ScatterAxisSource descriptors and a DataManager, this function computes the paired (x, y, TimeFrameIndex) triples by joining on the shared row type (TimeFrameIndex or ordinal position).





ScatterPointData buildScatterPoints(
    DataManager & dm,
    ScatterAxisSource const & x_source,
    ScatterAxisSource const & y_source
)
Build scatter point data from two axis sources.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to read data from
x_source X-axis data source descriptor
y_source Y-axis data source descriptor

Return: ScatterPointData with matched (x, y, time_index) triples
Precondition: sources must be compatible (check with checkSourceCompatibility() first) (enforcement: runtime_check)
For AnalogTimeSeries x AnalogTimeSeries: iterates over the intersection of valid TimeFrameIndex values, applying temporal offset by shifting the index.
For AnalogTimeSeries x TensorData (TimeFrameIndex rows): joins on shared TimeFrameIndex values.
For TensorData (Ordinal) x TensorData (Ordinal): uses positional pairing (row i from each tensor). TimeFrameIndex is set to the row index.

text:
Utility for extracting time indices from any DataManager data type.
See: tensor_column_refactor_proposal.md §4.4 Option A
This decouples UI code (e.g. TensorDesigner) from needing per-type includes and dispatch logic. The visitor lives in DataManager — which already depends on every data type — so callers only need this header.

title: src/DataManager/utils/TimeIndexExtractor.hpp
text:
TimeIndexResult extractTimeIndices(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & key
)
Extract time indices from any data type stored under key.
Parameters:

dm The DataManager to query (non-const because getData() is non-const).

Converts a rows × bins grid of scalar values into a colored rectangle batch.
Provides a generic grid-to-rectangle-batch mapper suitable for any widget that renders a 2D scalar field as colored cells:

HeatmapWidget: each row is a unit’s firing rate profile over time bins
SpectrogramWidget: each row is a frequency bin’s power over time bins

The mapper is agnostic to the data source — it works with HeatmapRowData, a lightweight struct describing one row of scalar values with X-axis metadata. The calling widget is responsible for converting its domain-specific data (e.g., RateProfile from EventRateEstimation) into HeatmapRowData.

Export heatmap data to CSV format.
Provides free functions to serialize heatmap data into CSV strings. Two export modes are supported:
Aggregate — wide matrix, one row per unit:
unit_key,-500.0,-490.0,-480.0,...
unit_A,0.4,1.2,3.7,...
unit_B,0.0,0.3,0.5,...
Per-trial — long-form tidy, one row per (unit, trial, bin):
unit_key,trial_index,bin_center,value
unit_A,0,-500.0,0.0
unit_A,0,-490.0,1.0
unit_A,1,-500.0,0.0
unit_B,0,-500.0,0.0
The metadata comment header (lines starting with #) records alignment parameters for reproducibility. Both Python (pd.read_csv(comment=‘#’)) and R (read_csv(comment=‘#’)) handle this natively.

title: src/IO/formats/CSV/tensors/Tensor_Data_CSV.hpp
text:
CSV loading and saving for TensorData objects.
Supports 2D tensors with three row types: TimeFrameIndex, Interval, and Ordinal. The CSV format uses a header row with column names and one data row per tensor row.
Row label column format:

TimeFrameIndex: integer time index
Interval: “start-end” (e.g. “100-200”)
Ordinal: row index integer

title: src/IO/formats/CSV/tensors/Tensor_Data_CSV.hpp

    CSVTensorLoaderOptions const & options
)
Load a TensorData from a CSV file.
Parameters:

options Loader options including filepath and delimiter

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error on file or parse errors

Return: Shared pointer to the loaded TensorData



DATAMANAGERIO_EXPORT bool save(
    TensorData const * tensor,
    CSVTensorSaverOptions const & opts
)
Save a TensorData to a CSV file.
Parameters:

tensor Pointer to the TensorData to save (non-owning, caller retains ownership)
opts Saver options including filename, parent_dir, delimiter

Return: true on success
Precondition:

tensor must not be null
tensor must be at least 2D

title: src/WhiskerToolbox/DataInspector_Widget/LineData/LineTableView.hpp
text:
Table view widget for LineData.
See:

BaseDataView for the base class

title: src/DeepLearning/channel_decoding/DecoderFactory.hpp
text:
Factory for channel decoders that map model output tensors back into DataManager geometry types.
See:

EncoderFactory
DecoderDispatch

Par: Spatial scaling contract
Every decoder registered here must upsample or reproject from tensor spatial dimensions (DecoderContext::height / DecoderContext::width) to DecoderContext::target_image_size using the same convention as the paired encoders in EncoderFactory.

Target convention: pixel-center grid (align_corners=false), matching PyTorch ImageEncoder resize and OpenCV cv2.resize sampling geometry.
Continuous geometry (points, lines): inverse of the encoder center mapping.
Discrete masks: inverse nearest-neighbor raster expansion (see [resize_mask](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8cpp.md#function-resize-mask) in [mask_utils.hpp](/api_generated/Files/mask__utils_8hpp.md#file-mask-utils.hpp)), not independent per-point scaling.

Encode and decode must be paired inverses per data category (continuous float vs discrete mask raster). Do not introduce ad-hoc scaling in individual decoders.

std::shared_ptr< LineData > lineIndexGrouping(
    std::shared_ptr< LineData > line_data,
    LineIndexGroupingParameters const * params
)
Group lines by their vector index at each timestamp.
Parameters:

line_data The LineData to process
params Parameters including group naming options

Return: The same LineData shared_ptr (operation is performed in-place on groups)
This function analyzes all timestamps in the LineData to find the maximum number of lines at any single timestamp. It then creates that many groups and assigns lines based on their position in the vector at each timestamp.
For example, if timestamps have [3, 5, 4, 2] lines respectively, it will create 5 groups (0-4). Lines at index 0 across all timestamps go to group 0, lines at index 1 go to group 1, etc.
