std::shared_ptr< LineData > lineKalmanGrouping(
    std::shared_ptr< LineData > line_data,
    LineKalmanGroupingParameters const * params
)
Group lines using Kalman filtering and assignment.
Parameters:

line_data The LineData to process
params Parameters including thresholds and Kalman settings

Return: The same LineData shared_ptr (operation is performed in-place on groups)
This function processes all time frames, using existing grouped lines as anchor points and tracking multiple line features (centroid + base point + length) with Kalman filters. Ungrouped lines are assigned to groups using the Hungarian algorithm with Mahalanobis distance.
The tracker operates directly on Line2D objects with on-demand feature extraction, avoiding unnecessary memory overhead. Features are computed only when needed for prediction, update, or assignment operations.
The system uses a metadata-driven approach to handle features with different temporal behaviors: kinematic features (with velocity) and static features (time-invariant) are combined seamlessly in the same tracking system.

title: src/DeepLearning/channel_decoding/ChannelDecoder.hpp
text:
Base interface for channel decoders and per-decoder parameter structs.
See:

PostEncoderModule.hpp for optional tensor-to-tensor post-processing applied before decoding
DecoderFactory.hpp for decoder registration and lookup

Channel decoders are the tensor-to-DataManager stage of the inference pipeline. They read a selected slice of a model output at::Tensor and produce a concrete geometry or tabular type that can be stored in the DataManager — for example [Mask2D](/api_generated/Classes/classMask2D.md), [Point2D](/api_generated/Classes/structPoint2D.md)<float>, [Line2D](/api_generated/Classes/classLine2D.md), or std::vector<float>.
Typical pipeline position:
encoder output [B, C, H, W]
     → (optional) PostEncoderModule::apply()   // torch → torch
     → TensorToMask2D::decode() / …            // torch → DataManager type
     → DataManager::setData / addAtTime
Concrete decoders (TensorToMask2D, TensorToPoint2D, TensorToLine2D, TensorToFeatureVector) implement static decode() methods and register via DecoderFactory. DecoderContext carries indexing and coordinate-scaling state populated by [SlotAssembler](/api_generated/Classes/classSlotAssembler.md); per-decoder params structs hold user settings.

text:
Design Philosophy
The registration function encapsulates:

Factory functions for state, view, and properties
Type metadata (display name, menu path, default zone)
Complex widget creation logic

This keeps MainWindow decoupled from widget implementation details.

title: src/TransformsV2/algorithms/IntervalReduction/IntervalReduction.hpp
text:
Binary container transforms that produce TensorData from interval + source pairs.
See:

GatherResult for the underlying gather pattern
RangeReductionRegistry for available reductions
TensorData::createFromIntervals for output construction

These transforms take a DigitalIntervalSeries (defining rows) and a source data container, gather the source data within each interval, apply a named range reduction, and produce a TensorData with interval-based RowDescriptor and a single column.
Three variants are provided for different source types:

AnalogIntervalReduction: (DigitalIntervalSeries, AnalogTimeSeries) → TensorData
EventIntervalReduction: (DigitalIntervalSeries, DigitalEventSeries) → TensorData
IntervalOverlapReduction: (DigitalIntervalSeries, DigitalIntervalSeries) → TensorData

Example JSON pipeline usage:
{
  "step_id": "reduce_analog",
  "transform_name": "AnalogIntervalReduction",
  "input_key": "trial_intervals",
  "additional_input_keys": ["firing_rate"],
  "output_key": "trial_mean_rate",
  "parameters": {
    "reduction_name": "MeanValue",
    "column_name": "mean_firing_rate"
  }
}

title: src/DataManager/transforms/utils/index_grouping.hpp
text:
template <typename DataMap ,
typename Entry >
inline std::size_t groupByIndex(
    DataMap const & data_map,
    EntityGroupManager * group_manager,
    std::string const & group_name_prefix,
    std::string const & group_description_template ="Group {} - elements at vector index {}"
)
Templated function to group data by vector index.
Parameters:

data_map Reference to the data map containing vectors of entries
group_manager The EntityGroupManager to add groups to
group_name_prefix Prefix for created group names (e.g., “Whisker”, “Point”)
group_description_template Template for group descriptions (can include {} for index)

Template Parameters:

DataMap The type of the data map (e.g., std::map<TimeFrameIndex, std::vector>)
Entry The entry type (e.g., LineEntry, PointEntry, MaskEntry)

Return: Number of groups created
This function operates on time-series data structures that store vectors of entries (e.g., LineEntry, PointEntry, MaskEntry) at each timestamp. It creates groups based on the position of elements within the vectors.
The algorithm:

Finds the maximum number of elements at any single timestamp
Creates that many groups (group 0, group 1, …, group N-1)
Assigns all elements at vector index 0 to group 0, index 1 to group 1, etc.

This is useful for:

Organizing tracked features by their detection order
Maintaining consistent identity across frames when detection order is stable
Grouping whiskers, body parts, or other tracked entities by their index

title: src/MLCore/models/supervised/SupervisedPCAOperation.hpp
text:
Supervised PCA fits PCA on labeled subset, projects all data.
Standard PCA finds components that maximize variance across the entire dataset. Supervised PCA fits only on the subset of observations that carry a label, so the principal components capture the variance structure of the labeled data. All observations (labeled + unlabeled) are then projected into that space.
This is useful when the labeled data represents a specific phenomenon of interest (e.g., whisker contact), and the user wants the top components to reflect variance within that phenomenon rather than variance across the full recording.
Inherits from MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation so it integrates with the SupervisedDimReductionPipeline and scatter-plot visualization.

Panel for configuring and running ML predictions.
PredictionPanel provides the prediction configuration UI for the Classification tab in MLCoreWidget. It contains:

Prediction region selector — combo box listing DigitalIntervalSeries keys in the DataManager, with an “All remaining frames” checkbox to predict on every frame not used for training.
Output prefix — text field for naming generated output data keys (e.g. “ml” → “Predicted:ml_class0”, “ml_prob_class0”).
Threshold slider/spin box — decision threshold for binary classification probability (0.01–0.99, default 0.50). The slider and spin box are bidirectionally synchronized.
Output type checkboxes:

Output predictions as DigitalIntervalSeries (class intervals)
Output probabilities as AnalogTimeSeries (per-class probabilities)

Predict button — emits predictRequested() for the parent widget to wire up to the ClassificationPipeline.

DigitalEventSeries generator that produces events via a homogeneous Poisson process.

VerticalAxisWithRangeControls createVerticalAxisWithRangeControls(
    VerticalAxisState * state,
    QWidget * axis_parent =nullptr,
    QWidget * controls_parent =nullptr
)
Factory function to create a complete vertical axis with range controls.
Parameters:

state VerticalAxisState object (must outlive the returned widgets)
axis_parent Parent widget for the axis widget (typically the plot widget)
controls_parent Parent widget for the range controls (typically properties widget)

Return: Factory result with all widgets linked to the state
This factory creates:

A VerticalAxisWidget for display
A VerticalAxisRangeControls widget for editing

All components are linked to the provided VerticalAxisState and handle anti-recursion to prevent update loops.
The factory automatically sets up the axis widget to read from the state and connect to range changes for repainting.

text:
Observer pattern implementation for data change notifications.
Note: This library is NOT thread-safe. All observer operations (add, remove, notify) must be performed from the same thread, or external synchronization must be provided by the caller.
This file provides the core observer pattern infrastructure used throughout Neuralyzer for propagating data changes to dependent components.

Functions Documentation

function resolveSourceRowType
ScatterSourceRowType resolveSourceRowType(
    DataManager & dm,
    ScatterAxisSource const & source
)
Resolve the scatter source row type for a single axis source.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to resolve the key against
source Axis source descriptor

Return: The resolved row type
Looks up source.data_key in dm. If the key is an AnalogTimeSeries, returns [ScatterSourceRowType::AnalogTimeSeries](/api_generated/Files/SourceCompatibility_8hpp.md#enumvalue-analogtimeseries). If the key is a TensorData, returns the row type from its RowDescriptor. Otherwise returns [ScatterSourceRowType::Unknown](/api_generated/Files/SourceCompatibility_8hpp.md#enumvalue-unknown).


function checkSourceCompatibility
SourceCompatibilityResult checkSourceCompatibility(
    DataManager & dm,
    ScatterAxisSource const & x_source,
    ScatterAxisSource const & y_source
)
Check whether two scatter axis sources are row-type compatible.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to resolve keys against
x_source X-axis data source descriptor
y_source Y-axis data source descriptor

Return: A SourceCompatibilityResult with compatibility flag and diagnostic
This function resolves the row type of each source and checks the compatibility matrix documented above. For TensorData Ordinal × Ordinal pairings, compatibility additionally requires that the two tensors have the same row count.

text:
std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries > interval_threshold(
    AnalogTimeSeries const * analog_time_series,
    IntervalThresholdParams const & thresholdParams
)
Detects intervals in an AnalogTimeSeries based on a threshold.
Parameters:

analog_time_series The AnalogTimeSeries to process. Must not be null.
thresholdParams Parameters containing threshold value, direction, lockout time, minimum duration, and missing data handling mode.

Return: A new DigitalIntervalSeries containing detected intervals. Returns an empty series if input is null or empty.
This function analyzes an analog time series and identifies continuous intervals where the signal meets specified threshold criteria. It supports positive, negative, and absolute value thresholding with configurable lockout time and minimum duration requirements.
Missing data handling: When time indices are not consecutive (indicating missing samples), the behavior depends on the missingDataMode parameter:

TREAT_AS_ZERO (default): Missing time points are treated as having zero values
IGNORE: Missing time points are skipped (original behavior)




std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries > interval_threshold(
    AnalogTimeSeries const * analog_time_series,
    IntervalThresholdParams const & thresholdParams,
    ProgressCallback progressCallback
)
Detects intervals in an AnalogTimeSeries based on a threshold with progress reporting.
Parameters:

analog_time_series The AnalogTimeSeries to process. Must not be null.
thresholdParams Parameters containing threshold value, direction, lockout time, minimum duration, and missing data handling mode.
progressCallback Function called with progress percentage (0-100) during computation.

Return: A new DigitalIntervalSeries containing detected intervals. Returns an empty series if input is null or empty.
This function analyzes an analog time series and identifies continuous intervals where the signal meets specified threshold criteria. It supports positive, negative, and absolute value thresholding with configurable lockout time and minimum duration requirements. Progress is reported through the provided callback.
Missing data handling: When time indices are not consecutive (indicating missing samples), the behavior depends on the missingDataMode parameter:

TREAT_AS_ZERO (default): Missing time points are treated as having zero values
IGNORE: Missing time points are skipped (original behavior)

title: src/IO/formats/CSV/mask/Mask_Data_CSV.hpp
text:
CSV loader/saver for MaskData using Run-Length Encoding (RLE).
Provides options structs and free functions for loading and saving MaskData in a CSV format where mask pixels are encoded as RLE triplets (y, x_start, length).
CSV format: Frame,“y,x_start,length,y,x_start,length,…”
Each row contains a frame number followed by a quoted string of RLE triplets. Each triplet (y, x_start, length) represents a horizontal run of pixels at row y, starting at column x_start, with the given length.

DATAMANAGERIO_EXPORT std::string encode_mask_rle(

)
Encode a Mask2D into RLE triplets string.
Parameters:

mask The mask to encode
rle_delimiter Delimiter between values in the RLE string

Return: RLE-encoded string
Converts a mask into a string of (y, x_start, length) triplets where each triplet represents a contiguous horizontal run of pixels at a given y row. Points are sorted by (y, x) before encoding.



DATAMANAGERIO_EXPORT Mask2D decode_mask_rle(
    std::string const & rle_str,

)
Decode an RLE triplets string into a Mask2D.
Parameters:

rle_str The RLE-encoded string
rle_delimiter Delimiter between values in the RLE string

Return: Decoded Mask2D
Parses a string of (y, x_start, length) triplets and expands each run into individual mask pixels.



DATAMANAGERIO_EXPORT std::map< TimeFrameIndex, std::vector< Mask2D > > load(
    CSVMaskRLELoaderOptions const & opts
)
Load MaskData from a single CSV file with RLE encoding.

opts Options controlling the load behavior

DATAMANAGERIO_EXPORT bool save(
    MaskData const * mask_data,

)
Save MaskData to a single CSV file with RLE encoding.
Parameters:

mask_data Non-null pointer to the MaskData to save.
opts Saver options (directory, filename, delimiters, header).

Return: true on success, false on I/O error.
Precondition: mask_data must not be null.
Uses atomic writes: data is written to a temporary file and then renamed over the target to prevent corruption on crash.

text:
Analog time series generator that produces a triangle wave.
Registers a “TriangleWave” generator in the DataSynthesizer registry. Produces: y[t] = amplitude * (2/π) * arcsin(sin(2π * (num_cycles/cycle_length) * t + phase)) + dc_offset phase is in radians. This formulation maintains the same phase semantics as SineWave: at t=0 with phase=0, the output is 0 and rising.

title: src/MLCore/features/FeatureConverter.hpp
text:
Converts TensorData feature matrices to arma::mat for mlpack consumption.
MLPack algorithms operate on double-precision arma::mat in column-major layout with observations as columns (features × observations). This converter handles:

Materialization of lazy columns (via TensorData::getColumn)
Float → double precision conversion
NaN/Inf row removal
Optional z-score normalization
Transposition to mlpack’s expected layout (features × observations)

Also provides convertTensorToArmaRowMajor() for row-major output and applyZscoreNormalization() for applying pre-computed normalization parameters.
The resulting ConvertedFeatures struct tracks which rows survived NaN dropping so that predictions can be mapped back to the original time frames.

text:
Analog time series generator that produces a square wave.
Registers a “SquareWave” generator in the DataSynthesizer registry. Produces: y[t] = +amplitude if fractional position within cycle < duty_cycle, -amplitude otherwise, plus dc_offset. Fractional position = fmod((num_cycles/cycle_length) * t + phase/(2π), 1.0). phase is in radians.

template <typename Derived ,
typename TData >
class RaggedStorageBase;
CRTP base class for ragged storage implementations.
Template Parameters:

Derived The concrete storage implementation type
TData The data type stored (e.g., Mask2D, Line2D, Point2D)

Uses Curiously Recurring Template Pattern to eliminate virtual function overhead while maintaining a polymorphic interface. Derived classes implement the actual storage strategy (owning SoA or view/filter).
The SoA (Structure of Arrays) layout stores parallel vectors:

TimeFrameIndex times[]
TData data[]
EntityId entity_ids[]

This provides:

O(1) EntityId lookup via hash map
Cache-friendly sequential iteration
Efficient view creation without data copying

Get total number of entries across all times.

) const
Get the TimeFrameIndex at a flat index.

) const
Find flat index by EntityId.

id The EntityId to find

Return: Flat index if found, std::nullopt otherwise
Note: O(1) for OwningRaggedStorage, O(1) for ViewRaggedStorage

    TimeFrameIndex time
) const
Get range of flat indices for a specific time.
Parameters:

time The TimeFrameIndex to query

Return: Pair of (start_idx, end_idx) where end is exclusive, or (0,0) if not found

Get number of distinct times with data.

Get the storage type identifier.

Check if this is a view (doesn’t own data).



inline RaggedStorageCache< TData > tryGetCache() const
Try to get cached pointers for fast-path access.
Return: RaggedStorageCache with valid pointers if contiguous, invalid otherwise
Returns a cache structure with direct pointers to contiguous data. If the storage is non-contiguous (e.g., ViewRaggedStorage), returns an invalid cache and callers must use the virtual dispatch path.

class MLCore::DBSCANOperation;
DBSCAN clustering wrapping mlpack::DBSCAN.
Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise. Discovers clusters of arbitrary shape based on local density. Points in low-density regions are labeled as noise (SIZE_MAX).
Unlike K-Means, DBSCAN does not require specifying the number of clusters in advance — the algorithm discovers them from the data. However, it also does not produce a fitted model that can directly predict on new data.
After fitting, this implementation stores the cluster centroids and the epsilon radius. New data can be assigned to clusters via nearest-centroid lookup, with points farther than epsilon from all centroids marked as noise.

class StateEstimation::IFilter;
Abstract interface for a state estimation filter.
This class defines the contract for all filter implementations, such as KalmanFilter, ExtendedKalmanFilter (EKF), or UnscentedKalmanFilter (UKF). It operates on generic feature vectors, keeping it decoupled from specific data types (like Lines or Points).

title: Neuralyzer::Entity::Lineage::EntityMappedLineage

struct Neuralyzer::Entity::Lineage::EntityMappedLineage;
Explicit entity-to-entity mapping for entity-bearing derived containers.
When both source and derived containers have their own EntityIds, this maps from derived EntityId to parent EntityId(s).
Example: LineData from MaskData via skeletonization

LineEntityId=200 came from Mask EntityId=100
LineEntityId=201 came from Mask EntityId=100 (1:N case)

For 1:1: each derived EntityId maps to exactly one parent For N:1: one derived EntityId maps to multiple parents For 1:N: multiple derived EntityIds map to the same parent

class dl::ModelExecution;
Multi-backend model execution layer.
[ModelExecution](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelExecution.md) dispatches inference to one of several backends (TorchScript, AOT Inductor, ExecuTorch) via the [InferenceBackend](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1InferenceBackend.md) strategy pattern. The backend is selected either explicitly via [BackendType](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespacedl.md#enum-backendtype) or auto-detected from the model file extension:

.pt → TorchScript (legacy, deprecated but functional)
.pt2 → AOT Inductor (recommended for new models)
.pte → ExecuTorch (optional, requires ENABLE_EXECUTORCH)

The public API is identical to the previous ExecuTorch-only implementation, so downstream code ([NeuroSAMModel](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1NeuroSAMModel.md), [RuntimeModel](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1RuntimeModel.md), [SlotAssembler](/api_generated/Classes/classSlotAssembler.md)) requires no changes.
Usage:
// Auto-detect from extension:
dl::ModelExecution exec;
exec.load("/path/to/model.pt2");     // → AOTInductorBackend

// Explicit backend:
dl::ModelExecution exec2(dl::BackendType::TorchScript);
exec2.load("/path/to/model.pt");     // → TorchScriptBackend

if (exec.isLoaded()) {
    auto outputs = exec.execute({input_tensor_1, input_tensor_2});
}

class dl::RuntimeModel;
A ModelBase implementation driven entirely by a RuntimeModelSpec (JSON).
RuntimeModel allows users to define model inputs, outputs, and metadata via a JSON specification file, without recompiling. It uses ModelExecution to load and run ExecuTorch .pte programs.
Usage:
auto spec_result = RuntimeModelSpec::fromJsonFile("model.json");
if (spec_result) {
    auto model = std::make_unique<RuntimeModel>(std::move(spec_result.value()));
    model->loadWeights("/path/to/model.pte");
    // ... use like any ModelBase ...
}

preferred_zone: Where the view widget goes (typically Center)
properties_zone: Where the properties widget goes (typically Right)
properties_as_tab: Whether to add as tab (true) or replace content
auto_raise_properties: Whether to bring properties to front on creation

title: EditorCreationController
text:
Ownership

The controller does NOT own the created widgets
Dock widgets are managed by the ADS dock manager
EditorState is registered with EditorRegistry
Callers can connect to dock widget signals for lifecycle events

Interface for type-erased container execution.
This interface allows executing container transforms without knowing the concrete input/output/parameter types at the call site. The types are captured at registration time.
This mirrors IParamExecutor for element transforms, enabling container transforms to be first-class citizens in the pipeline system.

class KeymapSystem::KeymapManager;
Central manager for keyboard shortcut registration, resolution, and dispatch.
Responsibilities:

Action registry: stores all KeyActionDescriptors
Override management: merges defaults with user customizations
Conflict detection: reports same key bound to multiple actions in the same scope
Scope resolution: resolves key presses using priority order (EditorFocused > AlwaysRouted > Global)
Adapter routing: dispatches actions to registered KeyActionAdapters

When installed as a QApplication event filter, it intercepts key events and dispatches them through the scope resolution pipeline. When focus is in a text-input widget (QLineEdit, QTextEdit, etc.), keybindings are not dispatched so normal typing is not interrupted.

class Media_Window;
The Media_Window class is responsible for plotting images, movies, and shapes on top of them. Shapes may take the form of lines, points, or arbitrary 2d masks. Advancing a frame will result in the video window loading new data.
This is a QGraphicsScene, which internally renders lines, paths, points, and shapes which are added to the scene
Shapes can be added to the specific frame being visualized after it has been rendered and saved or just temporarily (scrolled back it will not be there), or data assets can be loaded which are saved for the duration (loading keypoints to be plotted with each corresponding frame).

title: Media_Window
text:
class Media_Window;
The Media_Window class is responsible for plotting images, movies, and shapes on top of them. Shapes may take the form of lines, points, or arbitrary 2d masks. Advancing a frame will result in the video window loading new data.
This is a QGraphicsScene, which internally renders lines, paths, points, and shapes which are added to the scene
Shapes can be added to the specific frame being visualized after it has been rendered and saved or just temporarily (scrolled back it will not be there), or data assets can be loaded which are saved for the duration (loading keypoints to be plotted with each corresponding frame).

Uses [AppFileDialog](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceAppFileDialog.md) for session-aware path memory (dialog id "export_event_plot_svg"). Shows an informational message box on success and an error message box on failure. Does nothing if the scene is empty or the user cancels the dialog.



void handleExportCSV()
Open a file dialog and write raster event data to a CSV file.
Uses [AppFileDialog](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceAppFileDialog.md) for session-aware path memory (dialog id "export_event_plot_csv"). Re-gathers trial-aligned data and calls [PlotDataExport::exportRasterToCSV()](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespacePlotDataExport.md#function-exportrastertocsv).

OpenGL widget for rendering line plots with batch line selection.
Displays AnalogTimeSeries data aligned to trial intervals. Each trial is shown as a line plot with values rendered at their relative time positions.
Features:

Independent X (time) and Y (value) zooming
Panning with mouse drag
Wheel zoom (Shift+wheel for Y-only)
Line selection via Ctrl+Click drag (intersects trials)
Selection result emitted as trial indices

struct CSVMultiFileLineLoaderOptions;
Options for loading 2D LineData from multiple CSV files, one per timestamp.
Note: This struct uses parent_dir instead of filepath since it loads from a directory.
Each CSV file should contain X values in one column and Y values in another column. The filename (without extension) is parsed as the timestamp/frame number. Files are expected to be in the format: NNNNNN.csv (zero-padded frame numbers).
Uses reflect-cpp for automatic JSON serialization/deserialization. Optional fields can be omitted from JSON and will use default values.

class CorePlotting::Interaction::IGlyphInteractionController;
Abstract interface for interactive glyph creation and modification controllers.
See:

GlyphPreview for the preview geometry format
RenderableScene::previewToDataCoords() for coordinate conversion

This interface defines the contract for controllers that handle user interactions for creating or modifying visual elements (rectangles, lines, points, polygons).
Coordinate System: All coordinates are in canvas pixels (screen space). The widget is responsible for passing canvas coordinates from mouse events, and the Scene handles conversion to world/data coordinates via inverse transforms.
Lifecycle:

Widget creates appropriate controller based on interaction mode
[start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-start) called on mouse press with canvas coordinates
[update()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-update) called on mouse move to update preview
[complete()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-complete) called on mouse release to finalize
Widget retrieves preview via [getPreview()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-getpreview) and converts to data coordinates
Controller can be reused or destroyed

Modification vs Creation:

Creating new: [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-start) with existing_entity_id = std::nullopt
Modifying existing: [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-start) with the EntityId of the element being modified (e.g., interval edge drag). The controller may need additional info passed via a subclass-specific method (see RectangleInteractionController::startEdgeDrag).

Modifying existing: [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1IGlyphInteractionController.md#function-start) with the EntityId of the element being modified (e.g., interval edge drag). The controller may need additional info passed via a subclass-specific method (see RectangleInteractionController::startEdgeDrag).

class BinaryDatasetPreviewModel;
Lazy-loading table model for raw binary file preview.
This model presents binary file data in a table format based on user configuration (data type, channels, header offset, byte order).
When bitwise expansion is enabled, each element is expanded into individual bit columns, useful for interpreting digital event data from multi-channel acquisition devices.
Data is loaded in chunks (default 100 rows) and cached using QCache to provide smooth scrolling while minimizing memory usage.

class MLCore::LogitProjectionOperation;
Supervised linear projection via softmax logit extraction.
Given labeled feature data (D × N) and integer class labels, trains a softmax regression model and extracts the weight matrix W (C × D) and bias b (C). The logit projection for new data X is:
result = W * X + b_broadcast (C × N)

    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params,
    arma::mat & result
) override
Train softmax regression and project labeled data to logit space.
Parameters:

features (D × N) feature matrix in mlpack convention
labels (N,) label row with class indices in [0, C)
params LogitProjectionParameters or nullptr for defaults
result (C × N) output logit matrix

Return: true on success
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
labels.n_elem == features.n_cols (enforcement: runtime_check)
labels must contain at least 2 distinct classes (enforcement: runtime_check)
params is nullptr or points to a valid MLModelParametersBase (enforcement: runtime_check)
all values in features are finite — no NaN or Inf (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

isTrained() returns true on success
result.n_rows == numClasses(), result.n_cols == features.n_cols on success

class dl::TensorToLine2D;
Decodes a tensor channel into a Line2D by thresholding, skeletonization, and ordering.
Strategy:

Threshold the channel to produce a binary mask
Skeletonize (thin to 1-pixel width) using Zhang-Suen thinning
Order skeleton pixels into a connected polyline by tracing connectivity

Output coordinates are scaled from tensor (H, W) back to target_image_size. If target_image_size is {0, 0}, coordinates are returned in tensor space.
Expects a 4D input tensor laid out as [B, C, H, W].





virtual std::string name() const override
Reimplements: dl::ChannelDecoder::name



virtual std::string outputTypeName() const override
Reimplements: dl::ChannelDecoder::outputTypeName



static Line2D decode(
    at::Tensor const & tensor,
    DecoderContext const & ctx,
    LineDecoderParams const & params
)
Decode a tensor channel to an ordered polyline.
Parameters:

tensor 4D activation tensor [B, C, H, W].
ctx Decoder indexing context; height and width must match tensor dims 2 and 3.
params User threshold for line extraction.

Precondition:

tensor is defined
tensor.dim() == 4 (layout [B, C, H, W])
0 <= ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0)
0 <= ctx.source_channel < tensor.size(1)
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0
tensor.size(2) == ctx.height and tensor.size(3) == ctx.width

Postcondition: Returned line is empty when no pixels exceed params.threshold.

struct CSVTensorLoaderOptions;
Options for loading TensorData from CSV.
The CSV file is expected to have:

A header row with column names (first column is the row label)
One data row per tensor row, with the row label in the first column

Row types are auto-detected from the first data row:

If the first cell contains a ‘-’ character, it is parsed as an interval
If it is a plain integer, it is parsed as a TimeFrameIndex
Otherwise it is treated as ordinal

class CorePlotting::RowLayoutStrategy;
Horizontal row layout strategy (Raster plot style).
Arranges series in horizontal rows, typically for raster plots where each row represents a trial or condition. All rows have equal height and are stacked top-to-bottom.
LAYOUT RULES:

Each series gets one row
All rows have equal height (viewport divided equally)
Rows are ordered top-to-bottom by series index
No concept of “stackable” vs “full-canvas” — all series are rows

COORDINATE SYSTEM:

Y coordinates are in viewport space (typically -1 to +1 NDC)
Row heights are in viewport units
Row centers are positioned to create even vertical spacing

USE CASES:

Raster plots (events across trials)
Multi-trial time series
Condition-based grouping

class ImageProcessing::OpenCVImageProcessor;
OpenCV-based image processor implementation.
This class provides the OpenCV backend for the image processing chain. It maintains the current MediaData processing functionality while implementing the generic ImageProcessor interface.
The internal format is cv::Mat, allowing the processing chain to work directly with OpenCV functions without conversions between steps.
Uses variant approach to handle both 8-bit (CV_8U) and 32-bit float (CV_32F) processing.

title: SelectionContext
SelectionContext
text:
Key Concepts

Data Focus (Phase 1 Refactoring - Passive Awareness)
“Data Focus” represents what data the user is currently working with, separate from which widget has keyboard focus. When data focus changes, all “passively aware” widgets update their content accordingly.


Widget Focus
Which editor/widget has keyboard focus. This affects keyboard shortcuts but does NOT automatically change property panels.


Data Selection (Legacy)
One or more data objects (by key) can be selected. There is always a “primary” selection which is the most recently selected item.


Entity Selection
Within the currently selected data, specific entities can be selected. This is useful for line/mask/point data where each element has an EntityID.


Properties Context (Deprecated - Phase 6 removal)
Legacy mechanism for determining which properties panel to show. Being replaced by passive awareness pattern.

Memory-mapped file analog data storage using CRTP.
Provides efficient access to large binary files without loading entire dataset into memory. Supports:

Strided access (e.g., reading one channel from interleaved multi-channel data)
Type conversion from various integer/float formats to float32
Scale and offset transformations
Cross-platform memory mapping (POSIX mmap and Windows MapViewOfFile)

class MemoryMappedAnalogDataStorage;
Memory-mapped file analog data storage using CRTP.
Provides efficient access to large binary files without loading entire dataset into memory. Supports:

Strided access (e.g., reading one channel from interleaved multi-channel data)
Type conversion from various integer/float formats to float32
Scale and offset transformations
Cross-platform memory mapping (POSIX mmap and Windows MapViewOfFile)

RenderableScene::previewToDataCoords() for the conversion

Coordinate Spaces:

GlyphPreview: Canvas coordinates (pixels)
DataCoordinates: Data-space coordinates (time indices, data values)

Usage: After an interaction completes, the widget:

Gets the GlyphPreview from the controller
Calls scene.previewToDataCoords() to convert to data space
Uses this struct to update the DataManager

Decodes a tensor channel into a Mask2D by thresholding.
All pixels with activation above params.threshold are collected as mask pixels. Output pixel coordinates are scaled from tensor (H, W) back to target_image_size. If target_image_size is {0, 0}, coordinates are returned in tensor space.

Decode a tensor channel to a mask by thresholding.
Parameters:

tensor 4D activation tensor [B, C, H, W].
ctx Decoder indexing context; height and width must match tensor dims 2 and 3.
params User threshold for mask generation.

Precondition:

tensor is defined
tensor.dim() == 4 (layout [B, C, H, W])
0 <= ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0)
0 <= ctx.source_channel < tensor.size(1)
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0
tensor.size(2) == ctx.height and tensor.size(3) == ctx.width

Postcondition: Returned mask contains only pixels with activation > params.threshold.

struct MLCore::ICAParameters;
Parameters for ICA (RADICAL algorithm) dimensionality reduction.
Note:

ICA does not reduce dimensionality: the output has the same number of dimensions as the input. The components are ordered by the algorithm’s internal sweep order, not by variance.
RADICAL scales quadratically in the number of dimensions.

Wraps mlpack::Radical hyperparameters. RADICAL performs Independent Component Analysis — it finds a linear transformation (unmixing matrix) that maximizes statistical independence of the output components.





double noise_std_dev = 0.175;
Standard deviation of Gaussian noise added to data.



std::size_t replicates = 30;
Number of Gaussian-perturbed replicates per point.



std::size_t angles = 150;
Number of angles in brute-force search during 2D RADICAL.



std::size_t sweeps = 0;
Number of sweeps (0 = number of dimensions minus one).



std::size_t m = 0;
Vasicek’s m-spacing estimator parameter (0 = sqrt(dimensions)).

struct AnalogDataStorageCache;
Cache structure for fast-path access to contiguous analog storage.
Analog samples are stored as contiguous float values when possible. This cache exposes a raw pointer and size for zero-overhead iteration when the underlying storage is contiguous. For non-contiguous backends (lazy views, strided mmap), the cache is marked invalid and callers must fall back to virtual dispatch.

class dl::TensorToFeatureVector;
Decodes a [B, C] (or [C]) feature tensor into a flat std::vector<float>.
Intended for use after a post-encoder module (e.g. [GlobalAvgPoolModule](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1GlobalAvgPoolModule.md)) has reduced a spatial feature map to a global descriptor. Extracts the feature vector for a single batch element.
Supported input shapes:

[C] — single unbatched vector; returns all C values.
[B, C] — batched; returns the vector at ctx.batch_index.

class PlottingOpenGL::PolyLineRenderer;
Renders RenderablePolyLineBatch data using OpenGL 3.3+ compatible calls.
See: CorePlotting::RenderablePolyLineBatch
This renderer is designed for the DataViewer use case: relatively few polylines (analog time series) that may have many vertices each.
Rendering Strategy:

Uses GL_LINE_STRIP for each polyline segment
Supports per-line colors (if provided) or a global batch color
Model matrix from the batch is combined with provided View/Projection

Shader Loading:

By default, uses ShaderManager with shaders from WhiskerToolbox/shaders/
Can fall back to embedded shaders if shader files are not available
Shader program name: “polyline_renderer”

For high-performance scenarios with 100,000+ short lines (e.g., raster plots), consider using a ComputePolyLineRenderer with SSBOs instead.
Vertex Format:

Position: vec2 (x, y) in world space
Color: vec4 (r, g, b, a) - either from uniform or vertex attribute

class StateEstimation::LineLengthExtractor;
Feature extractor that computes line length.
This extractor computes the total arc length of a line by summing the Euclidean distances between consecutive points. Line length is typically time-invariant or slowly varying, so it’s treated as a STATIC feature with no velocity tracking.
Features returned:

Filter features: [length] (1D scalar)
Initial state: [length] (1D, no velocity component)

class MLCore::NaiveBayesOperation;
Naive Bayes classifier wrapping mlpack::NaiveBayesClassifier.
Supervised binary/multi-class classification using Gaussian Naive Bayes. Assumes features are conditionally independent given the class label, with each feature modeled as a Gaussian distribution per class.

function train
virtual bool train(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params
) override
Train the model on labeled data.
Parameters:

features Feature matrix (features × observations). Each column is one observation with features.n_rows feature values.
labels Label row vector (1 × observations). Each element is a class index in [0, num_classes).
params Algorithm-specific parameters. May be nullptr to use defaults. Must be castable to the concrete parameter type expected by this model.

Return: true if training succeeded
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
labels.n_elem must equal features.n_cols (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features are expected to be z-score normalized for scale-sensitive classifiers (Logistic Regression, Softmax Regression). Tree-based methods (Random Forest) are scale-invariant. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Reimplements: MLCore::MLModelOperation::train
After successful training, [isTrained()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1NaiveBayesOperation.md#function-istrained) returns true, and [numClasses()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1NaiveBayesOperation.md#function-numclasses) and [numFeatures()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1NaiveBayesOperation.md#function-numfeatures) reflect the training data dimensions.
The default implementation returns false (unsupervised models).

) override

Parameters:

features Feature matrix (features × observations)
predictions [out] Predicted label row vector (1 × observations)

Return: true if prediction succeeded
Precondition:

isTrained() must be true (enforcement: runtime_check)
features.n_rows must equal numFeatures() (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features must be z-score normalized using the SAME parameters (mean/std) that were used for the training data passed to train(). Use FeatureConverter::applyZscoreNormalization() with stored parameters. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

class LineBaseFlipTransform;
Transform that flips the base of lines based on distance to a reference point.
This transform allows users to manually place a reference point in the media viewer. For each line, it compares the distance from both endpoints to the reference point. If the current base (first point) is farther from the reference than the end point, the line is flipped so that the closer endpoint becomes the new base.

class TableView;
The main orchestrator for tabular data views with lazy evaluation.
TableView manages a collection of heterogeneous columns and provides unified access to tabular data. It implements lazy evaluation with caching for both individual columns and ExecutionPlans. The TableView handles dependency resolution and ensures columns are computed in the correct order.

struct ImageMaskSaverOptions;
Options for saving 2D MaskData to binary image files.
This saver creates a directory containing binary (black and white) image files where each file represents a mask for a specific frame. The filename will contain the frame number, optionally with a prefix.





std::string parent_dir = ".";
The directory where binary image files will be saved.



std::string image_format = "PNG";
Image format to save (e.g., “PNG”, “BMP”, “TIFF”).



std::string filename_prefix = "";
Optional prefix before the frame number in filenames (e.g., “mask_” for “mask_0001.png”).



int frame_number_padding = 4;
Number of digits for zero-padding frame numbers (e.g., 4 for “0001”).



int image_width = 640;
Width of the output images in pixels.



int image_height = 480;
Height of the output images in pixels.



int background_value = 0;
Pixel value for background (non-mask) pixels (0-255).

Pixel value for mask pixels (0-255).



bool overwrite_existing = false;
If true, overwrite existing files. If false, skip existing files and continue with next file.

title: MLCore::MLDimReductionOperation
text:
Fit/Transform workflow
op->fitTransform(features, params, result);  // fit + transform in one call
op->transform(new_features, result);          // project new data (if supported)
auto ratio = op->explainedVarianceRatio();    // inspect explained variance
All matrices use mlpack convention: (features × observations) — each column is one observation.
Unlike clustering operations, dimensionality reduction produces a transformed matrix rather than cluster labels. The output matrix has n_components rows and the same number of columns as the input.

text:

function fitTransform
virtual bool fitTransform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params,
    arma::mat & result
) =0
Fit the model to data and transform in a single call.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (features × observations) in mlpack convention
params Algorithm-specific parameters
result Output: reduced matrix (n_components × observations)

Return: true on success
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params must be of the correct concrete type for this operation (enforcement: none)
Features are expected to be z-score normalized (mean≈0, std≈1 per feature) when scale-sensitive comparison across features is desired. Normalization is the caller’s responsibility (via FeatureConverter). Centering is handled internally by each algorithm. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

isTrained() returns true on success
result has n_components rows and features.n_cols columns

Reimplemented by: MLCore::ICAOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::PCAOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::RobustPCAOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::TSNEOperation::fitTransform


function transform
virtual bool transform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::mat & result
) =0
Project new data using the fitted model.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (features × observations)
result Output: reduced matrix (n_components × observations)

Return: true on success, false if not fitted or projection unsupported
Precondition:

isTrained() must be true (enforcement: runtime_check)
features.n_rows must equal numFeatures() (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features must be z-score normalized using the SAME parameters (mean/std) that were used for the training data passed to fitTransform(). Use FeatureConverter::applyZscoreNormalization() with stored parameters. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

class CorePlotting::StackedLayoutStrategy;
Vertical stacking layout strategy (DataViewer style).
Stacks series vertically with equal height allocation. This is the default layout for DataViewer where analog time series and digital event series share the canvas in a stacked arrangement.
LAYOUT RULES:

Stackable series (analog + stacked events) divide viewport equally
Non-stackable series (full-canvas digital intervals) span entire viewport
Series are ordered top-to-bottom by their index in the request
Global zoom/scale/pan are applied uniformly to all series

COORDINATE SYSTEM:

Y coordinates are in viewport space (typically -1 to +1 NDC)
Heights are in viewport units
Series centers are positioned to create even vertical spacing

class dl::ModelBase;
Abstract base class for all v2 deep-learning model wrappers.
A ModelBase subclass declares its expected input and output tensor slots via [inputSlots()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelBase.md#function-inputslots) and [outputSlots()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelBase.md#function-outputslots). The caller allocates and fills input tensors (using ChannelEncoders), invokes [forward()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelBase.md#function-forward), and decodes the output tensors (using ChannelDecoders).
Tensors always have a leading batch dimension. The model advertises [preferredBatchSize()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelBase.md#function-preferredbatchsize) and [maxBatchSize()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1ModelBase.md#function-maxbatchsize) so the UI can choose how many frames to process per call.

function train
virtual bool train(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params
) override
Train the model on labeled data.
Parameters:

features Feature matrix (features × observations). Each column is one observation with features.n_rows feature values.
labels Label row vector (1 × observations). Each element is a class index in [0, num_classes).
params Algorithm-specific parameters. May be nullptr to use defaults. Must be castable to the concrete parameter type expected by this model.

Return: true if training succeeded
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
labels.n_elem must equal features.n_cols (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features are expected to be z-score normalized for scale-sensitive classifiers (Logistic Regression, Softmax Regression). Tree-based methods (Random Forest) are scale-invariant. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Reimplements: MLCore::MLModelOperation::train
After successful training, [isTrained()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1LogisticRegressionOperation.md#function-istrained) returns true, and [numClasses()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1LogisticRegressionOperation.md#function-numclasses) and [numFeatures()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1LogisticRegressionOperation.md#function-numfeatures) reflect the training data dimensions.
The default implementation returns false (unsupervised models).

Features must be z-score normalized using the SAME parameters (mean/std) that were used for the training data passed to train(). Use FeatureConverter::applyZscoreNormalization() with stored parameters. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

class dl::Mask2DEncoder;
Encodes a Mask2D (set of pixel coordinates) into a tensor channel.
Supported modes:

Binary: Sets 1.0 at each mask pixel (scaled to tensor dimensions)

Mask pixel coordinates are scaled from source ImageSize to (H, W).





virtual std::string name() const override
Human-readable name for UI / registry.
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::name



virtual std::string inputTypeName() const override
Which geometry type this encoder expects (e.g. “Point2D”, “Mask2D”).
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::inputTypeName



static void encode(
    Mask2D const & mask,
    ImageSize source_size,
    at::Tensor & tensor,
    EncoderContext const & ctx,
    Mask2DEncoderParams const & params
)
Encode mask pixel set into tensor[batch_index, target_channel, :, :].
Parameters:

mask Set of pixel coordinates in source image coordinate space
source_size Spatial dimensions of the source image used to scale mask coordinates into tensor space
tensor Pre-allocated [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor to write into
ctx Encoder context (batch_index, target_channel, height, width)
params User-configurable encoding parameters (mode)

Precondition:

params.mode == Binary (enforcement: exception)
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; zero causes floating-point division by zero producing a +Inf scale factor, which makes static_cast of the resulting Inf undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; negative values (e.g. the ImageSize default -1) produce a negative scale factor, mapping all mask pixels to coordinate 0 instead of their true position (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor with at least 4 dimensions; fewer dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access when indexing tensor[batch_index][target_channel] (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0 and ctx.target_channel < tensor.size(1); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height == tensor.size(2) and ctx.width == tensor.size(3); if either ctx dimension exceeds the actual tensor spatial dimension the accessor write is out-of-bounds (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero causes std::clamp to receive an upper bound of -1 which is less than the lower bound of 0, invoking undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

An empty mask produces no output (no-op early return). Mask point coordinates outside the source image bounds are clamped to the tensor edges after scaling.

template <typename ViewType >
class LazyDigitalIntervalStorage;
Lazy digital interval storage that computes intervals on-demand from a view.
Stores a computation pipeline as a random-access view that transforms data on-demand. Enables efficient composition of transforms without materializing intermediate results.
The view must yield objects with .interval and .entity_id members (ClockTicksIntervalWithId, IntervalWithId, or convertible pair/tuple).

title: LazyDigitalIntervalStorage
LazyDigitalIntervalStorage
text:
Range-query limitation
getOverlappingRangeImpl() always uses an O(n) linear scan. Unlike OwningDigitalIntervalStorage and ViewDigitalIntervalStorage, lazy storage does not expose assumeDisjointIntervals() and therefore does not use the O(log n) binary-search fast path, even when the underlying view yields disjoint intervals. This is intentional for transform intermediates ([IntervalLayout::Overlapping](/api_generated/Files/Digital__Interval__Series_8hpp.md#enumvalue-overlapping)) where overlaps are possible; a disjoint fast path may be added later if needed.
ViewTypeType of the random-access range view

class RectangleInteractionController;
Controller for interactive rectangle creation and modification.
See: IGlyphInteractionController for the interface contract
Supports two modes:
Creation Mode (via [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classRectangleInteractionController.md#function-start)):

User clicks to set first corner
Drags to set opposite corner
Rectangle preview updates during drag
Complete on mouse release

Modification Mode (via [startEdgeDrag()](/api_generated/Classes/classRectangleInteractionController.md#function-startedgedrag)):

Used when user clicks on an edge of an existing rectangle
Only the specified edge moves during drag
Shows ghost of original position

Interval Mode (constrain_to_x_axis = true):

Rectangle height spans full canvas
Only X coordinates matter (for DigitalIntervalSeries)

Selection Box Mode (constrain_to_x_axis = false):

User defines both width and height
For rectangular selection regions

class PlottingSVG::SVGDocument;
Builds a UTF-8 SVG 1.1 document string with a full-canvas background and ordered <g> layers.
Precondition: ).
Layer content is concatenated verbatim; [build()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md#function-build) does not escape or validate SVG/XML. Callers must supply safe strings (see [setBackground](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md#function-setbackground), [setDescription](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md#function-setdescription), [addElements](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md#function-addelements), and [build](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md#function-build)





explicit SVGDocument(
    int width,
    int height
)
Create a document with pixel width and height used for the root <svg> and viewBox.
Precondition: width > 0 and height > 0 for a conventional pixel canvas and viewBox="0 0 …" (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



void setBackground(
    std::string const & hex_color
)
Set the full-canvas background rectangle fill (SVG paint syntax, typically #RRGGBB).
Precondition: hex_color must not contain ", &, or < (and otherwise be valid inside a double-quoted XML attribute). Values are inserted unescaped (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



void setDescription(
    std::string const & desc
)
Set prose inside <desc>…</desc>; the tag is omitted only when the stored string is empty.
Precondition: desc must not break XML structure (e.g. must not contain a raw </desc> sequence or unescaped & / < unless intentional). Content is inserted unescaped (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



void addElements(
    std::string const & layer_name,
    std::vector< std::string > const & elements
)
Append SVG fragments into a named layer (<g id="layer_name">).
Precondition:

layer_name must be safe inside a double-quoted id="…" attribute (no ", &, <, etc.). Should be a valid id token for consumers that enforce XML/SVG id rules (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Each string in elements should be a single SVG element (or fragment) that is valid in this context; content is written verbatim with indentation only (enforcement: none) [LOW]

If layer_name already exists, elements are appended to that layer’s vector in order.



std::string build() const
Serialize the accumulated document.
Postcondition:

Returns a string starting with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>, then a root <svg> with xmlns, width, height, and viewBox="0 0 width height" from the constructor.
When the stored description is non-empty, includes one <desc> child with that text (unescaped).
Always includes a full-viewport <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="…"/> using the current background string.
Emits one <g id="…"> per distinct layer_name in insertion order, each containing all accumulated elements for that layer, then closes </svg>.
Does not throw under normal std::ostringstream behavior.

class RaggedAnalogTimeSeries;
Ragged analog time series data structure.
RaggedAnalogTimeSeries stores time series data where each TimeFrameIndex can have a variable-length vector of float values. Unlike regular AnalogTimeSeries, the number of samples at each time point need not be constant.
This class manages:

Time series storage via type-erased storage wrapper (supports owning, view, and lazy)
TimeFrame association for time-based operations
Observer pattern integration for data change notifications
Range-based iteration interface
Cache optimization for fast-path iteration over contiguous storage

Storage Backends:

OwningRaggedAnalogStorage: Default, owns data in SoA layout
ViewRaggedAnalogStorage: Zero-copy filtered view of another storage
LazyRaggedAnalogStorage: On-demand computation from a transform view

Use cases include:

Spike trains with varying numbers of detected events per time bin
Multi-unit recordings where channel count varies over time
Feature vectors with time-varying dimensionality

Returns std::pair<[TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md), float> for backward compatibility with existing code that uses .first, .second, and structured bindings.

FlatElement
TimeSeriesConcepts.hpp for concept definitions

Return: A lazy range view of FlatElement objects
This creates a lazy view that flattens the ragged structure into individual FlatElement objects. Each element satisfies the TimeSeriesElement and ValueElement concepts, enabling use with generic time series algorithms.
Use this method when you need concept-compliant elements for generic algorithms. Use elements() when you need backward-compatible pair iteration.

for (auto elem : ragged_analog.elementsView()) { auto t = elem.time(); auto v = elem.value(); }

title: RaggedAnalogTimeSeries
text:
class RaggedAnalogTimeSeries;
Ragged analog time series data structure.
RaggedAnalogTimeSeries stores time series data where each TimeFrameIndex can have a variable-length vector of float values. Unlike regular AnalogTimeSeries, the number of samples at each time point need not be constant.
This class manages:

Time series storage via type-erased storage wrapper (supports owning, view, and lazy)
TimeFrame association for time-based operations
Observer pattern integration for data change notifications
Range-based iteration interface
Cache optimization for fast-path iteration over contiguous storage

Storage Backends:

OwningRaggedAnalogStorage: Default, owns data in SoA layout
ViewRaggedAnalogStorage: Zero-copy filtered view of another storage
LazyRaggedAnalogStorage: On-demand computation from a transform view

Use cases include:

Spike trains with varying numbers of detected events per time bin
Multi-unit recordings where channel count varies over time
Feature vectors with time-varying dimensionality

Return: A lazy range view of (TimeFrameIndex, float) pairs
This creates a lazy view that flattens the ragged structure into individual (time, value) pairs. This is the analog of RaggedTimeSeries::elements() and enables uniform iteration API across all ragged container types.
Returns std::pair<[TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md), float> for backward compatibility with existing code that uses .first, .second, and structured bindings.

FlatElement
TimeSeriesConcepts.hpp for concept definitions

Return: A lazy range view of FlatElement objects
This creates a lazy view that flattens the ragged structure into individual FlatElement objects. Each element satisfies the TimeSeriesElement and ValueElement concepts, enabling use with generic time series algorithms.
Use this method when you need concept-compliant elements for generic algorithms. Use elements() when you need backward-compatible pair iteration.

for (auto elem : ragged_analog.elementsView()) { auto t = elem.time(); auto v = elem.value(); }

class CSVLoader;
Format-centric CSV loader for all CSV file data types.
This loader follows the format-centric architecture where one loader handles a specific file format (CSV) for all applicable data types.
Supported data types:

DM_DataType::Line: Line/whisker data (single or multi-file CSV)
DM_DataType::Points: Point tracking data (simple CSV or DLC format)
DM_DataType::Mask: Mask data (RLE-encoded CSV)
DM_DataType::Analog: Analog time series (single/two column CSV)
DM_DataType::DigitalEvent: Digital event timestamps (with optional multi-series)
DM_DataType::DigitalInterval: Digital intervals (start/end column pairs or binary state columns)

This loader supports batch loading for:

DigitalEvent CSV with identifier column (returns one series per identifier)
DigitalEvent CSV with multi_file=true (returns one series per file in a directory)
Points DLC format with all_bodyparts=true (returns one PointData per bodypart)
DigitalInterval with csv_layout=“binary_state” and all_columns=true (returns one series per column)

CSV Layouts for DigitalInterval:

“intervals” (default): Two columns with start/end times for each interval
“binary_state”: Rows represent time points, columns contain 0/1 state values. Intervals are extracted from contiguous regions where value >= threshold.

Configuration options vary by data type - see individual load methods for required and optional JSON configuration fields.

class PlottingOpenGL::AxisRenderer;
Renders axis lines and grid overlays using OpenGL.
Note: The shaders must be loaded into ShaderManager before calling render methods. Typically done by the hosting widget in initializeGL().
This renderer manages its own shader programs:

“axes” shader for solid lines (from ShaderManager)
“dashed_line” shader for grid lines (from ShaderManager)

Unlike other batch renderers, AxisRenderer does not implement IBatchRenderer because it doesn’t receive data from RenderableScene batches. Instead, it renders directly from configuration structs.

class PlottingOpenGL::AxisRenderer;
Renders axis lines and grid overlays using OpenGL.
Note: The shaders must be loaded into ShaderManager before calling render methods. Typically done by the hosting widget in initializeGL().
This renderer manages its own shader programs:

“axes” shader for solid lines (from ShaderManager)
“dashed_line” shader for grid lines (from ShaderManager)

Unlike other batch renderers, AxisRenderer does not implement IBatchRenderer because it doesn’t receive data from RenderableScene batches. Instead, it renders directly from configuration structs.

struct dl::RuntimeModelSpec;
JSON-serializable specification for a runtime-defined model.
Allows users to specify an ExecuTorch model’s inputs and outputs via JSON at runtime, without recompilation.
JSON example: ```json
{ “model_id”: “my_tracker”, “display_name”: “My Tracker”, “description”: “Tracks whisker tips”, “weights_path”: “model.pte”, “preferred_batch_size”: 1, “max_batch_size”: 1, “batch_mode”: { “dynamic”: { “min”: 1, “max”: 8 } }, “weights_variants”: [ { “path”: “model_batch1.pt2”, “batch_size”: 1, “label”: “recurrent” }, { “path”: “model_batch8.pt2”, “batch_size”: 8, “label”: “batched” } ], “inputs”: [ { “name”: “image”, “shape”: [3, 256, 256], “recommended_encoder”: “ImageEncoder” } ], “outputs”: [ { “name”: “heatmap”, “shape”: [1, 256, 256], “recommended_decoder”: “TensorToMask2D” } ], “post_encoder”: [ { “module”: “global_avg_pool” } ] }

Similar to TypedParamExecutor but for container-level operations. Eliminates per-call parameter casts by capturing params at construction.

DataInspectorState
text:
Pinning Behavior
When unpinned (default), the inspector responds to SelectionContext changes and updates to show the newly selected data.
When pinned, the inspector ignores SelectionContext and continues to show its current data, allowing the user to compare data across selections.

title: DataInspectorState
text:
Multiple Inspectors
Multiple DataInspector instances can exist simultaneously. Each has its own state and can be pinned independently.

typename InContainer2 ,
typename OutContainer ,
typename Params >
class Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::RegisterBinaryContainerTransform;
RAII helper for compile-time binary container transform registration.
Registers a container-level transform that takes two containers as input.
Example usage: ```cpp
namespace { auto const register_digital_interval_boolean = RegisterBinaryContainerTransform< DigitalIntervalSeries, DigitalIntervalSeries, DigitalIntervalSeries, DigitalIntervalBooleanParams>( “DigitalIntervalBoolean”, digitalIntervalBoolean, ContainerTransformMetadata{ .description = “Apply boolean logic between two interval series”, .category = “Signal Processing / Logic” } ); }

Load and compile the compute shader program.
Parameters:

shader_resource_path Path to the .comp shader (file or Qt resource). Defaults to “:/shaders/line_intersection.comp”.

Return: true if the shader compiled and linked successfully.
Must be called with a current OpenGL 4.3+ context. Uses ShaderManager to manage the program lifetime per-context.



void cleanup()
Release the shader program (managed by ShaderManager, so this is a no-op on the program itself, but resets internal state).



inline bool isAvailable() const
Return: true if initialize() succeeded and the compute shader is usable.



virtual CorePlotting::LineIntersectionResult intersect(
    CorePlotting::LineBatchData const & batch,
    CorePlotting::LineIntersectionQuery const & query
) const override
Find all lines whose segments intersect the query line.
Parameters:

batch (Ignored in GPU path; interface conformance only.)
query The query line and transform parameters.

Return: Indices of intersected lines (0-based into LineBatchData::lines).
Note: The batch parameter is unused — segment data is read from the store’s SSBOs. The parameter exists to satisfy the interface. The CPU-side data from the store is used for result mapping.
Precondition:

initialize() must have been called and returned true (enforcement: runtime_check — returns empty result if !m_initialized)
A valid OpenGL context must be current on the calling thread (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL] — resetIntersectionCount(), dispatchBatched(), glMemoryBarrier(), glMapBufferRange() all issue raw GL calls. initialize() checks the context at setup time but does not re-check at call time.
m_store.isInitialized() == true (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT] — if the store’s SSBOs are not created, bindForCompute() silently no-ops, the compute shader runs with unbound SSBOs, and an empty result is returned with no error. The caller cannot distinguish “no intersections” from “store not ready”.
m_store.upload() must have been called at least once (enforcement: runtime_check — silent, via cpu.empty() guard) — if no data has been uploaded, the function returns an empty result before dispatch. The CPU mirror check provides the guard, but gives no diagnostic to distinguish “no data” from “no hits”.
query.start_ndc != query.end_ndc (query line must be non-degenerate) (enforcement: none) [LOW] — a zero-length query line is sent to the shader as-is and will produce no intersections (or undefined shader behaviour).
query.tolerance > 0.0f (enforcement: none) [LOW] — zero or negative tolerance means no segment can be “within” the threshold; all queries return empty results silently.
m_store must remain valid (not destroyed) for the lifetime of this intersector (enforcement: none — by construction contract on ctor)

Reimplements: CorePlotting::ILineBatchIntersector::intersect
Dispatches the compute shader in batches respecting hardware work-group limits, then reads back results via buffer mapping. The number of results is capped at BatchLineStore::RESULTS_CAPACITY.
Returns an empty result (not an error) if:

!isAvailable() or the compute program is null
The store’s CPU data is empty (no upload() has been called)
GLFunctions::getExtra() returns null after dispatch
The compute shader produces zero intersection hits
m_store is not initialized (bindForCompute() silently no-ops)

class CorePlotting::Interaction::PolygonInteractionController;
Controller for interactive polygon creation and modification.
See:

IGlyphInteractionController for the interface contract
PolygonSelectionHandler for the original Qt-based implementation

Unlike LineInteractionController and RectangleInteractionController which use drag-based interactions, PolygonInteractionController uses a click-based approach where each click adds a new vertex to the polygon.
Creation Mode (via [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-start) + repeated [addVertex()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-addvertex) calls):

Call [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-start) to begin polygon creation (adds first vertex)
Call [addVertex()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-addvertex) for each additional vertex
Call [complete()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-complete) to finalize the polygon (requires min_vertices)
Alternatively, click near the first vertex to auto-close (if enabled)

Modification Mode (via [startVertexDrag()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-startvertexdrag)):

Used when user clicks on a vertex of an existing polygon
Only the specified vertex moves during drag
Shows ghost of original polygon

Preview Updates:

Call [updateCursorPosition()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1PolygonInteractionController.md#function-updatecursorposition) during mouse move to show a preview line from the last vertex to the current cursor position

std::string model_name = "Logit Projection";
Name of the supervised dim reduction model (must be in the registry).
Defaults to “Logit Projection”. The model must have task type MLTaskType::SupervisedDimensionalityReduction.



MLModelParametersBase const  * model_params = nullptr;
Model-specific parameters (optional — nullptr uses defaults).



std::string feature_tensor_key;
DataManager key of the TensorData to reduce.
Must be a 2D tensor whose rows represent observations.



ConversionConfig conversion_config;
Feature conversion configuration (NaN dropping, z-score normalization).



LabelAssemblyConfig label_config;
Label assembly configuration (which labeling mode to use).
Choose from: LabelFromIntervals, LabelFromTimeEntityGroups, LabelFromDataEntityGroups, or LabelFromEvents.



std::string label_interval_key;
DataManager key of the DigitalIntervalSeries for interval-based labels.
Required when label_config holds LabelFromIntervals.



std::string label_event_key;
DataManager key of the DigitalEventSeries for event-based labels.
Required when label_config holds LabelFromEvents.



std::string training_interval_key;
DataManager key of a DigitalIntervalSeries defining the training region.
When non-empty, only feature rows whose TimeFrameIndex falls within these intervals are used for model fitting. Rows outside the training region are excluded from fitting but are still projected (transformed) by the fitted model. This mirrors the classification pipeline’s training region concept.
When empty (default), all labeled rows are used for fitting.



std::string output_key = "logit_projection";
DataManager key to store the output TensorData under.



std::string time_key_str = "time";
Time key string for TimeFrame lookups.
Identifies which TimeFrame the feature tensor’s rows are indexed by.



bool defer_dm_writes = false;
If true, skip DataManager writes and store output in the result.
Set this to true when running from a background thread to avoid DataManager observer callbacks modifying Qt widgets from the wrong thread.

struct MLCore::PredictionRegionConfig;
Specifies where prediction should be performed.
If predict_all_rows is true, predictions are made on all feature rows (the same tensor used for training — useful for full-dataset scoring).
Otherwise, a separate prediction tensor can be specified via prediction_tensor_key. If neither is set, no prediction is performed.





bool predict_all_rows = true;
If true, predict on all rows of the training feature tensor.



std::string prediction_tensor_key;
DataManager key for a separate prediction feature tensor.
Used when predict_all_rows is false. Must have the same column structure as the training tensor. Rows can be different. If empty and predict_all_rows is false, no prediction is performed.



std::string prediction_interval_key;
DataManager key of a DigitalIntervalSeries specifying target output frames.
When non-empty, the pipeline computes the bounding span across training labels and this interval for prediction (so sequence models retain full temporal context), then filters output to only frames within this interval.
When empty and predict_all_rows is true, output includes all frames.



bool constrained_decoding = true;
For sequence models, clamp the HMM initial distribution at boundaries.
When true and the model is a sequence model (isSequenceModel()), the pipeline overrides the HMM initial state distribution to the last known ground-truth label at prediction segment boundaries. This avoids cold-start inaccuracy when predicting regions adjacent to labeled data.
Ignored for frame-independent models.

template <typename TData >
class RaggedTimeSeries;
Base template class for ragged time series data structures.
Template Parameters:

TData The data type stored in each entry (e.g., Line2D, Mask2D, Point2D)

RaggedTimeSeries provides a unified interface for time series data where multiple unique entries can exist at each timestamp. Each entry has a unique EntityId for tracking and manipulation.
This base class manages:

Time series storage as a map from TimeFrameIndex to vectors of DataEntry
Image size metadata
TimeFrame association
Identity context (data key and EntityRegistry) for automatic EntityId management

Derived classes (LineData, MaskData, PointData) specialize the template parameter TData and provide domain-specific operations.





using RaggedTimeSeries< TData >::DataModifier =  ModificationHandle<TData>;
Type alias for modification handle.
This provides a unified type for RAII-style modification handles. Derived classes can use this or define their own aliases for convenience.

template <typename DerivedTarget >
inline std::optional< std::size_t > mergeOverwriteTo(
    DerivedTarget & target,
    NotifyObservers notify
) const
Merge all entries from this series into the target with per-time overwrite.
Parameters:

target The target to merge into
notify If true, the target will notify its observers after the operation

Template Parameters:

DerivedTarget The derived class type (LineData, MaskData, or PointData)

Return: Number of entries copied on success; std::nullopt on precondition violation
Precondition:

target must not be the same object as *this
[getTimeFrame()](/api_generated/Classes/classRaggedTimeSeries.md#function-gettimeframe) and target.getTimeFrame() must be non-null and refer to the same [TimeFrame](/api_generated/Classes/classTimeFrame.md) object (shared_ptr identity)

Postcondition:

For every t in [getTimesWithData()](/api_generated/Classes/classRaggedTimeSeries.md#function-gettimeswithdata), target content at t equals source content at t (same data and EntityIds)
Times present only in the target are unchanged
The source is unchanged

For every time present in the source, any existing target entries at that time are removed and replaced with the source entries. Times present only in the target are left unchanged. Source EntityIds are preserved in the target. The source is not modified.
Cross-time removal via clearByEntityIds applies only to registered EntityIds (non-sentinel). [EntityId(0)](/api_generated/Classes/structEntityId.md) is treated as anonymous and is not used for global identity cleanup.

Get the storage cache for fast-path iteration.

This is useful for performance-critical code that needs to iterate over all data with minimal overhead:
auto cache = ts.getStorageCache();
if (cache.isValid()) {
    // Fast path: direct pointer access
    for (size_t i = 0; i < cache.cache_size; ++i) {
        auto time = cache.getTime(i);
        auto const& data = cache.getData(i);
        // ...

    // Slow path: use elements() view
    for (auto [time, entry] : ts.elements()) {
        // ...

The view must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned RaggedTimeSeries. Capture by value in lambdas or ensure base series outlives the lazy series.
For materialized (eager) storage, call .materialize() on the result

Creates a RaggedTimeSeries that computes values on-demand from a ranges view. The view must be a random-access range that yields tuples compatible with (TimeFrameIndex, EntityId, TData) or (TimeFrameIndex, EntityId, TData const&). No intermediate data is materialized - values are computed when accessed.
This enables efficient transform pipelines without intermediate allocations:
// Skeletonization without materializing intermediate results
auto transformed_view = mask_data.flattened_data()
    | std::views::transform([](auto tuple) {
        auto const& [time, eid, mask_ref] = tuple;
        return std::make_tuple(time, eid, skeletonize(mask_ref.get()));
    });

auto lazy_skeleton = RaggedTimeSeries<Line2D>::createFromView(
    transformed_view, 
    mask_data.getTimeFrame(),
    mask_data.getImageSize()
);

// Access computes skeletonization on-demand
auto skeleton = lazy_skeleton->getData(0);

template <typename TData >
class RaggedTimeSeries;
Base template class for ragged time series data structures.
Template Parameters:

TData The data type stored in each entry (e.g., Line2D, Mask2D, Point2D)

RaggedTimeSeries provides a unified interface for time series data where multiple unique entries can exist at each timestamp. Each entry has a unique EntityId for tracking and manipulation.
This base class manages:

Time series storage as a map from TimeFrameIndex to vectors of DataEntry
Image size metadata
TimeFrame association
Identity context (data key and EntityRegistry) for automatic EntityId management

Derived classes (LineData, MaskData, PointData) specialize the template parameter TData and provide domain-specific operations.
