Parameters:

target The target to merge into
notify If true, the target will notify its observers after the operation

Template Parameters:

DerivedTarget The derived class type (LineData, MaskData, or PointData)

Return: Number of entries copied on success; std::nullopt on precondition violation
Precondition:

target must not be the same object as *this
[getTimeFrame()](/api_generated/Classes/classRaggedTimeSeries.md#function-gettimeframe) and target.getTimeFrame() must be non-null and refer to the same [TimeFrame](/api_generated/Classes/classTimeFrame.md) object (shared_ptr identity)

Postcondition:

For every t in [getTimesWithData()](/api_generated/Classes/classRaggedTimeSeries.md#function-gettimeswithdata), target content at t equals source content at t (same data and EntityIds)
Times present only in the target are unchanged
The source is unchanged

For every time present in the source, any existing target entries at that time are removed and replaced with the source entries. Times present only in the target are left unchanged. Source EntityIds are preserved in the target. The source is not modified.
Cross-time removal via clearByEntityIds applies only to registered EntityIds (non-sentinel). [EntityId(0)](/api_generated/Classes/structEntityId.md) is treated as anonymous and is not used for global identity cleanup.

inline RaggedStorageCache< TData > const & getStorageCache() const
Get the storage cache for fast-path iteration.
Return: RaggedStorageCache with valid pointers if storage is contiguous
Returns a cache structure that provides direct pointer access to underlying data when storage is contiguous (owning). For view-based storage, returns an invalid cache.
This is useful for performance-critical code that needs to iterate over all data with minimal overhead:
auto cache = ts.getStorageCache();
if (cache.isValid()) {
    // Fast path: direct pointer access
    for (size_t i = 0; i < cache.cache_size; ++i) {
        auto time = cache.getTime(i);
        auto const& data = cache.getData(i);
        // ...
    }
} else {
    // Slow path: use elements() view
    for (auto [time, entry] : ts.elements()) {
        // ...
    }
}

flattened_data() to get a view over an existing RaggedTimeSeries

Return: std::shared_ptr Lazy ragged time series
Note:

The view must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned RaggedTimeSeries. Capture by value in lambdas or ensure base series outlives the lazy series.
For materialized (eager) storage, call .materialize() on the result

Creates a RaggedTimeSeries that computes values on-demand from a ranges view. The view must be a random-access range that yields tuples compatible with (TimeFrameIndex, EntityId, TData) or (TimeFrameIndex, EntityId, TData const&). No intermediate data is materialized - values are computed when accessed.
This enables efficient transform pipelines without intermediate allocations:
// Skeletonization without materializing intermediate results
auto transformed_view = mask_data.flattened_data()
    | std::views::transform([](auto tuple) {
        auto const& [time, eid, mask_ref] = tuple;
        return std::make_tuple(time, eid, skeletonize(mask_ref.get()));
    });

auto lazy_skeleton = RaggedTimeSeries<Line2D>::createFromView(
    transformed_view, 
    mask_data.getTimeFrame(),
    mask_data.getImageSize()
);

// Access computes skeletonization on-demand
auto skeleton = lazy_skeleton->getData(0);

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::IntervalReductionParams;
Parameters for interval reduction transforms.
Controls which range reduction is applied to data gathered within each interval.
Example JSON: ```json
{ “reduction_name”: “MeanValue”, “column_name”: “mean_firing_rate” }

## Public Attributes Documentation

### variable reduction_name

```cpp
std::string reduction_name = "MeanValue";
Name of the range reduction to apply.
Must be a reduction registered in RangeReductionRegistry. The reduction must accept the element type of the source data:

AnalogTimeSeries → TimeValuePoint reductions (MeanValue, MaxValue, etc.)
DigitalEventSeries → EventWithId reductions (EventCount, EventPresence, etc.)
DigitalIntervalSeries → IntervalWithId reductions (IntervalCount, etc.)



std::string reduction_params_json = "{}";
JSON string for reduction-specific parameters.
Most built-in reductions are stateless and don’t need parameters.



std::string column_name = "value";
Name of the output column in the produced TensorData.

class DigitalIntervalSeries;
A sorted collection of time intervals with entity tracking.
DigitalIntervalSeries stores intervals as (start, end, EntityId) tuples, maintaining intervals in sorted order by start time. Each interval represents a time range (compare to DigitalEventSeries for discrete time points).

text:
Primary Interface

view(): Returns a lazy range of ClockTicksIntervalWithId objects for iteration
getStoredInterval(): Returns index-space interval at storage index (save/export)
viewInRange(): Returns intervals overlapping a time range (requires TimeFrame)
hasIntervalAtTime(): Check if any interval contains a time (requires TimeFrame)
addEvent()/removeInterval(): Modify intervals (owning storage only)
createView()/createFromView(): Create view/lazy backed series
materialize(): Convert any storage type to owning storage

title: DigitalIntervalSeries

The class supports three storage backends (Owning, View, Lazy) that provide different performance tradeoffs. See Digital_Interval_Series.hpp for details.

struct CorePlotting::FeatureColor::ThresholdMapping;
Threshold (binary) mapping from float values to colors.
Values are compared against a threshold, if float >= threshold then above_color, else below_color.
Useful for:

DigitalIntervalSeries (already 0/1, threshold=0.5)
Continuous data with a meaningful cutoff (e.g., “highlight velocity > 20 cm/s”)
TensorData columns with binary labels (0/1 classifier output)

struct CorePlotting::LayoutRequest;
Request for layout computation.
Contains all information needed by LayoutEngine to compute positions. Immutable input to layout algorithms.
Note: User zoom/pan state is NOT part of LayoutRequest. That state belongs in ViewState (CoordinateTransform/ViewState.hpp), which is the single source of truth for camera state. The LayoutEngine computes relative series positions; ViewState handles the View and Projection matrices that apply zoom/pan.
MVP composition in widgets: Model = SeriesLayout::computeModelMatrix() // From LayoutEngine View + Projection = computeMatricesFromViewState() // From ViewState Final = Projection * View * Model

class dl::PostEncoderModule;
Abstract base class for tensor-to-tensor post-encoder processing.
See: ChannelDecoder for the complementary stage that converts torch outputs into DataManager-compatible types
Implementations expose [apply()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1PostEncoderModule.md#function-apply) to transform feature tensors and [outputShape()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1PostEncoderModule.md#function-outputshape) to propagate rank/shape metadata without running inference. Modules are stateless by default; stateful modules (e.g. [SpatialPointExtractModule](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1SpatialPointExtractModule.md)) expose setters to update per-frame query state before [apply()](/api_generated/Classes/classdl_1_1PostEncoderModule.md#function-apply).
Usage:
dl::GlobalAvgPoolModule pool;
at::Tensor features = encoder.forward(inputs)["features"];
at::Tensor pooled = pool.apply(features);  // [B, C, H, W] → [B, C]

template <typename DataType >
class StateEstimation::CompositeFeatureExtractor;
Feature extractor that chains multiple extractors together.
Template Parameters:

DataType The raw data type to extract features from (e.g., Line2D)

This extractor allows combining multiple feature extractors to produce a concatenated feature vector. The extractors are applied in the order they are added, and their outputs are concatenated together.
The composite respects each feature’s temporal behavior metadata:

KINEMATIC_2D features: 2D measurement → 4D state (position + velocity)
STATIC features: 1D measurement → 1D state (no velocity)
SCALAR_DYNAMIC features: 1D measurement → 2D state (value + derivative)

Example: Combining centroid (KINEMATIC_2D) + length (STATIC): Measurements: [x_centroid, y_centroid, length] (3D) State: [x, y, vx, vy, length] (5D)
The initial state is constructed by concatenating the states from each extractor and combining their covariances into a block-diagonal matrix.

title: StateEstimation::CompositeFeatureExtractor
text:
template <typename DataType >
class StateEstimation::CompositeFeatureExtractor;
Feature extractor that chains multiple extractors together.
Template Parameters:

DataType The raw data type to extract features from (e.g., Line2D)

This extractor allows combining multiple feature extractors to produce a concatenated feature vector. The extractors are applied in the order they are added, and their outputs are concatenated together.
The composite respects each feature’s temporal behavior metadata:

KINEMATIC_2D features: 2D measurement → 4D state (position + velocity)
STATIC features: 1D measurement → 1D state (no velocity)
SCALAR_DYNAMIC features: 1D measurement → 2D state (value + derivative)

Example: Combining centroid (KINEMATIC_2D) + length (STATIC): Measurements: [x_centroid, y_centroid, length] (3D) State: [x, y, vx, vy, length] (5D)
The initial state is constructed by concatenating the states from each extractor and combining their covariances into a block-diagonal matrix.

struct CorePlotting::SeriesDataCache;
Cached statistical data for a series.
Note: All members are mutable to allow lazy computation even when accessed through const references.
Contains computed values that are expensive to calculate (e.g., mean, standard deviation) but needed for display calculations (e.g., intrinsic scaling). These are mutable caches that get invalidated when the underlying data changes.
Separated from style configuration and layout results per the CorePlotting architecture (see DESIGN.md, ROADMAP.md Phase 0).

class dl::TorchScriptBackend;
TorchScript inference backend — loads .pt files via torch::jit::load().
This backend uses the TorchScript interpreter built into libtorch to load and execute serialized models produced by torch.jit.trace() or torch.jit.script() in Python.
While TorchScript is deprecated by the PyTorch team, it remains fully functional in libtorch 2.9.0 and provides the simplest export path. Legacy models (EfficientSAM, scm) already use this format.
Key characteristics:

Interpreter-based execution with JIT fusion optimizations
Supports multiple named methods (e.g. “forward”, “encode”, “decode”)
Supports arbitrary dynamic shapes natively
Model runs on the device selected by DeviceManager (CPU or CUDA)

title: dl::TorchScriptBackend
text:
class dl::TorchScriptBackend;
TorchScript inference backend — loads .pt files via torch::jit::load().
This backend uses the TorchScript interpreter built into libtorch to load and execute serialized models produced by torch.jit.trace() or torch.jit.script() in Python.
While TorchScript is deprecated by the PyTorch team, it remains fully functional in libtorch 2.9.0 and provides the simplest export path. Legacy models (EfficientSAM, scm) already use this format.
Key characteristics:

Interpreter-based execution with JIT fusion optimizations
Supports multiple named methods (e.g. “forward”, “encode”, “decode”)
Supports arbitrary dynamic shapes natively
Model runs on the device selected by DeviceManager (CPU or CUDA)

class CorePlotting::Interaction::RectangleInteractionController;
Controller for interactive rectangle creation and modification.
See: IGlyphInteractionController for the interface contract
Supports two modes:
Creation Mode (via [start()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1RectangleInteractionController.md#function-start)):

User clicks to set first corner
Drags to set opposite corner
Rectangle preview updates during drag
Complete on mouse release

Modification Mode (via [startEdgeDrag()](/api_generated/Classes/classCorePlotting_1_1Interaction_1_1RectangleInteractionController.md#function-startedgedrag)):

Used when user clicks on an edge of an existing rectangle
Only the specified edge moves during drag
Shows ghost of original position

Interval Mode (constrain_to_x_axis = true):

Rectangle height spans full canvas
Only X coordinates matter (for DigitalIntervalSeries)

Selection Box Mode (constrain_to_x_axis = false):

User defines both width and height
For rectangular selection regions

struct NewAnalogTimeSeriesDisplayOptions;
Display options for new analog time series visualization system.
Comprehensive configuration for analog series display including scaling, positioning, and visual properties.
ARCHITECTURE NOTE (Phase 0 Cleanup): This struct has been refactored to use CorePlotting’s separated concerns:

[style](/api_generated/Classes/structNewAnalogTimeSeriesDisplayOptions.md#variable-style): Pure visual configuration (color, alpha, thickness) - user-settable
layout: Positioning output from LayoutEngine - read-only computed values
[data_cache](/api_generated/Classes/structNewAnalogTimeSeriesDisplayOptions.md#variable-data-cache): Expensive statistical calculations - mutable cache

This separation clarifies ownership and prevents conflation of concerns. See CorePlotting/DESIGN.md and ROADMAP.md Phase 0 for details.

std::string model_name;
Name of the model to use (must be registered in the registry).
E.g., “Random Forest”, “Naive Bayes”, “Logistic Regression”



MLModelParametersBase const  * model_params = nullptr;
Model-specific parameters (optional — nullptr uses defaults).
Must match the concrete parameter type expected by the chosen model.



std::string feature_tensor_key;
DataManager key of the TensorData to use as the feature matrix.
The tensor must be 2D with time-indexed rows (RowType::TimeFrameIndex).



LabelAssemblyConfig label_config;
Label assembly configuration (which labeling mode to use).



std::string label_interval_key;
DataManager key of the DigitalIntervalSeries for interval-based labels.
Required when label_config holds LabelFromIntervals. Ignored for other labeling modes.



std::string label_event_key;
DataManager key of the DigitalEventSeries for event-based labels.
Required when label_config holds LabelFromEvents. Ignored for other labeling modes.



std::string training_interval_key;
DataManager key of a DigitalIntervalSeries defining the training region.
When non-empty, only feature rows whose TimeFrameIndex falls within one of the intervals in this series are used for training. Rows outside the training region are excluded from label assembly, class balancing, and model fitting, but may still be used for prediction.
When empty, all rows in the feature tensor are used for training.



std::string validation_interval_key;
DataManager key of a DigitalIntervalSeries defining the validation region.
When non-empty, only frames within these intervals are used for computing validation metrics. Unlike the old heuristic (“everything outside training = validation”), this explicitly specifies which intervals have known labels for evaluation.
Validation intervals are NOT used for training.



std::size_t max_cv_folds = 5;
Maximum number of leave-one-interval-out cross-validation folds.
When > 0 and at least 2 training intervals exist, the pipeline holds out each training interval in turn (up to this many), retrains on the rest, and predicts the held-out interval with boundary constraints. Set to 0 to disable cross-validation.



ConversionConfig conversion_config;
Feature conversion configuration.
Controls NaN dropping, z-score normalization, etc.



bool balance_classes = false;
Whether to apply class balancing before training.



BalancingConfig balancing_config;
Class balancing configuration (used if balance_classes is true).



PredictionRegionConfig prediction_region;
Where to make predictions after training.



PredictionWriterConfig output_config;
Configuration for writing prediction outputs.



std::string time_key_str = "time";
Time key string for time frame lookups.
Identifies which TimeFrame the feature tensor’s rows are indexed by. Used for label assembly (interval lookups) and output writing.



bool defer_dm_writes = false;
If true, skip DataManager writes and store output in the result.
When running from a background thread, DataManager writes trigger observer callbacks that may manipulate Qt widgets, which is undefined behavior. Set this to true and perform the writes on the main thread instead.

template <typename DataType >
class StateEstimation::StateEstimator;
State estimator for smoothing and outlier detection on grouped data.
Template Parameters:

DataType raw observation type (e.g., Line2D)

This class performs forward-backward smoothing using a Kalman filter (or any IFilter) on data that has already been grouped. It is separate from the assignment problem and can be used for:

Final smoothing after global assignment
Outlier detection for manual review

V2 parameters for Z-Score normalization.
Unlike V1 ZScoreNormalizationParams, this struct has no rfl::Skip fields or preprocess() method. Instead, mean and std_dev are regular fields that get populated via parameter bindings from the PipelineValueStore.
This eliminates the need for PreprocessingRegistry and enables configuration purely through JSON pipeline definitions.

Derived The concrete storage implementation type.

Uses Curiously Recurring Template Pattern to eliminate virtual function overhead while maintaining a polymorphic-like interface. Events are stored as TimeFrameIndex values (representing event times) with associated EntityIds.

TimeFrameIndex events[] - sorted event times

struct MLCore::HMMParameters;
Parameters for Hidden Markov Model (Gaussian emissions).
Maps to mlpack::HMM<mlpack::GaussianDistribution<>> hyperparameters. Supervised training uses labeled sequences to estimate transition and emission parameters directly.
When [use_diagonal_covariance](/api_generated/Classes/structMLCore_1_1HMMParameters.md#variable-use-diagonal-covariance) is true, uses mlpack::DiagonalGaussianDistribution instead of the full covariance variant. Diagonal covariance reduces parameters per state from M(M+1)/2 to M, improving numerical stability with limited training data and reducing emission evaluation cost from O(M^2) to O(M).

class Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline;
Builder for chaining multiple transforms together.
This class enables composing a sequence of transforms that will be applied in order, with automatic container type transitions.
The pipeline is fully generic and works with any compatible transforms.
Example usage: ```cpp
auto pipeline = TransformPipeline() .addStep(“CalculateMaskArea”, MaskAreaParams{}) .addStep(“SumReduction”, SumReductionParams{});
// Execute with correct input/output types std::shared_ptr result = pipeline.execute<MaskData, AnalogTimeSeries>(mask_data);

Return: Output container
Analyzes the pipeline structure and chooses the optimal execution strategy:

Pure element chains: Fused single-pass execution (via executeFused)
Chains with time-grouped: Materialized intermediate execution (via execute)

Use this when the output type is known at compile time.

Execute a multi-step element-level pipeline with full fusion (Specialist).
Parameters:

input Input data

Template Parameters:

InputContainer Input container type
OutputContainer Output container type

See:

executeOptimized Automatic selection of this method
executeAsView For lazy evaluation without materialization

Return: Output with composed transformation applied
For element→element→element pipelines (no time-grouped transforms), this composes all transforms into a single function and executes in one pass with zero intermediate allocations.
Example: Mask2D → skeletonize → fitLine → resample Results in: for (mask : masks) { output.add(resample(fitLine(skeletonize(mask)))); }
Performance:

Single pass through input data
No intermediate container allocations
Intermediate values stay hot in CPU cache
Type erasure overhead (~1-2 pointer dereferences per element per step)

Implementation: Uses runtime function composition with type-erased intermediate values. This allows arbitrary pipeline lengths determined at runtime (e.g., from UI).

template <typename Derived >
class DigitalIntervalStorageBase;
CRTP base class for digital interval storage implementations.
Template Parameters:

Derived The concrete storage implementation type

Uses Curiously Recurring Template Pattern to eliminate virtual function overhead while maintaining a polymorphic interface. Intervals are stored as Interval values (representing start/end times) with associated EntityIds.
The SoA (Structure of Arrays) layout stores parallel vectors:

Interval intervals[] - sorted by start time
EntityId entity_ids[] - corresponding entity identifiers

title: DigitalIntervalStorageBase

template <typename Derived >
class DigitalIntervalStorageBase;
CRTP base class for digital interval storage implementations.
Template Parameters:

Derived The concrete storage implementation type

Uses Curiously Recurring Template Pattern to eliminate virtual function overhead while maintaining a polymorphic interface. Intervals are stored as Interval values (representing start/end times) with associated EntityIds.
The SoA (Structure of Arrays) layout stores parallel vectors:

Interval intervals[] - sorted by start time
EntityId entity_ids[] - corresponding entity identifiers

class PlottingSVG::SVGScalebar;
Decoration that draws a horizontal scale bar in pixel space.
Bar length in pixels is scalebar_length * (canvas_width / visible_time_span), matching [PlottingSVG::createScalebarSVG](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespacePlottingSVG.md#function-createscalebarsvg) / legacy DataViewer export: full canvas width represents time_range_end - time_range_start.





explicit SVGScalebar(
    int scalebar_length,
    float time_range_start,
    float time_range_end
)
Build a scalebar for a fixed length in time units over a visible time interval.
Parameters:

scalebar_length Extent of the bar in time units (label shows this integer as text).
time_range_start Start of the visible time window (same units as the plot time axis).
time_range_end End of the visible time window; must be strictly after time_range_start for [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) to emit elements.

Precondition:

time_range_end > time_range_start with a finite positive difference if callers expect non-empty output from [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
time_range_start and time_range_end are finite values so the stored span behaves as a normal numeric interval (enforcement: none) [LOW] — non-finite values make [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) return an empty vector in typical cases but are not asserted
scalebar_length != 0 if the bar should have non-zero pixel length for typical ranges (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition: Length and time endpoints match the arguments; style and corner use defaults until setters run.

    ScalebarCorner corner
)
Choose which canvas corner anchors the scalebar group.

corner Anchor corner for layout.

Precondition: None (all enum values are handled).

    int pixels
)
Inset from the relevant canvas edges when placing the bar (pixels).
Parameters:

pixels Padding used by corner layout (distance from edges).

Precondition: pixels >= 0 so “inset from edge” matches the intended geometry (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



void setBarThickness(
    int pixels
)
Stroke width of the main horizontal bar (stroke-width on the bar <line>).
Parameters:

pixels Thickness in pixels.

Precondition: pixels > 0 for a visible bar stroke (enforcement: none) [LOW]



void setTickHeight(
    int pixels
)
Total extent of each end tick along the axis perpendicular to the bar (pixels).
Parameters:

pixels Tick height (half above and half below the bar centerline).

Precondition: pixels >= 0 for non-inverted tick geometry (enforcement: none) [LOW]



void setLabelFontSize(
    int pixels
)
Font size for the numeric label (font-size on the <text> element).
Parameters:

pixels Size in pixels.

Precondition: pixels > 0 for readable text (enforcement: none) [LOW]



void setStrokeColor(
    std::string hex
)
Stroke color for the bar and ticks (SVG stroke attribute value).
Parameters:

hex Color string (e.g. #000000); invalid values yield invalid SVG (enforcement: none) [LOW]




void setLabelFillColor(
    std::string hex
)
Fill color for the numeric label (SVG fill attribute value).
Parameters:

hex Color string (e.g. #000000); invalid values yield invalid SVG (enforcement: none) [LOW]




virtual std::vector< std::string > render(
    int canvas_width,
    int canvas_height
) const override
Emit the bar, two end ticks, and centered numeric label as SVG element strings.
Parameters:

canvas_width SVG viewport width in pixels.
canvas_height SVG viewport height in pixels.

Precondition:

canvas_width > 0 and canvas_height > 0 for non-empty output (enforcement: runtime_check)
time_range_end - time_range_start must be finite and strictly positive for non-empty output (enforcement: runtime_check)
Layout is not clipped by the implementation: very large bar length in pixels or negative padding may draw outside the viewBox (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns an empty vector if canvas_width, canvas_height, or the stored time span fail the runtime checks above.
Otherwise returns exactly four strings: main bar <line>, left tick <line>, right tick <line>, and label <text> (decimal text is scalebar_length).
Does not throw.

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::Examples::LineSubsegmentParams;
Parameters for line subsegment extraction.
This transform extracts a subsegment from a line between two fractional positions along its arc length. Two methods are available:

Direct: Extracts points directly from the line, optionally preserving original spacing
Parametric: Fits a parametric polynomial and resamples the subsegment uniformly

Example JSON: ```json
{ “start_position”: 0.2, “end_position”: 0.8, “method”: “Direct”, “polynomial_order”: 3, “output_points”: 50, “preserve_original_spacing”: true }

class dl::Point2DEncoder;
Encodes Point2D data into a tensor channel.
Supported modes:

Binary: Sets 1.0 at the nearest pixel for each point
Heatmap: Places a 2D Gaussian centered on each point

Points are scaled from source ImageSize to the tensor’s (H, W).





virtual std::string name() const override
Human-readable name for UI / registry.
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::name



virtual std::string inputTypeName() const override
Which geometry type this encoder expects (e.g. “Point2D”, “Mask2D”).
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::inputTypeName



static void encode(
    Point2D< float > point,
    ImageSize source_size,
    at::Tensor & tensor,
    EncoderContext const & ctx,
    Point2DEncoderParams const & params
)
Encode a single point into tensor[batch_index, target_channel, :, :].
Parameters:

point Point in source image coordinate space
source_size Spatial dimensions of the source image used to scale the point into tensor space
tensor Pre-allocated [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor to write into
ctx Encoder context (batch_index, target_channel, height, width)
params User-configurable encoding parameters (mode, gaussian_sigma)

Precondition:

params.mode == Binary or params.mode == Heatmap (enforcement: exception)
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; zero causes floating-point division by zero producing a +Inf scale factor, which makes static_cast of the resulting Inf undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; negative values (e.g. the ImageSize default -1) produce a negative scale factor, mapping points to mirrored coordinates (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor with at least 4 dimensions; fewer dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access when indexing tensor[batch_index][target_channel] (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0 and ctx.target_channel < tensor.size(1); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height == tensor.size(2) and ctx.width == tensor.size(3); if either ctx dimension exceeds the actual tensor spatial dimension the channel write is out-of-bounds (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero causes std::clamp to receive an upper bound of -1 which is less than the lower bound of 0, invoking undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params.gaussian_sigma > 0 when mode == Heatmap; zero causes floating-point division by zero in the Gaussian weight computation, producing NaN at the centre pixel (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
point.x and point.y are finite; NaN coordinates cause round() to return an unspecified value and static_cast of NaN is undefined behaviour in Binary mode; in Heatmap mode the bounding-box calculations also invoke UB (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]




static void encode(
    std::vector< Point2D< float > > const & points,
    ImageSize source_size,
    at::Tensor & tensor,
    EncoderContext const & ctx,
    Point2DEncoderParams const & params
)
Encode multiple points into tensor[batch_index, target_channel, :, :].
Parameters:

points Points in source image coordinate space
source_size Spatial dimensions of the source image used to scale points into tensor space
tensor Pre-allocated [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor to write into
ctx Encoder context (batch_index, target_channel, height, width)
params User-configurable encoding parameters (mode, gaussian_sigma)

Precondition:

params.mode == Binary or params.mode == Heatmap (enforcement: exception)
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; zero causes floating-point division by zero producing a +Inf scale factor, which makes static_cast of the resulting Inf undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; negative values (e.g. the ImageSize default -1) produce a negative scale factor, mapping points to mirrored coordinates (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor with at least 4 dimensions; fewer dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access when indexing tensor[batch_index][target_channel] (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0 and ctx.target_channel < tensor.size(1); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height == tensor.size(2) and ctx.width == tensor.size(3); if either ctx dimension exceeds the actual tensor spatial dimension the channel write is out-of-bounds (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero causes std::clamp to receive an upper bound of -1 which is less than the lower bound of 0, invoking undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params.gaussian_sigma > 0 when mode == Heatmap; zero causes floating-point division by zero in the Gaussian weight computation, producing NaN at centre pixels (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
each element of points has finite x and y; NaN coordinates invoke undefined behaviour in the pixel-coordinate computation for both Binary and Heatmap modes (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

An empty points vector is a safe no-op. When multiple points map to the same pixel in Binary mode the pixel is simply set to 1.0; in Heatmap mode the maximum Gaussian value across all points is retained.

tensor Pre-allocated [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor to write into
ctx Encoder context (batch_index, target_channel, height, width)
params User-configurable encoding parameters (mode, gaussian_sigma)

Precondition:

params.mode == Binary or params.mode == Heatmap (enforcement: exception)
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; zero causes floating-point division by zero producing a +Inf scale factor, which makes static_cast of the resulting Inf undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; negative values (e.g. the ImageSize default -1) produce a negative scale factor, mapping points to mirrored coordinates (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor with at least 4 dimensions; fewer dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access when indexing tensor[batch_index][target_channel] (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0 and ctx.target_channel < tensor.size(1); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height == tensor.size(2) and ctx.width == tensor.size(3); if either ctx dimension exceeds the actual tensor spatial dimension the channel write is out-of-bounds (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero causes std::clamp to receive an upper bound of -1 which is less than the lower bound of 0, invoking undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params.gaussian_sigma > 0 when mode == Heatmap; zero causes floating-point division by zero in the Gaussian weight computation, producing NaN at the centre pixel (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
point.x and point.y are finite; NaN coordinates cause round() to return an unspecified value and static_cast of NaN is undefined behaviour in Binary mode; in Heatmap mode the bounding-box calculations also invoke UB (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Lazy view-based analog data storage.
Template Parameters:

ViewType Type of the random-access range view.

Stores a computation pipeline as a random-access view that transforms data on-demand. Enables efficient composition of transforms without materializing intermediate results. Works with any random-access range that yields values compatible with [AnalogTimeSeries::TimeValuePoint](/api_generated/Classes/structAnalogTimeSeries_1_1TimeValuePoint.md) or ([TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md), float) pairs (the value accessor is inferred).

struct Neuralyzer::TensorBuilders::ColumnRecipe;
Describes how one tensor column is computed.
A ColumnRecipe captures all the information needed to build a ColumnProviderFn closure. It is JSON-serializable (via reflect-cpp) for save/load of TensorDesigner configurations.
The recipe does NOT store the closure itself — closures capture runtime pointers (DataManager*, shared_ptrs) that are not serializable. Use buildProviderFromRecipe() to reconstruct the closure at runtime.

class PlottingSVG::SVGSceneRenderer;
Orchestrates [SVGDocument](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md) assembly, per-batch SVG renderers, and optional decorations.
Scene geometry is grouped into fixed layer ids: rectangles, polylines, and glyphs (batches are appended in scene vector order within each layer). Non-empty decoration output is added as layer decorations. If no scene is set, or the scene pointer is null at [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render) time, the document still contains the default [SVGDocument](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md) metadata and background, with no scene geometry layers.





SVGSceneRenderer()
Construct a renderer with default canvas size (1920×1080), white background, and no scene.



void setScene(
    CorePlotting::RenderableScene const & scene
)
Bind the scene whose batches and view/projection matrices are exported on [render()]().
Precondition:

scene must remain valid (not destroyed) for every subsequent call to [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render) or [renderToFile()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-rendertofile) while this pointer is still stored (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
scene.view_matrix and scene.projection_matrix should reflect the intended camera transform (enforcement: none — identity produces valid but usually incorrect output) [IMPORTANT]

The renderer reads scene.view_matrix and scene.projection_matrix at [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render) time to compute the final MVP (projection * view * batch.model_matrix) for every batch. Callers must ensure these matrices reflect the desired camera state before calling [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render). The RenderableScene defaults are identity, which maps world coordinates directly to NDC — this is almost never the correct camera for a plot widget. Typically the caller copies the same view/projection matrices used by the live OpenGL renderer onto the scene before exporting.



void setCanvasSize(
    int width,
    int height
)
Set the pixel width and height used for the root <svg>, viewBox, and all renderers.
Precondition: width > 0 and height > 0 for a conventional canvas and correct NDC→pixel mapping in batch renderers (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



void setBackgroundColor(
    std::string const & hex_color

void setScene(
    CorePlotting::RenderableScene const & scene
)
Bind the scene whose batches and view/projection matrices are exported on [render()]().
Precondition:

scene must remain valid (not destroyed) for every subsequent call to [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render) or [renderToFile()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-rendertofile) while this pointer is still stored (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
scene.view_matrix and scene.projection_matrix should reflect the intended camera transform (enforcement: none — identity produces valid but usually incorrect output) [IMPORTANT]

The renderer reads scene.view_matrix and scene.projection_matrix at [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render) time to compute the final MVP (projection * view * batch.model_matrix) for every batch. Callers must ensure these matrices reflect the desired camera state before calling [render()](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGSceneRenderer.md#function-render). The RenderableScene defaults are identity, which maps world coordinates directly to NDC — this is almost never the correct camera for a plot widget. Typically the caller copies the same view/projection matrices used by the live OpenGL renderer onto the scene before exporting.

template <typename ViewType >
class LazyDigitalEventStorage;
Lazy digital event storage that computes events on-demand from a view.
Template Parameters:

ViewType Type of the random-access range view.

Stores a computation pipeline as a random-access view that transforms data on-demand. Enables efficient composition of transforms without materializing intermediate results.
The view must yield objects with .event_time and .entity_id members (or first/second for pair-like types).

class GroupingTransformParametersBase;
Base class for transform parameters that need access to the EntityGroupManager.
This extends the basic TransformParametersBase to provide access to the group management system for operations that modify entity groups rather than creating new data.
The EntityGroupManager can be null initially and set later via setGroupManager(). This allows getDefaultParameters() to return actual parameter objects while still requiring the group manager to be set before execution.

title: LazyColumnTensorStorage
LazyColumnTensorStorage
text:
Key properties

Shape is always 2D: [num_rows, num_columns]
Not contiguous: [flatData()](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-flatdata) throws (no single contiguous buffer). Use [materializeAll()](/api_generated/Classes/classLazyColumnTensorStorage.md#function-materializeall) + flatCache() or [getColumn()](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-getcolumn) for access.
Per-column caching: each column is materialized independently.
Per-column invalidation: invalidateColumn(col) clears one cache; [invalidateAll()](/api_generated/Classes/classLazyColumnTensorStorage.md#function-invalidateall) clears all.
Thread safety: column materialization is guarded by a mutex so that concurrent reads don’t race on cache population. The mutex is per-storage, not per-column, for simplicity.

title: LazyColumnTensorStorage
text:
Relationship to other storages

[ArmadilloTensorStorage](/api_generated/Classes/classArmadilloTensorStorage.md) / [DenseTensorStorage](/api_generated/Classes/classDenseTensorStorage.md): owned, contiguous data.
ViewTensorStorage: zero-copy slice of another storage.
[LazyColumnTensorStorage](/api_generated/Classes/classLazyColumnTensorStorage.md): each column computed on demand, cached.

Mixed materialized + lazy columns: a “materialized” column is just a provider that returns fixed data (called once, cached forever if never invalidated).

This model presents HDF5 dataset data in a table format:

1D datasets: Single column with index as row
2D datasets: Rows and columns map directly

Data is loaded in chunks (default 100 rows) and cached using QCache to provide smooth scrolling while minimizing memory usage.

class PreReductionPanel;
Collapsible panel for managing pre-reduction steps.
Pre-reductions are computed over the entire input data range before the main pipeline executes. The results are stored in a value store and can be referenced via param_bindings in pipeline steps.
Example: ZScoreNormalizeV2 requires “mean” and “stddev” pre-reductions.

void _saveLaneLayout()
Save the current lane layout (displayed series + overrides) to a JSON file.
Opens a file dialog for the user to choose a destination. Writes all currently-displayed series with their colors and all lane-placement overrides to a .json file that can be restored with _loadLaneLayout().



void _loadLaneLayout()
Load a previously saved lane layout from a JSON file.
Opens a file dialog for the user to select a .json file produced by _saveLaneLayout(). Series listed in the file that exist in the DataManager but are not currently displayed are automatically added. Series absent from the DataManager are silently skipped.



void _loadLaneLayoutFromText(
    QString const & text
)
Load a lane layout profile from JSON text.
Parameters:

text Raw lane layout profile JSON

Applies the same profile logic as _loadLaneLayout without opening a file dialog. Series absent from the DataManager are skipped.



void _loadSpikeToAnalogPairing()
Load spike-to-analog pairing CSV via a file dialog and apply placement overrides.
Opens [SpikeToAnalogConfigDialog](/api_generated/Classes/classSpikeToAnalogConfigDialog.md) to collect all parse options, group prefixes, placement mode, and CSV file path, then reads the file and delegates to _applyAnalogPairing.



void _loadSpikeToAnalogPairingFromText(
    QString const & digital_group,
    QString const & analog_group,
    QString const & text,
    int placement_mode
)
Parse spike-to-analog CSV text and apply lane placement overrides.
Parameters:

digital_group Group prefix for digital spike series (e.g. “spikes_”)
analog_group Group prefix for analog LFP series (e.g. “voltage_”)
text Raw CSV content
placement_mode Cast of SpikeToAnalogPlacementMode to int

Uses the default [SpikeToAnalogParseConfig](/api_generated/Classes/structSpikeToAnalogParseConfig.md) (comma delimiter, columns 2 and 3, 1-based indexing). Exposed as a named slot so that unit tests can invoke it via QMetaObject::invokeMethod without needing to pass a parse config.



void _handleSeriesRelativePlacement(
    QString const & source_key,
    QString const & target_key,
    bool above
)
Handle a relative placement request from the properties widget context menu.
Parameters:

source_key Series key to reposition
target_key Series key to place relative to
above true = place source above target, false = place below

Places source_key immediately above or below target_key in the visual lane stack by writing deterministic lane_order overrides to DataViewerState.

MLCore::MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation
text:
Workflow

op->fitTransform(features, labels, params, result);  // fit + project in one call
op->transform(new_features, result);                 // project new unlabeled data
auto names = op->outputColumnNames();                // "Logit:0", "Logit:1", ...
All matrices use mlpack convention: (features × observations) — each column is one observation. The output result has [outputDimensions()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation.md#function-outputdimensions) rows and the same number of columns as the input.
[transform()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation.md#function-transform) requires a prior call to [fitTransform()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation.md#function-fittransform). It uses the fitted weight matrix directly and does not require labels.

function fitTransform
virtual bool fitTransform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params,
    arma::mat & result
) =0
Fit the model on labeled data and project to reduced space.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (D × N) in mlpack convention
labels Label row vector (N,) with class indices in [0, C)
params Algorithm-specific parameters
result Output: reduced matrix (C × N) — one row per class logit

Return: true on success
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
labels.n_elem must equal features.n_cols (enforcement: runtime_check)
At least 2 distinct classes must appear in labels (enforcement: runtime_check)
params must be of the correct concrete type for this operation (enforcement: none)
Features are expected to be z-score normalized (mean≈0, std≈1 per feature) when scale-sensitive comparison across features is desired. Normalization is the caller’s responsibility (via FeatureConverter). Centering is handled internally by each algorithm. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

isTrained() returns true on success
result has outputDimensions() rows and features.n_cols columns

Reimplemented by: MLCore::LARSProjectionOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::LogitProjectionOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::SupervisedPCAOperation::fitTransform, MLCore::SupervisedRobustPCAOperation::fitTransform


function transform
virtual bool transform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::mat & result
) =0
Project new unlabeled data using the fitted weight matrix.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (D × N) — must have same D as training data
result Output: reduced matrix (C × N)

Return: true on success, false if model not fitted or dimension mismatch
Precondition:

isTrained() must be true (enforcement: runtime_check)
features.n_rows must equal numFeatures() (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features must be z-score normalized using the SAME parameters (mean/std) that were used for the training data passed to fitTransform(). Use FeatureConverter::applyZscoreNormalization() with stored parameters. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

function requiresAllClassesForFitting
inline virtual bool requiresAllClassesForFitting() const
Whether the model requires all class labels for fitting.
Reimplemented by: MLCore::SupervisedPCAOperation::requiresAllClassesForFitting, MLCore::SupervisedRobustPCAOperation::requiresAllClassesForFitting
Discriminative models (e.g. LogitProjection) need samples from every class to learn a decision boundary ⇒ return true (the default).
Non-discriminative models (e.g. SupervisedPCA) only need the “positive” class subset to fit a projection ⇒ return false. The pipeline uses this flag to subset to only the positive class (label > 0) when all rows already carry a label (e.g. interval-based labeling).

class PointParticleFilterOperation;
Transform operation for tracking points through masks with particle filter.
This operation applies a discrete particle filter to track sparse point labels through mask data. The filter:

Uses existing point labels as ground truth anchors
Fills in missing frames between ground truth labels
Constrains particle states to mask pixels only
Performs forward filtering and backward smoothing for each segment

Points are organized by group ID, and each group is tracked independently.

text:
class PointParticleFilterOperation;
Transform operation for tracking points through masks with particle filter.
This operation applies a discrete particle filter to track sparse point labels through mask data. The filter:

Uses existing point labels as ground truth anchors
Fills in missing frames between ground truth labels
Constrains particle states to mask pixels only
Performs forward filtering and backward smoothing for each segment

Points are organized by group ID, and each group is tracked independently.

title: ScatterAxisSource
text:
struct ScatterAxisSource;
Describes a single axis data source (X or Y) for a scatter plot.
The data_key references a DataManager entry, which must be either an [AnalogTimeSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classAnalogTimeSeries.md) or a [TensorData](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorData.md). When the key points to [TensorData](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorData.md), tensor_column_name (preferred) or tensor_column_index selects the column to use. Both may be set; the name takes priority when resolving.
time_offset shifts the lookup index by the given number of [TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md) steps, enabling lag-plots (\(x(t)\) vs \(x(t-1)\)).

class BinaryFormatLoader;
Format-centric binary loader for all binary file data types.
This loader follows the format-centric architecture where one loader handles a specific file format (binary) for all applicable data types.
Supported data types:

DM_DataType::Analog: Multi-channel analog time series (int16, float32, etc.)
DM_DataType::DigitalEvent: Digital events extracted from TTL channels
DM_DataType::DigitalInterval: Digital intervals extracted from TTL channels

This loader supports batch loading for multi-channel binary files, returning all channels in a single loadBatch() call.
Configuration options vary by data type - see individual load methods for required and optional JSON configuration fields.

    DM_DataType dataType,

Load a single data object from binary file.
Reimplements: IFormatLoader::load
For multi-channel binary files (Analog with num_channels > 1), this returns only the first channel. Use loadBatch() for all channels.

    DM_DataType dataType
) const override
Check if batch loading is supported for this format/type.

class TimestampValueComputer;
Computer for extracting values from analog sources at specific timestamps.
Source type: IAnalogSource Selector type: Timestamp Output type: double
This computer works with timestamp-based row selectors (TimestampSelector) and extracts single values from an analog source at each specified timestamp. It’s designed for cases where you want to sample analog data at specific time points rather than computing statistics over intervals.
The computer takes an analog source and returns a vector of values corresponding to the timestamps defined by the row selector. Each value represents the analog signal value at that specific timestamp.

struct CorePlotting::Interaction::GlyphPreview;
Preview geometry for rendering during interactive glyph creation/modification.
See:

IGlyphInteractionController for the source of preview data
PlottingOpenGL::PreviewRenderer for rendering

This struct holds the geometric state of an interaction in canvas coordinates (pixels). It is produced by IGlyphInteractionController::getPreview() and consumed by PlottingOpenGL::PreviewRenderer.
Coordinate System: All positions are in canvas pixels with:

Origin at top-left corner of the viewport
X increasing rightward
Y increasing downward

Supported Primitive Types:

Point: Single position (for placing markers)
Line: Two endpoints (for line selection/annotation)
Rectangle: Position + size (for intervals, selection boxes)
Polygon: Arbitrary vertex list (for freeform regions)

Modification Mode: When modifying an existing element (vs creating new), the “original” fields contain the element’s position before modification, allowing the renderer to show a “ghost” of the original alongside the new position.

struct CorePlotting::Interaction::GlyphPreview;
Preview geometry for rendering during interactive glyph creation/modification.
See:

IGlyphInteractionController for the source of preview data
PlottingOpenGL::PreviewRenderer for rendering

This struct holds the geometric state of an interaction in canvas coordinates (pixels). It is produced by IGlyphInteractionController::getPreview() and consumed by PlottingOpenGL::PreviewRenderer.
Coordinate System: All positions are in canvas pixels with:

Origin at top-left corner of the viewport
X increasing rightward
Y increasing downward

Supported Primitive Types:

Point: Single position (for placing markers)
Line: Two endpoints (for line selection/annotation)
Rectangle: Position + size (for intervals, selection boxes)
Polygon: Arbitrary vertex list (for freeform regions)

Modification Mode: When modifying an existing element (vs creating new), the “original” fields contain the element’s position before modification, allowing the renderer to show a “ghost” of the original alongside the new position.

template <typename T >
class IntervalOverlapComputer;
Templated computer for analyzing overlaps between row intervals and column intervals.
Source type: IIntervalSource Selector type: Interval Output type: T
This computer works with two sets of intervals: the row intervals (from the ExecutionPlan) and the column intervals (from an IIntervalSource). It can perform different operations to analyze their relationships:

AssignID: For each row interval, finds the index of the column interval that contains it
CountOverlaps: For each row interval, counts how many column intervals overlap with it

The template parameter T determines the return type:

IntervalOverlapOperation::AssignID requires T = int64_t (returns -1 if no overlap)
IntervalOverlapOperation::CountOverlaps requires T = int64_t or size_t

struct LineKalmanGroupingParameters;
Parameters for the line Kalman grouping operation.
This operation uses Kalman filtering and smoothing to track multiple line features across time frames and assign ungrouped lines to existing groups using the Hungarian algorithm with Mahalanobis distance.
Features tracked:

Line centroid (center of mass of all points) - KINEMATIC_2D
Line base point (first point in the line) - KINEMATIC_2D
Line length (total arc length) - STATIC

The metadata-driven system automatically handles different temporal behaviors:

Kinematic features: Track position + velocity (2D measurement → 4D state)
Static features: Track value only, no velocity (1D measurement → 1D state)

Total measurement space: 5D (2D + 2D + 1D) Total state space: 9D (4D + 4D + 1D)

title: LineKalmanGroupingParameters
text:
struct LineKalmanGroupingParameters;
Parameters for the line Kalman grouping operation.
This operation uses Kalman filtering and smoothing to track multiple line features across time frames and assign ungrouped lines to existing groups using the Hungarian algorithm with Mahalanobis distance.
Features tracked:

Line centroid (center of mass of all points) - KINEMATIC_2D
Line base point (first point in the line) - KINEMATIC_2D
Line length (total arc length) - STATIC

The metadata-driven system automatically handles different temporal behaviors:

Kinematic features: Track position + velocity (2D measurement → 4D state)
Static features: Track value only, no velocity (1D measurement → 1D state)

Total measurement space: 5D (2D + 2D + 1D) Total state space: 9D (4D + 4D + 1D)

struct Neuralyzer::TensorDesign::ColumnRecipe;
Describes how one tensor column is computed.
A ColumnRecipe captures all the information needed to build a ColumnProviderFn closure. It is JSON-serializable (via reflect-cpp) for save/load of TensorDesigner configurations.
The recipe does NOT store the closure itself — closures capture runtime pointers (DataManager*, shared_ptrs) that are not serializable. Use buildProviderFromRecipe() to reconstruct the closure at runtime.

class dl::Line2DEncoder;
Encodes a Line2D (ordered polyline) into a tensor channel.
Supported modes:

Binary: Rasterizes the polyline using Bresenham-style line drawing
Heatmap: Rasterizes the polyline with Gaussian blur along the line

Line point coordinates are scaled from source ImageSize to (H, W).





virtual std::string name() const override
Human-readable name for UI / registry.
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::name



virtual std::string inputTypeName() const override
Which geometry type this encoder expects (e.g. “Point2D”, “Mask2D”).
Reimplements: dl::ChannelEncoder::inputTypeName



static void encode(
    Line2D const & line,
    ImageSize source_size,
    at::Tensor & tensor,
    EncoderContext const & ctx,
    Line2DEncoderParams const & params
)
Encode a polyline into tensor[batch_index, target_channel, :, :].
Parameters:

line Ordered polyline in source image coordinate space
source_size Spatial dimensions of the source image used to scale line coordinates into tensor space
tensor Pre-allocated [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor to write into
ctx Encoder context (batch_index, target_channel, height, width)
params User-configurable encoding parameters (mode, gaussian_sigma)

Precondition:

params.mode == Binary or params.mode == Heatmap (enforcement: exception)
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; zero causes floating-point division by zero in coordinate scaling producing +Inf scaled coordinates (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
source_size.width > 0 and source_size.height > 0; negative values (e.g. the ImageSize default -1) invert the scale factor, producing garbage coordinates (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] float32 tensor with at least 4 dimensions; fewer dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access when indexing tensor[batch_index][target_channel] (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0 and ctx.target_channel < tensor.size(1); an out-of-range value causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height == tensor.size(2) and ctx.width == tensor.size(3); if ctx.height or ctx.width exceeds the actual tensor spatial dimension the Bresenham clamp limit exceeds the accessor bound, causing an out-of-bounds accessor write (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero causes std::clamp to receive an upper bound of -1 which is less than the lower bound of 0, invoking undefined behaviour (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params.gaussian_sigma > 0 when mode == Heatmap; zero sigma causes floating-point division by zero in the Gaussian weight computation, producing +Inf weights and NaN output for pixels exactly on the line (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Lines with fewer than 2 points produce no output (no-op early return). Point coordinates outside the source image bounds are clamped to the tensor edges in Binary mode; in Heatmap mode they are handled naturally by the bounding-box loop and clamping.

class DataKeyFrameFilter;
Frame filter backed by a [DigitalIntervalSeries](/api_generated/Classes/classDigitalIntervalSeries.md) key in [DataManager](/api_generated/Classes/classDataManager.md).
When skip_tracked is true (the default), frames whose index falls inside any interval of the series are skipped. Setting skip_tracked to false inverts the behaviour: frames outside all intervals are skipped, which can be used to confine playback to annotated regions.
The filter is dynamic: it re-fetches the series on every call to [shouldSkip()](/api_generated/Classes/classDataKeyFrameFilter.md#function-shouldskip), so changes made by hotkeys (Phase 2) are reflected immediately during playback without needing to rebuild the filter.

Tensor storage backend using Armadillo (arma::fvec, arma::fmat, arma::fcube).
This is the default storage backend for tensors with ≤3 dimensions. Armadillo is a required project dependency, so this backend is always available.
Wraps arma::fvec (1D), arma::fmat (2D), or arma::fcube (3D) and provides:

Efficient column extraction leveraging Armadillo’s native col() access

Tensor storage backend using Armadillo (arma::fvec, arma::fmat, arma::fcube).
This is the default storage backend for tensors with ≤3 dimensions. Armadillo is a required project dependency, so this backend is always available.
Wraps arma::fvec (1D), arma::fmat (2D), or arma::fcube (3D) and provides:

title: ArmadilloTensorStorage
text:
Layout note
Armadillo uses column-major storage. This class presents row-major semantics to consumers through the TensorStorageBase interface:

[flatData()](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-flatdata) returns data in Armadillo’s native column-major layout (consumers needing row-major should use [getValueAt()](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-getvalueat) or [getColumn()](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-getcolumn))
[getValueAt](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageBase.md#function-getvalueat)({r, c}) on a matrix accesses row r, column c regardless of internal layout
getColumn(c) efficiently extracts column c using Armadillo’s native col()

For zero-copy Armadillo access (e.g., passing to mlpack), use [matrix()](/api_generated/Classes/classArmadilloTensorStorage.md#function-matrix) or [cube()](/api_generated/Classes/classArmadilloTensorStorage.md#function-cube) directly — these return const references to the underlying Armadillo objects with no translation.

title: StateEstimation::MaskPointTracker
StateEstimation::MaskPointTracker
text:
IMPORTANT STATE MODEL LIMITATIONS:
This is a POSITION-ONLY particle filter with NO VELOCITY component in the state.
Each particle represents only a 2D position (x, y) on the mask. There is no tracking of velocity, momentum, or direction of motion. The state transition model is a MEMORYLESS random walk on mask pixels:

With probability (1 - random_walk_prob):

Sample uniformly from pixels within transition_radius of current position
This creates local, short-range transitions

With probability random_walk_prob:

Sample uniformly from ALL mask pixels (with distance penalty)
This allows exploration and recovery from tracking failures

title: StateEstimation::MaskPointTracker
text:
CONSEQUENCES OF NO VELOCITY MODEL:
• Particles have no “momentum” or preferred direction of motion • Over long gaps between labels, particles spread out randomly across the mask • Backward smoothing selects based on proximity to next frame, not trajectory smoothness • This can cause JUMPS at label boundaries when the best particle isn’t actually following a smooth path • The filter cannot predict where the point is “heading” - it only knows where it was

title: StateEstimation::MaskPointTracker
text:
WHEN JUMPS OCCUR:
Large jumps between frames happen when:

Gap between ground truth labels is large (many frames)
Mask topology allows particles to explore distant regions
Random walk allows particles to “teleport” across the mask
Backward smoothing picks a particle that’s close spatially but came from a different trajectory

title: StateEstimation::MaskPointTracker
text:
POTENTIAL IMPROVEMENTS:
To reduce jumps, consider: • Add velocity to particle state: Particle { position, velocity } • Use velocity in transition: new_position = position + velocity + noise • Track trajectory smoothness during backward smoothing • Penalize sudden direction changes in the backward pass • Use a constant-velocity Kalman filter for comparison
However, velocity models increase state dimensionality and may not work well when motion is highly constrained by mask topology or when the point genuinely changes direction rapidly.

Source type: IAnalogSource Selector type: Timestamp Output type: double

The computer calculates the mean and standard deviation of the entire source column, then applies the standardization formula element-wise.
This computer demonstrates column-to-column dependency handling, where the output depends on the materialized data of another column rather than directly on a data source.

ExecuTorch inference backend — loads .pte programs.
Note: ExecuTorch operates on CPU only in the default configuration. Input tensors are converted to contiguous CPU tensors before execution.

This backend is optional and only available when the project is built with ENABLE_EXECUTORCH=ON. It is designed for edge/mobile deployment scenarios.

class dl::ExecuTorchBackend;
ExecuTorch inference backend — loads .pte programs.
Note: ExecuTorch operates on CPU only in the default configuration. Input tensors are converted to contiguous CPU tensors before execution.
This backend wraps the ExecuTorch C++ runtime to load and execute ExecuTorch programs. It bridges between libtorch at::Tensor and ExecuTorch’s EValue execution API.
This backend is optional and only available when the project is built with ENABLE_EXECUTORCH=ON. It is designed for edge/mobile deployment scenarios.

tensor is a valid initialized [B, C, H, W] tensor with at least 4 dimensions; missing dimensions cause an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.batch_index >= 0 and ctx.batch_index < tensor.size(0); a negative or out-of-range batch index causes an out-of-bounds tensor access (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
ctx.target_channel >= 0; a negative value causes an out-of-bounds channel access inside the tensor write loop (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
ctx.height > 0 and ctx.width > 0; zero spatial target dimensions cause libtorch interpolation to fail (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
tensor.size(2) == ctx.height and tensor.size(3) == ctx.width; a spatial dimension mismatch causes a libtorch shape error on channel assignment (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

std::vector< EntityId > resolveToSource(
    std::string const & data_key,
    TimeFrameIndex time,
    std::size_t local_index =0
) const
Resolve derived element to source EntityIds (single step).
Parameters:

data_key Key of the (possibly derived) container
time TimeFrameIndex of element
local_index For ragged containers, which element at that time (0-indexed)

Return: Vector of source EntityIds (empty if no lineage or not found)
Note:

For Source lineage, returns EntityIds from the container itself
For OneToOneByTime, returns EntityIds from source at same time/index
For AllToOneByTime, returns ALL EntityIds from source at that time

Looks up the lineage for the given data key and returns the EntityIds from the immediate source container that correspond to the given time and local index.



std::vector< EntityId > resolveToRoot(
    std::string const & data_key,
    TimeFrameIndex time,
    std::size_t local_index =0
) const
Resolve all the way to root source containers.
Parameters:

data_key Key of the derived container
time TimeFrameIndex of element
local_index For ragged containers, which element at that time

Return: Vector of root source EntityIds
Traverses the lineage chain until reaching containers with Source lineage. This handles multi-level derivations like: MaskData → AnalogTimeSeries (areas) → DigitalEventSeries (peaks)

class AutoParamWidget;
Generic Qt form widget generated from a ParameterSchema.
This widget reads a ParameterSchema and dynamically creates a form with appropriate Qt widgets for each field. It provides bidirectional JSON ↔︎ UI synchronization.





using AutoParamWidget::PostEditHook =  std::function<std::string(std::string const & json)>;
Callback type for post-edit hooks.
Receives the current JSON from the widget after a user edit. Should return the (possibly modified) JSON. If the returned JSON differs from the input, the widget re-populates itself with the new values (without re-triggering the hook).
Use cases:

Bidirectional derived-field calculation (e.g., alpha/beta ↔︎ min/max)
Clamping or snapping values (e.g., forcing odd kernel sizes)




using AutoParamWidget::FileDialogOpener =  std::function<QString(
            QWidget * parent,
            QString dialog_id,
            QString caption,
            QString filter,
            QString fallback_dir,
            bool pick_directory)>;

fallback_dir Initial directory when no session memory exists

template <typename T >
class BlockingQueue;
A thread-safe, blocking queue for producer-consumer patterns.
Template Parameters:

T The type of items to be stored in the queue.

This queue has a maximum size to prevent excessive memory usage. It is designed to be closed to signal the end of production, allowing consumers to terminate gracefully.





inline explicit BlockingQueue(
    size_t max_size
)
Constructs a blocking queue with a specified maximum size.
Parameters:

max_size The maximum number of items the queue can hold.




inline bool push(
    T && item
)
Pushes an item into the queue, blocking if the queue is full.
Parameters:

item The item to push, moved into the queue.

Return: True if the item was pushed successfully, false if the queue was closed.



inline bool pop(
    T & item
)
Pops an item from the queue, blocking if the queue is empty.
Parameters:

item A reference to store the popped item.

Return: True if an item was popped successfully, false if the queue is empty and has been closed.



inline void close()

struct MLCore::MultiClassMetrics;
Metrics for a multi-class classification problem.
The confusion matrix is stored as an arma::umat of shape (num_classes × num_classes). Entry (i, j) is the count of observations with true class i that were predicted as class j.
Per-class precision, recall, and F1 are vectors of size num_classes. When a denominator is zero, the corresponding metric is 0.0.

class TimeIndexStorage;
Abstract base class for time index storage strategies.
TimeIndexStorage provides a mapping from logical array positions (0, 1, 2, …) to TimeFrameIndex values. Different implementations can optimize storage based on data characteristics (dense/consecutive vs sparse/irregular sampling).
This abstraction allows multiple data series to share the same time base (e.g., multi-channel electrophysiology recordings) and supports future extensions like memory-mapped or calculated time indices.

class RelativeOwningDigitalEventStorage;
Immutable owning storage for trial-relative digital event times.
Stores event data in parallel vectors for cache-friendly access:

_events[i] - relative ClockTicks for event i (sorted)

Constructed once from caller-provided vectors; no mutation API is provided. Does not require an associated TimeFrame.

class MLCore::MLModelOperation;
Abstract base for all ML model operations.
A model operation encapsulates a single ML algorithm. It can be trained (supervised) or fit (unsupervised), then used for prediction or cluster assignment. Each operation declares its task type so the registry can categorize it.

function train
inline virtual bool train(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params
)
Train the model on labeled data.
Parameters:

features Feature matrix (features × observations). Each column is one observation with features.n_rows feature values.
labels Label row vector (1 × observations). Each element is a class index in [0, num_classes).
params Algorithm-specific parameters. May be nullptr to use defaults. Must be castable to the concrete parameter type expected by this model.

Return: true if training succeeded
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
labels.n_elem must equal features.n_cols (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Features are expected to be z-score normalized for scale-sensitive classifiers (Logistic Regression, Softmax Regression). Tree-based methods (Random Forest) are scale-invariant. (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Reimplemented by: MLCore::HiddenMarkovModelOperation::train, MLCore::LogisticRegressionOperation::train, MLCore::MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation::train, MLCore::NaiveBayesOperation::train, MLCore::RandomForestOperation::train, MLCore::SoftmaxRegressionOperation::train
After successful training, [isTrained()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLModelOperation.md#function-istrained) returns true, and [numClasses()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLModelOperation.md#function-numclasses) and [numFeatures()](/api_generated/Classes/classMLCore_1_1MLModelOperation.md#function-numfeatures) reflect the training data dimensions.
The default implementation returns false (unsupervised models).

class OwningDigitalEventStorage;
Owning digital event storage using Structure of Arrays layout.
Stores event data in parallel vectors for cache-friendly access:

_events[i] - TimeFrameIndex for event i (sorted)
_entity_ids[i] - EntityId for event i

Maintains acceleration structures:

Events are always sorted by time
O(log n) lookup by time using binary search
O(1) lookup by EntityId using hash map

class CorePlotting::SceneBuilder;
Helper class for constructing RenderableScene objects.
Provides a fluent interface for building scenes incrementally:

Set bounds (required for spatial indexing of discrete elements)
Add mapped elements using range-based API:

addGlyphs() for discrete points/events
addRectangles() for intervals
addPolyLine()/addPolyLines() for continuous data

Optionally set View/Projection matrices
Call build() to finalize the scene

Example usage with TimeSeriesMapper: ```cpp
using namespace CorePlotting;
RenderableScene scene = SceneBuilder() .setBounds(bounds) .setViewState(view_state) .addGlyphs(“trial1”, TimeSeriesMapper::mapEvents(events1, layout1, tf)) .addGlyphs(“trial2”, TimeSeriesMapper::mapEvents(events2, layout2, tf)) .addRectangles(“intervals”, TimeSeriesMapper::mapIntervals(intervals, layout, tf)) .build();

The builder creates both rendering geometry AND spatial index from the same position data, ensuring they remain synchronized.

struct dl::BatchModeSpec;
JSON-serializable batch mode specification.
Maps to [dl::BatchMode](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespacedl.md#using-batchmode) at runtime. Exactly one of [fixed](/api_generated/Classes/structdl_1_1BatchModeSpec.md#variable-fixed), [dynamic](/api_generated/Classes/structdl_1_1BatchModeSpec.md#variable-dynamic), or [recurrent_only](/api_generated/Classes/structdl_1_1BatchModeSpec.md#variable-recurrent-only) should be set.
JSON examples: ```json
“batch_mode”: { “fixed”: 4 } “batch_mode”: { “dynamic”: { “min”: 1, “max”: 8 } } “batch_mode”: { “recurrent_only”: true }

class Neuralyzer::Plots::PlotTooltipManager;
Manages tooltip lifecycle for plot widgets.
Owns a single-shot QTimer. On each mouse move the timer is restarted. When the timer fires (mouse is “stationary”), the hit-test provider is called. If a hit is found, the content provider generates the tooltip content, which is then displayed.
The manager must be told about panning state so that tooltips are suppressed during drag operations.

Set the full content provider (supports text and pixmap).

Notify the manager of a mouse move.
Parameters:

screen_pos Current screen-space cursor position
is_interacting True if the widget is currently panning/dragging

Call this from the widget’s mouseMoveEvent(). The manager restarts the dwell timer at the new position. If is_interacting is true (e.g. panning or drawing), the timer is suppressed.



void onLeave()
Notify the manager that the mouse left the widget.
Stops the timer and hides any visible tooltip. Call this from leaveEvent().



void hide()
Hide the tooltip immediately.
Useful when the scene changes (rebuild) or the widget starts an interaction that should dismiss the tooltip.

class OutputRedirector;
C++ class exposed to Python to capture sys.stdout / sys.stderr.
An instance is injected as sys.stdout and sys.stderr inside the embedded interpreter. Every [write()](/api_generated/Classes/classOutputRedirector.md#function-write) call appends to an internal buffer that can be drained by C++ after execution completes.
The class satisfies the minimal Python “file-like object” protocol (write, flush, readable, writable, seekable) so that the Python runtime and libraries like traceback accept it without complaint.

class EntityRegistry;
Central registry of session-scoped entity identifiers.
Provides deterministic, session-local mapping between (data_key, kind, time, local_index) tuples and opaque EntityId values. Thread-safe for concurrent access.





EntityId ensureId(
    std::string const & data_key,
    EntityKind kind,
    TimeFrameIndex const & time,
    int local_index
)
Get or create an EntityId for the tuple.
Parameters:

data_key Logical key for the data object (opaque; empty allowed)
kind Entity kind (Point, Line, Event, Interval, Mask, TimeEntity)
time TimeFrameIndex for the entity
local_index Stable 0-based index within that time. For IntervalEntity, this is the interval end time (not a storage index).

Return: EntityId for the tuple; same tuple always returns the same id
Note: Thread-safe
Precondition: local_index >= 0 (enforcement: assert)



std::optional< EntityDescriptor > get(
    EntityId id
) const
Lookup descriptor for an EntityId.
Parameters:

id EntityId to look up (e.g. from ensureId or from group/lineage).

Return: EntityDescriptor if the id was ever produced by ensureId on this registry, otherwise std::nullopt. No preconditions on id; unknown ids return nullopt.
Note: Thread-safe



void rebindKey(
    EntityId id,
    TimeFrameIndex const & time,
    int local_index
)
Rebind an existing EntityId to a new (time, local_index) tuple.
Parameters:

id EntityId previously allocated by ensureId on this registry
time New TimeFrameIndex for the entity
local_index New local_index (interval end for IntervalEntity)

Note: Thread-safe; no-op if id is unknown
Precondition:

local_index >= 0 (enforcement: assert)
id was previously registered via ensureId

Updates both lookup maps so ensureId on the new tuple returns the same id. Used when interval bounds change but the logical entity identity is preserved.



void clear()
Clear all registered entities (session reset).
Note: Thread-safe
