title: Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::DataManagerPipelineExecutor
text:
class Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::DataManagerPipelineExecutor;
Executor that runs V2 pipelines with DataManager integration.
This class bridges the gap between the V2 transform system and DataManager:

Loads pipeline configuration from JSON (V1-compatible format)
Retrieves input data from DataManager using input_key
Executes transforms using V2TransformPipeline
Stores results back to DataManager using output_key

Example usage: ```cpp
DataManager dm; // … populate dm with data …
DataManagerPipelineExecutor executor(&dm); if (executor.loadFromJson(json_config)) { auto result = executor.execute(); if (result.success) { // Results are now in DataManager } }

## Public Functions Documentation

### function DataManagerPipelineExecutor

```cpp
explicit DataManagerPipelineExecutor(
    DataManager * data_manager
)
Construct executor with DataManager pointer.
Parameters:

data_manager Non-owning pointer to the DataManager; the executor stores this pointer but does not take ownership or delete the object.

Precondition:

data_manager must not be null (enforcement: exception)
The DataManager object pointed to by data_manager must remain valid and not be destroyed for the entire lifetime of this executor (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]



bool loadFromJson(
    nlohmann::json const & json_config
)
Load pipeline configuration from JSON object.
Parameters:

json_config JSON value to parse. No structural precondition is imposed by this function — schema validation is performed internally and failure is reported via the return value.

Return: true if the complete configuration was loaded successfully.
Postcondition:

If returns true, getSteps() returns the complete parsed pipeline (enforcement: runtime_check — parseJsonFormat validates all required fields).
If returns false, steps_ may be partially populated (steps before the first failing step are retained). The executor must not be used for execution without a subsequent successful loadFromJson() or clear() call (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Any previously loaded configuration is cleared before parsing begins. Any valid nlohmann::json value is accepted; values that do not conform to the expected schema cause the function to return false rather than throw. All exceptions from parsing are caught internally and result in a false return.



bool loadFromJsonFile(
    std::string const & json_file_path
)
Load pipeline configuration from JSON file.
Parameters:

json_file_path Path to a readable file containing a valid JSON pipeline configuration.

Return: true if the file was opened, parsed, and the pipeline loaded successfully.
Precondition:

json_file_path must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check — empty string causes ifstream::open to fail, triggering the is_open() guard)
The file at json_file_path must exist and be readable by the current process (enforcement: runtime_check — guarded by !file.is_open() early return)
The file content must be valid JSON (enforcement: exception — nlohmann::json parse errors are caught and converted to false return)
The parsed JSON must contain a “steps” array conforming to the pipeline schema (enforcement: runtime_check — propagated from loadFromJson/parseJsonFormat)

Postcondition: If returns false, steps_ may be partially populated (same postcondition as loadFromJson). The executor must not be used for execution without a subsequent successful load or clear() call (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Opens the file at json_file_path, parses its contents as JSON, and delegates to loadFromJson(). Any previously loaded configuration is cleared before parsing begins. All I/O and parse errors are caught internally and result in a false return rather than a throw.



V2PipelineResult execute(
    const V2PipelineProgressCallback & progress_callback =nullptr
)
Execute the loaded pipeline.
Parameters:

progress_callback Optional callable invoked before each step and once on completion. May be null/empty (tested before every call). If provided, must not capture references that may be invalidated during execution (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Return: V2PipelineResult describing overall and per-step outcomes.
Precondition:

A successful loadFromJson() or loadFromJsonFile() call must have completed before calling execute(); executing a partially-loaded pipeline (from a failed load) produces partial or incorrect results (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
The DataManager passed to the constructor must still be valid (enforcement: none — propagated from constructor) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

If steps_ is empty, returns success=true with steps_completed=0 and total_steps=0 (empty pipeline is considered trivially successful).
If progress_callback is provided and steps_ is empty, it is invoked with step_index=-1 (completion sentinel). Callbacks should handle negative step_index values (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Iterates over all enabled steps, delegating each to executeStep(). Steps whose enabled field is explicitly set to false are skipped. All exceptions from individual steps are caught internally; the result struct carries success/failure state and per-step error messages.



V2StepResult executeStep(
    size_t step_index,
    const std::function< void(int)> & progress_callback =nullptr
)
Execute a single step by index.
Parameters:

step_index Zero-based index of the step to execute.
progress_callback Currently unused. Reserved for future per-step progress reporting.

Return: V2StepResult describing success/failure and timing.
Note: The progress_callback parameter is accepted but currently unused — it is never invoked inside this function. Per-step progress reporting is handled by the enclosing execute() call.
Precondition:

step_index must be less than steps_.size() (enforcement: runtime_check — guarded by bounds check returning failure result)
steps_[step_index].input_key must name a key present in the DataManager or in temporary_data_ (for single-input steps) (enforcement: runtime_check — missing key is detected by getInputData() and reported as failure)
steps_[step_index].transform_name must be registered in ElementRegistry (enforcement: runtime_check — unregistered name causes executeTransform() to return nullopt, reported as failure)
The DataManager passed to the constructor must still be valid (enforcement: none — propagated from constructor) [IMPORTANT]
For multi-input steps, all keys in additional_input_keys must also be present in DataManager or temporary_data_ (enforcement: runtime_check — propagated through executeMultiInputStep())

Retrieves the step at step_index, fetches its input data from the DataManager or from temporary storage (outputs of prior steps), runs the registered transform, and stores the result. All errors are returned in the result struct rather than thrown.



std::vector< std::string > validate() const
Validate the loaded pipeline configuration.
Return: Empty vector if the pipeline is valid; otherwise one diagnostic string per error. An empty steps_ vector is considered valid and returns an empty vector.
Precondition: Must be called after a successful loadFromJson() or loadFromJsonFile() to be meaningful. Calling on an empty or partially-loaded pipeline returns the errors for whatever steps_ currently contains (enforcement: none) [LOW]
Postcondition:

Return value is empty if and only if all of the following hold for every step: transform_name is registered in ElementRegistry, and input_key is non-empty (enforcement: runtime_check).
Does not modify any member state; safe to call multiple times (enforcement: static — declared const).

Checks each step against the ElementRegistry and verifies that required fields are non-empty. Does not access the DataManager — input key existence is not verified at this stage (that would require runtime data). Does not throw; always returns a (possibly empty) vector.

Clear the current pipeline configuration.

steps_ is empty (enforcement: static — std::vector::clear() guarantee).

temporary_data_ is empty (enforcement: static — std::unordered_map::clear() guarantee).
data_manager_ is unchanged (enforcement: static — not touched by this function).

template <typename T >
class EventInIntervalComputer;
Templated computer for processing events within time intervals.
Template Parameters:

T The return type for the computation. Must match the operation:
EventOperation::Presence requires T = bool
EventOperation::Count requires T = int
EventOperation::Gather requires T = std::vector
EventOperation::Gather_Center requires T = std::vector

Par: Usage Example:
// Create an event source with spike data
auto spikeSource = std::make_shared<SpikeEventSource>("Neuron1", timeFrame, spikeTimes);

// Create intervals for analysis
std::vector<TimeFrameInterval> intervals = {
    TimeFrameInterval(TimeFrameIndex(0), TimeFrameIndex(10)),  // 0-10ms
    TimeFrameInterval(TimeFrameIndex(10), TimeFrameIndex(20)), // 10-20ms
    TimeFrameInterval(TimeFrameIndex(20), TimeFrameIndex(30))  // 20-30ms
};
ExecutionPlan plan(intervals, timeFrame);

// Check for presence of events in each interval
EventInIntervalComputer<bool> presenceComputer(spikeSource, EventOperation::Presence, "Neuron1");
auto presenceResults = presenceComputer.compute(plan);
// Result: [true, false, true] - events present in intervals 0-10ms and 20-30ms

// Count events in each interval
EventInIntervalComputer<int> countComputer(spikeSource, EventOperation::Count, "Neuron1");
auto countResults = countComputer.compute(plan);
// Result: [3, 0, 2] - 3 events in 0-10ms, 0 in 10-20ms, 2 in 20-30ms

// Gather all events in each interval
EventInIntervalComputer<std::vector<float>> gatherComputer(spikeSource, EventOperation::Gather, "Neuron1");
auto gatherResults = gatherComputer.compute(plan);
// Result: [[1.2, 3.4, 8.9], [], [22.1, 25.7]] - actual event times
Source type: DigitalEventSeries Selector type: Interval Output type: T
This computer analyzes event data from a DigitalEventSeries and performs statistical operations on events that fall within specified time intervals. It supports different analysis modes through the EventOperation enum, each requiring a specific template parameter type.
The computer efficiently processes events using binary search algorithms and handles time frame conversions between source and destination time frames automatically.

plan The execution plan containing interval boundaries and destination time frame. Must contain valid intervals and a non-null time frame.

std::runtime_error if the operation type doesn’t match the template parameter T
std::runtime_error if the source time frame is incompatible with the destination time frame

Return: Vector of computed results for each interval in the same order as the plan. The size of the result vector equals the number of intervals in the plan.
Precondition:

plan contains valid intervals (start <= end for each interval)
plan.getTimeFrame() is not null
The template parameter T matches the operation type:
EventOperation::Presence requires T = bool

EventOperation::Gather requires T = std::vector
EventOperation::Gather_Center requires T = std::vector

Postcondition:

Result vector size equals plan.getIntervals().size()
For Presence operation: each result is true if any events exist in the interval, false otherwise
For Count operation: each result is the number of events in the corresponding interval
For Gather operation: each result is a vector of event times within the interval
For Gather_Center operation: each result is a vector of event times relative to interval center

Computes the actual event times within each interval of the execution plan. Returns a vector of float vectors where each inner vector contains the event times that occurred within the corresponding interval.
This specialization supports two modes:

EventOperation::Gather: Returns absolute event times within each interval
EventOperation::Gather_Center: Returns event times relative to interval center

This is particularly useful for detailed event analysis, spike timing studies, and when the exact timing of events within intervals is required.

class CsvDatasetPreviewModel;
Lazy-loading table model for CSV file preview.
This model presents CSV data in a table format:

Rows correspond to data lines (after skipping header lines)
Columns are determined by splitting the first data line on the delimiter
Column headers come from the first header line (if configured) or are auto-generated

Data is loaded in chunks (default 100 rows) and cached using QCache to provide smooth scrolling while minimizing memory usage.
The model supports line-based random access by pre-scanning the file to build a line offset index on load.

title: TensorStorageWrapper
TensorStorageWrapper
text:
Pattern
Uses the same Sean Parent type-erasure pattern as:

AnalogTimeSeries::DataStorageWrapper (shared_ptr, copyable)
RaggedStorageWrapper (unique_ptr, move-only)

This wrapper uses std::shared_ptr to enable zero-copy view sharing: when a ViewTensorStorage is created from a TensorStorageWrapper, both share ownership of the underlying concept (via the shared_ptr aliasing constructor or direct shared_ptr copy).

title: TensorStorageWrapper
text:
Ownership
The wrapper is copyable (shared ownership via shared_ptr).

Copies share the same underlying storage (cheap, O(1))
This enables ViewTensorStorage to reference the source without worrying about lifetime
For exclusive ownership, create a new storage and wrap it

title: TensorStorageWrapper
text:
Type Recovery
[tryGetAs](/api_generated/Classes/classTensorStorageWrapper.md#function-trygetas)<ConcreteStorage>() uses dynamic_cast on the internal concept/model hierarchy to recover the concrete type. This is the same approach as RaggedStorageWrapper::tryGet() and enables zero-copy backend-specific access (e.g., Armadillo matrix for mlpack, at::Tensor for model inference).

title: TensorStorageWrapper
text:
Thread Safety
Same as the underlying storage. The wrapper itself adds no synchronization. shared_ptr reference counting is thread-safe, but concurrent mutation of the pointee is not.

void loadSpikeToAnalogPairing(
    std::string const & digital_group,
    std::string const & analog_group,
    std::vector< SpikeToAnalogPairing > const & pairings,
    SpikeToAnalogPlacementMode mode,
    SpikeToAnalogParseConfig const & config =SpikeToAnalogParseConfig{},
    bool overlay_render_digital_events_as_boxes =false
)
Apply lane placement overrides based on spike-to-analog pairings.
Parameters:

digital_group Group prefix for digital (spike) series (e.g. “spikes”)
analog_group Group prefix for analog (LFP) series (e.g. “voltage”)
pairings Parsed pairings from parseSpikeToAnalogCSV
mode Lane placement policy
config Parse config; the digital_key_one_based and analog_key_one_based fields control how the numeric suffix in series key names is interpreted when building the channel-to-key lookup maps.
overlay_render_digital_events_as_boxes If true and mode is Overlay, set each affected digital event series’ glyph_shape to Box in state.

Precondition: pairings must not be empty; zero-length pairings are no-ops.
For each pairing in pairings, locates the digital series key (digital_group + “” + (digital_channel + 1)) and the analog series key (analog_group + ”” + (analog_channel + 1)) that are currently registered in the data store.
The placement policy applied is controlled by mode:

AdjacentBelow: the digital series is inserted in its own auto-lane immediately below the analog series’ lane.
AdjacentAbove: the digital series is inserted immediately above.
Overlay: the digital series shares the analog series’ lane_id (with overlay_mode set to Overlay).

The current visual order of all displayed series is read from _multi_lane_axis_state->lanes() to determine insertion positions. New lane_order values are assigned with the same ``(N - i) * 10 formula used throughout the ordering system.

void loadSpikeToAnalogPairing(
    std::string const & digital_group,
    std::string const & analog_group,
    std::vector< SpikeToAnalogPairing > const & pairings,
    SpikeToAnalogPlacementMode mode,
    SpikeToAnalogParseConfig const & config =SpikeToAnalogParseConfig{},
    bool overlay_render_digital_events_as_boxes =false
)
Apply lane placement overrides based on spike-to-analog pairings.
Parameters:

digital_group Group prefix for digital (spike) series (e.g. “spikes”)
analog_group Group prefix for analog (LFP) series (e.g. “voltage”)
pairings Parsed pairings from parseSpikeToAnalogCSV
mode Lane placement policy
config Parse config; the digital_key_one_based and analog_key_one_based fields control how the numeric suffix in series key names is interpreted when building the channel-to-key lookup maps.
overlay_render_digital_events_as_boxes If true and mode is Overlay, set each affected digital event series’ glyph_shape to Box in state.

Precondition: pairings must not be empty; zero-length pairings are no-ops.
For each pairing in pairings, locates the digital series key (digital_group + “” + (digital_channel + 1)) and the analog series key (analog_group + ”” + (analog_channel + 1)) that are currently registered in the data store.
The placement policy applied is controlled by mode:

AdjacentBelow: the digital series is inserted in its own auto-lane immediately below the analog series’ lane.
AdjacentAbove: the digital series is inserted immediately above.
Overlay: the digital series shares the analog series’ lane_id (with overlay_mode set to Overlay).

The current visual order of all displayed series is read from _multi_lane_axis_state->lanes() to determine insertion positions. New lane_order values are assigned with the same ``(N - i) * 10 formula used throughout the ordering system.

class IMultiColumnComputer;
Templated interface for computing multiple output columns in one pass.
A multi-column computer produces N outputs of the same element type T, typically representing closely related measures that should be computed in a single pass for performance.

class DataViewer::AnalogVertexCache;
Ring buffer-based cache for analog series vertices.
Maintains a circular buffer of vertices with tracking of the cached time range. Automatically discards old data when new data is pushed, enabling efficient incremental updates during scrolling.





AnalogVertexCache() =default



void initialize(
    size_t capacity
)
Initialize the cache with a given capacity.
Parameters:

capacity Maximum number of vertices to cache

Recommended capacity is 2-3x the visible window size to allow for smooth scrolling in both directions.



void invalidate()
Clear all cached data and reset state.



inline bool isInitialized() const
Check if the cache has been initialized.



inline bool isValid() const
Check if the cache contains valid data.



inline TimeFrameIndex cachedStart() const
Get the currently cached time range.



inline TimeFrameIndex cachedEnd() const



bool covers(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Check if the requested range is fully covered by the cache.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: true if the entire range is cached
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start (inverted range), the condition start >= m_cached_start && end <= m_cached_end can evaluate to true even though no meaningful range is requested, giving a spurious “covered” result — wrong but harmless as the caller would then skip regeneration and getVerticesForRange() returns empty for an inverted range (enforcement: none) [LOW]
start and end must be in the same time coordinate system as the cached data (series time frame, not master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces wrong coverage decisions (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Returns false when !isValid() or vertices are empty
Returns true only when start >= cachedStart() && end <= cachedEnd()

Returns true only when the cache is valid, non-empty, and the entire interval [start, end) lies within [cachedStart(), cachedEnd()). Returns false (conservatively) when the cache is invalid or empty.
This function is purely computational: no memory allocation, no dereferences, safe to call regardless of cache validity.



bool needsUpdate(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Check if the cache needs updating for a new time range.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: true if vertex generation is required before rendering
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the overlap check end <= m_cached_start may fire incorrectly, causing the function to return true (spurious cache miss) even when data is fully cached — wasted work but no crash or data corruption (enforcement: none) [LOW]
start and end must be in the same time coordinate system as the cached data (series time frame, not master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces wrong update decisions (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Return value is true when !isValid() or vertices are empty
Return value is false only when covers(start, end) would return true

Returns true if:

Cache is invalid or empty
Requested range has no overlap with the cached window (jumped location)
Requested range extends beyond the cached window at either end

Returns false (no update needed) only when the cache is valid and fully covers [start, end).
This function is purely computational: no memory allocation, no dereferences, safe to call regardless of cache validity.



std::vector< MissingRange > getMissingRanges(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Calculate which ranges need to be generated.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: Vector of at most 2 missing sub-ranges
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the no-overlap branch may fire and return an inverted MissingRange (start > end) that will corrupt any downstream call to generateVerticesForRange, prependVertices, or appendVertices (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start and end must be expressed in the same time coordinate system as the indices stored in the cache (i.e., the series time frame, not the master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces geometrically wrong gap ranges (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Return value contains at most 2 entries
If return value has 2 entries, [0].prepend == true and [1].prepend == false
Every returned MissingRange satisfies start <= end when the input satisfies start <= end

Returns 0, 1, or 2 [MissingRange](/api_generated/Classes/structDataViewer_1_1MissingRange.md) entries describing the subranges of [start, end) that are not present in the cache:

0 ranges — fully cached; nothing to generate
1 range, prepend=false — complete cache miss (cache invalid/empty or no overlap); the single entry spans the entire requested window
1 range, prepend=true — left edge missing (scrolling left)
1 range, prepend=false — right edge missing (scrolling right)
2 ranges — both edges missing; first has prepend=true, second has prepend=false

This function is purely computational (no memory allocation beyond the returned vector) and safe to call regardless of cache validity.



void prependVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex requested_start
)
Add vertices to the front of the cache (for scrolling left).
Parameters:

vertices Vertices to prepend (may be empty; call is a no-op if so)
requested_start Start time index of the requested range (inclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If isValid() is true, every element of vertices must have time_idx < cachedStart(); otherwise the buffer becomes unsorted at the join point and binary search in getVerticesForRange() produces wrong results (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty; if capacity is 0, push_front is a no-op yet m_valid is set to true, leaving the cache in an inconsistent state (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty, state is unchanged
If vertices is non-empty and capacity() > 0, isValid() == true
cachedStart() <= old cachedStart() (window expands or stays)
size() <= capacity()

Inserts vertices before all currently cached vertices. Vertices are inserted via push_front in reverse so that the buffer remains sorted by ascending time_idx. If the buffer overflows, the newest vertices at the back are discarded and [cachedEnd()](/api_generated/Classes/classDataViewer_1_1AnalogVertexCache.md#function-cachedend) is narrowed accordingly.
If the cache is currently invalid (empty), this call initialises it using the extent of vertices alone.



void appendVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex requested_end
)
Add vertices to the back of the cache (for scrolling right).
Parameters:

vertices Vertices to append (may be empty; call is a no-op if so)
requested_end End time index of the requested range (exclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If isValid() is true, every element of vertices must have time_idx >= cachedEnd(); otherwise the buffer becomes unsorted at the join point and binary search in getVerticesForRange() produces wrong results (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty; if capacity is 0, push_back is a no-op yet m_valid is set to true and m_cached_end is overwritten with a value derived from vertices, leaving the cache in an inconsistent state (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty, state is unchanged
If vertices is non-empty and capacity() > 0, isValid() == true
cachedEnd() >= old cachedEnd() (window expands or stays)
size() <= capacity()

Inserts vertices after all currently cached vertices via push_back. The circular buffer automatically discards the oldest (front) entries on overflow and [cachedStart()](/api_generated/Classes/classDataViewer_1_1AnalogVertexCache.md#function-cachedstart) is advanced to match.
If the cache is currently invalid (empty), this call initialises it using the extent of vertices alone.



void setVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
)
Replace all cached vertices (for cache misses or initialization).
Parameters:

vertices New vertex data (may be empty, in which case the cache is invalidated)
start Start time index of the data (inclusive)
end End time index of the data (exclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start <= end (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If vertices is non-empty, vertices.front().time_idx >= start (enforcement: none) [LOW]
If vertices is non-empty, vertices.back().time_idx < end (enforcement: none) [LOW]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty, otherwise all data is silently discarded (enforcement: runtime_check)

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty or capacity is 0, isValid() == false
If vertices is non-empty and capacity > 0, isValid() == true
size() <= capacity()
cachedStart() <= cachedEnd()

Clears the cache and loads vertices. If the circular buffer capacity is smaller than vertices.size(), the oldest (front) entries are silently discarded and the cached range is narrowed to match what was actually stored.



std::vector< float > getVerticesForRange(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time
) const
Extract vertices for a specific time range.
Parameters:

start Start of range to extract (inclusive)
end End of range to extract (exclusive)
x_origin_master_absolute_time Absolute physical time at the current view’s left edge (same as AnalogBatchParams::x_origin_master_absolute_time)

Return: Flat vertex array [x0,y0,x1,y1,…], or empty if range not cached
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the reserve() call computes static_cast(negative_int64) * 2, which wraps to near SIZE_MAX and causes std::length_error or std::bad_alloc (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
The buffer must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx; the binary search in findIndexForTime() produces wrong results if the buffer is unsorted (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start >= cachedStart() and end <= cachedEnd() for a non-empty result; requesting a range outside the cached window returns empty (enforcement: runtime_check)

Postcondition:

Return value size is even (pairs of x,y floats)
Return value is empty when cache is invalid or start is not found

Returns a flat float array suitable for GPU upload: [x0, y0, x1, y1, …]. Each output x is [CachedAnalogVertex::x](/api_generated/Classes/structDataViewer_1_1CachedAnalogVertex.md#variable-x) minus x_origin_master_absolute_time (integer-to-double subtraction, then cast to float), matching TimeSeriesMapper view-relative coordinates. y is copied from the cache. Uses binary search to locate start in the buffer, then linearly scans forward until a vertex with time_idx >= end is encountered.
Returns an empty vector (without crashing) when:

The cache is invalid or empty
start is not found in the buffer (beyond the cached range)




void extractVerticesForRange(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time,
    std::vector< float > & out_buffer
) const
Extract vertices for a specific time range into a caller-supplied buffer.
Parameters:

start Start of range to extract (inclusive)
end End of range to extract (exclusive)
x_origin_master_absolute_time Absolute physical time at the current view’s left edge
out_buffer Output buffer to populate in-place

Reuses the capacity of out_buffer (via .clear()), eliminating dynamic heap allocations.



std::vector< float > getVerticesForRangeDecimated(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    int bucket_count,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time
) const
Extract vertices for a specific time range with fast-path min-max decimation.
Parameters:

start Start of range to extract (inclusive)
end End of range to extract (exclusive)
bucket_count Number of temporal buckets to decimate into
x_origin_master_absolute_time Absolute physical time at the current view’s left edge

Return: Flat vertex array [x0,y0,x1,y1,…] of decimated points
Directly downsamples cached vertices into min-max pairs across bucket_count buckets. Avoids intermediate buffer allocations and floating-point bucket hashing.



void extractVerticesForRangeDecimated(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    int bucket_count,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time,
    std::vector< float > & out_buffer
) const

Parameters:

start Start of range to extract (inclusive)

void initialize(
    size_t capacity
)
Initialize the cache with a given capacity.
Parameters:

capacity Maximum number of vertices to cache

Recommended capacity is 2-3x the visible window size to allow for smooth scrolling in both directions.



void invalidate()
Clear all cached data and reset state.



inline bool isInitialized() const
Check if the cache has been initialized.



inline bool isValid() const
Check if the cache contains valid data.



inline TimeFrameIndex cachedStart() const
Get the currently cached time range.



inline TimeFrameIndex cachedEnd() const



bool covers(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Check if the requested range is fully covered by the cache.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: true if the entire range is cached
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start (inverted range), the condition start >= m_cached_start && end <= m_cached_end can evaluate to true even though no meaningful range is requested, giving a spurious “covered” result — wrong but harmless as the caller would then skip regeneration and getVerticesForRange() returns empty for an inverted range (enforcement: none) [LOW]
start and end must be in the same time coordinate system as the cached data (series time frame, not master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces wrong coverage decisions (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Returns false when !isValid() or vertices are empty
Returns true only when start >= cachedStart() && end <= cachedEnd()

Returns true only when the cache is valid, non-empty, and the entire interval [start, end) lies within [cachedStart(), cachedEnd()). Returns false (conservatively) when the cache is invalid or empty.
This function is purely computational: no memory allocation, no dereferences, safe to call regardless of cache validity.



bool needsUpdate(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Check if the cache needs updating for a new time range.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: true if vertex generation is required before rendering
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the overlap check end <= m_cached_start may fire incorrectly, causing the function to return true (spurious cache miss) even when data is fully cached — wasted work but no crash or data corruption (enforcement: none) [LOW]
start and end must be in the same time coordinate system as the cached data (series time frame, not master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces wrong update decisions (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Return value is true when !isValid() or vertices are empty
Return value is false only when covers(start, end) would return true

Returns true if:

Cache is invalid or empty
Requested range has no overlap with the cached window (jumped location)
Requested range extends beyond the cached window at either end

Returns false (no update needed) only when the cache is valid and fully covers [start, end).
This function is purely computational: no memory allocation, no dereferences, safe to call regardless of cache validity.



std::vector< MissingRange > getMissingRanges(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
) const
Calculate which ranges need to be generated.
Parameters:

start Start of requested range (inclusive)
end End of requested range (exclusive)

Return: Vector of at most 2 missing sub-ranges
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the no-overlap branch may fire and return an inverted MissingRange (start > end) that will corrupt any downstream call to generateVerticesForRange, prependVertices, or appendVertices (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start and end must be expressed in the same time coordinate system as the indices stored in the cache (i.e., the series time frame, not the master time frame); mixing coordinate systems produces geometrically wrong gap ranges (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Return value contains at most 2 entries
If return value has 2 entries, [0].prepend == true and [1].prepend == false
Every returned MissingRange satisfies start <= end when the input satisfies start <= end

Returns 0, 1, or 2 [MissingRange](/api_generated/Classes/structDataViewer_1_1MissingRange.md) entries describing the subranges of [start, end) that are not present in the cache:

0 ranges — fully cached; nothing to generate
1 range, prepend=false — complete cache miss (cache invalid/empty or no overlap); the single entry spans the entire requested window
1 range, prepend=true — left edge missing (scrolling left)
1 range, prepend=false — right edge missing (scrolling right)
2 ranges — both edges missing; first has prepend=true, second has prepend=false

This function is purely computational (no memory allocation beyond the returned vector) and safe to call regardless of cache validity.



void prependVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex requested_start
)
Add vertices to the front of the cache (for scrolling left).
Parameters:

vertices Vertices to prepend (may be empty; call is a no-op if so)
requested_start Start time index of the requested range (inclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If isValid() is true, every element of vertices must have time_idx < cachedStart(); otherwise the buffer becomes unsorted at the join point and binary search in getVerticesForRange() produces wrong results (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty; if capacity is 0, push_front is a no-op yet m_valid is set to true, leaving the cache in an inconsistent state (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty, state is unchanged
If vertices is non-empty and capacity() > 0, isValid() == true
cachedStart() <= old cachedStart() (window expands or stays)
size() <= capacity()

Inserts vertices before all currently cached vertices. Vertices are inserted via push_front in reverse so that the buffer remains sorted by ascending time_idx. If the buffer overflows, the newest vertices at the back are discarded and [cachedEnd()](/api_generated/Classes/classDataViewer_1_1AnalogVertexCache.md#function-cachedend) is narrowed accordingly.
If the cache is currently invalid (empty), this call initialises it using the extent of vertices alone.



void appendVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex requested_end
)
Add vertices to the back of the cache (for scrolling right).
Parameters:

vertices Vertices to append (may be empty; call is a no-op if so)
requested_end End time index of the requested range (exclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If isValid() is true, every element of vertices must have time_idx >= cachedEnd(); otherwise the buffer becomes unsorted at the join point and binary search in getVerticesForRange() produces wrong results (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty; if capacity is 0, push_back is a no-op yet m_valid is set to true and m_cached_end is overwritten with a value derived from vertices, leaving the cache in an inconsistent state (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty, state is unchanged
If vertices is non-empty and capacity() > 0, isValid() == true
cachedEnd() >= old cachedEnd() (window expands or stays)
size() <= capacity()

Inserts vertices after all currently cached vertices via push_back. The circular buffer automatically discards the oldest (front) entries on overflow and [cachedStart()](/api_generated/Classes/classDataViewer_1_1AnalogVertexCache.md#function-cachedstart) is advanced to match.
If the cache is currently invalid (empty), this call initialises it using the extent of vertices alone.



void setVertices(
    std::vector< CachedAnalogVertex > const & vertices,
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
)
Replace all cached vertices (for cache misses or initialization).
Parameters:

vertices New vertex data (may be empty, in which case the cache is invalidated)
start Start time index of the data (inclusive)
end End time index of the data (exclusive)

Precondition:

vertices must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start <= end (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
If vertices is non-empty, vertices.front().time_idx >= start (enforcement: none) [LOW]
If vertices is non-empty, vertices.back().time_idx < end (enforcement: none) [LOW]
capacity() > 0 when vertices is non-empty, otherwise all data is silently discarded (enforcement: runtime_check)

Postcondition:

If vertices is empty or capacity is 0, isValid() == false
If vertices is non-empty and capacity > 0, isValid() == true
size() <= capacity()
cachedStart() <= cachedEnd()

Clears the cache and loads vertices. If the circular buffer capacity is smaller than vertices.size(), the oldest (front) entries are silently discarded and the cached range is narrowed to match what was actually stored.



std::vector< float > getVerticesForRange(
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time
) const
Extract vertices for a specific time range.
Parameters:

start Start of range to extract (inclusive)
end End of range to extract (exclusive)
x_origin_master_absolute_time Absolute physical time at the current view’s left edge (same as AnalogBatchParams::x_origin_master_absolute_time)

Return: Flat vertex array [x0,y0,x1,y1,…], or empty if range not cached
Precondition:

start <= end; if end < start, the reserve() call computes static_cast(negative_int64) * 2, which wraps to near SIZE_MAX and causes std::length_error or std::bad_alloc (enforcement: none) [CRITICAL]
The buffer must be sorted in ascending order by time_idx; the binary search in findIndexForTime() produces wrong results if the buffer is unsorted (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
start >= cachedStart() and end <= cachedEnd() for a non-empty result; requesting a range outside the cached window returns empty (enforcement: runtime_check)

Postcondition:

Return value size is even (pairs of x,y floats)
Return value is empty when cache is invalid or start is not found

Returns a flat float array suitable for GPU upload: [x0, y0, x1, y1, …]. Each output x is [CachedAnalogVertex::x](/api_generated/Classes/structDataViewer_1_1CachedAnalogVertex.md#variable-x) minus x_origin_master_absolute_time (integer-to-double subtraction, then cast to float), matching TimeSeriesMapper view-relative coordinates. y is copied from the cache. Uses binary search to locate start in the buffer, then linearly scans forward until a vertex with time_idx >= end is encountered.
Returns an empty vector (without crashing) when:

The cache is invalid or empty
start is not found in the buffer (beyond the cached range)

    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    ClockTicks x_origin_master_absolute_time,

std::vector< float > getVerticesForRangeDecimated(

class NpyDatasetPreviewModel;
Lazy-loading table model for NumPy .npy file preview.
This model presents .npy array data in a table format:

1D arrays: Single column with index as row
2D arrays: Rows and columns map directly
ND arrays: First dimension is rows, remaining dimensions flattened to columns

Data is loaded in chunks (default 100 rows) and cached using QCache to provide smooth scrolling while minimizing memory usage.

title: NpyDatasetPreviewModel
text:
class NpyDatasetPreviewModel;
Lazy-loading table model for NumPy .npy file preview.
This model presents .npy array data in a table format:

1D arrays: Single column with index as row
2D arrays: Rows and columns map directly
ND arrays: First dimension is rows, remaining dimensions flattened to columns

Data is loaded in chunks (default 100 rows) and cached using QCache to provide smooth scrolling while minimizing memory usage.

class PlottingOpenGL::IBatchRenderer;
Abstract base interface for all batch renderers.
See: PolyLineRenderer, GlyphRenderer, RectangleRenderer
This interface defines the lifecycle and rendering contract for GPU-accelerated batch renderers. Implementations handle specific primitive types (polylines, glyphs, rectangles) and manage their own GPU resources (VBOs, VAOs, shaders).
Lifecycle:

Construction (renderer created but not initialized)
initialize() - Allocate GPU resources (must be called with valid GL context)
uploadData() - Upload batch data to GPU (called when data changes)
render() - Issue draw calls (called each frame)
cleanup() - Release GPU resources (call before context destruction)

Thread Safety: All methods must be called from the thread with the active OpenGL context.

class MLCore::SupervisedRobustPCAOperation;
Supervised Robust PCA dimensionality reduction.
Fits Robust PCA (via ROSL decomposition) on the labeled subset of observations, then projects all data (labeled and unlabeled) into the resulting principal-component space. The ROSL decomposition separates the labeled data into a low-rank component and sparse errors, making the resulting projection robust to outliers.

class PlottingOpenGL::GLFunctions;
Accessor for OpenGL functions in the current context.
Call GLFunctions::get() to obtain a pointer to the QOpenGLFunctions interface for the current context. Returns nullptr if no context is current.
Usage: auto* f = GLFunctions::get(); if (f) { f->glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3); }

Unsupervised clustering that partitions data into K clusters by minimizing within-cluster sum of squared distances. After fitting, the centroids can be used to assign new observations to the nearest cluster.

class OwningRaggedAnalogStorage;
Owning ragged analog storage using Structure of Arrays layout.
Stores float data in parallel vectors for cache-friendly access:

_times[i] - TimeFrameIndex for entry i
_values[i] - float value for entry i

Maintains acceleration structures:

_time_ranges: O(log n) time range lookup

Unlike RaggedTimeSeries storage, this doesn’t track EntityIds since RaggedAnalogTimeSeries doesn’t use them.

class OwningRaggedAnalogStorage;
Owning ragged analog storage using Structure of Arrays layout.
Stores float data in parallel vectors for cache-friendly access:

_times[i] - TimeFrameIndex for entry i
_values[i] - float value for entry i

Maintains acceleration structures:

_time_ranges: O(log n) time range lookup

Unlike RaggedTimeSeries storage, this doesn’t track EntityIds since RaggedAnalogTimeSeries doesn’t use them.

struct LineGroupToIntervalsParameters;
Parameters for converting line group presence to digital intervals.
This transformation analyzes LineData to determine which TimeFrameIndex values contain lines that are members of a specified group. It then creates a DigitalIntervalSeries representing continuous sequences of frames where the group is either present or absent.
Use cases:

Track when specific whiskers (groups) are detected across frames
Identify gaps in tracking for quality control
Create binary signals for correlation analysis with other time series data






EntityGroupManager * group_manager = nullptr;
Pointer to the EntityGroupManager for group lookups.
This is required to query which entities belong to the target group. Must be set before execution.



GroupId target_group_id = 0;
The GroupId to track across frames.
The transformation will check each TimeFrameIndex for lines that are members of this group.



bool track_presence = true;
If true, create intervals where group is PRESENT; if false, where ABSENT.

true (default): Output intervals represent frames containing group members
false: Output intervals represent frames WITHOUT group members (gaps)




int min_interval_length = 1;
Minimum number of consecutive frames to form an interval.
Intervals shorter than this will be filtered out. Useful for removing noise or brief detection artifacts. Default: 1 (no filtering)



int merge_gap_threshold = 1;
If true, merge intervals separated by gaps smaller than this value.
Set to > 1 to bridge small gaps in detection. For example, if set to 3, intervals separated by 1-2 frames will be merged into a single interval. Default: 1 (no merging)

struct CSVMultiFileLineSaverOptions;

class MultiLaneVerticalAxisWidget;
Widget that renders per-lane labels and separators for a stacked layout.
Shows:

Channel name labels centered vertically in each lane
Horizontal separator lines at lane boundaries
Viewport-aware rendering (culls off-screen lanes)

The widget is driven by MultiLaneVerticalAxisState, which receives lane descriptors from the DataViewer after each layout computation.





using MultiLaneVerticalAxisWidget::ViewportGetter =  std::function<std::pair<float, float>()>;
Function type that returns the effective Y viewport bounds.
Returns {y_min, y_max} in world coordinates after applying zoom and pan. Used to keep labels aligned with the OpenGL rendering surface.

class ImageProcessing::ImageProcessor;
Base interface for image processing chains.
This abstract base class provides a framework for implementing different image processing backends while maintaining type safety and avoiding unnecessary conversions within processing chains.
The design allows for backend-specific implementations (e.g., OpenCV, SIMD, etc.) while providing a unified interface for MediaData to use.
Uses variant approach to handle both 8-bit (uint8_t) and 32-bit (float) image data.

struct CorePlotting::LayoutResponse;
Response from layout computation.
Contains computed layout for all requested series.

    std::string const & series_id
) const
Find layout by series ID.
Return: Pointer to layout, or nullptr if not found



bool isSeriesVisible(
    std::string const & series_id,
    float y_min,
    float y_max
) const
Check whether a series lane overlaps a Y viewport range.
Parameters:

series_id Series to test
y_min Bottom of the effective viewport (includes pan)
y_max Top of the effective viewport (includes pan)

Return: true if the lane overlaps the viewport, or if the series has no layout
Precondition: y_min <= y_max
The lane extent is derived from the series layout’s y_transform: center = y_transform.offset, half_height = |y_transform.gain|. A lane is visible when its [center - half_height, center + half_height] interval intersects [y_min, y_max].



std::vector< std::string > visibleSeriesIds(
    float y_min,
    float y_max
) const
Collect IDs of all series whose lanes overlap a Y viewport range.
Parameters:

y_min Bottom of the effective viewport (includes pan)
y_max Top of the effective viewport (includes pan)

Return: Vector of visible series IDs
Precondition: y_min <= y_max
Non-stackable series (intervals, full-canvas events) that do not appear in the layout are always included.

struct CorePlotting::LayoutTransform;
Pure geometric transform that is output = input * gain + offset.
This is the fundamental building block for positioning data in world space. The LayoutEngine outputs these, and they become part of the Model matrix.
The transform is applied as: transformed_value = raw_value * gain + offset
This simple abstraction allows:

Data normalization (z-score, peak-to-peak, etc.)
Layout positioning (vertical stacking)
User adjustments (manual gain/offset tweaks)

Transforms can be composed: applying A then B is equivalent to A.compose(B).

other Transform applied first

Return: Combined transform equivalent to applying other then this
If we apply other then this: result = (x * other.gain + other.offset) * this.gain + this.offset = x * (other.gain * this.gain) + (other.offset * this.gain + this.offset)

template <typename TData >
struct RaggedStorageCache;
Cache structure for fast-path access to contiguous storage.
Template Parameters:

TData The data type stored (e.g., Mask2D, Line2D, Point2D)

When storage is contiguous (OwningRaggedStorage), iterators can use cached pointers for zero-overhead access. For non-contiguous storage (ViewRaggedStorage, LazyRaggedStorage), the cache is invalid and iterators fall back to virtual dispatch.
This optimization mirrors the pattern used in AnalogTimeSeries where contiguous storage gets pointer caching for fast iteration.





inline bool isValid() const
Check if the cache is valid for fast-path access.
Return:

true if storage is contiguous (can use direct pointer access)
false if storage is non-contiguous (must use virtual dispatch)

A valid cache indicates that the underlying storage is contiguous and pointer arithmetic can be used for iteration. Note that an empty owning storage still has a valid cache (is_contiguous=true), it just has cache_size=0.

class CorePlotting::SceneHitTester;
Multi-strategy hit tester for RenderableScene.
This class orchestrates multiple hit testing strategies to determine what element (if any) exists at a given world coordinate. It supports:

QuadTree queries for discrete elements (events, points)
Interval containment for rectangle batches
Series region queries for analog series

The tester prioritizes hits by distance and type, typically preferring discrete elements over continuous regions.
Usage:
SceneHitTester tester;

// Convert screen coordinates to world coordinates
glm::vec2 world_pos = screenToWorld(mouse_pos, viewport_size, 
                                     scene.view_matrix, scene.projection_matrix);

// Perform hit test
HitTestResult result = tester.hitTest(world_pos.x, world_pos.y, scene, layout);

if (result.hasHit()) {
    if (result.hit_type == HitType::DigitalEvent) {
        selectEvent(result.entity_id.value());
    }
}

virtual bool fitTransform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::Row< std::size_t > const & labels,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params,
    arma::mat & result
) override
Fit LARS models and select features with non-zero coefficients.
Parameters:

features (D × N) feature matrix in mlpack convention
labels (N,) label row with class indices in [0, C)
params LARSProjectionParameters or nullptr for defaults
result (A × N) output — input rows for selected features only

Return: true on success, false on validation failure
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must have at least 2 columns (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
labels must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
labels.n_elem must equal features.n_cols (enforcement: runtime_check)
labels must contain at least 2 distinct class values (enforcement: runtime_check)
params, if non-null, must be dynamic_castable to LARSProjectionParameters (enforcement: runtime_check — falls back to defaults if cast fails)

Postcondition:

On success: isTrained() == true, result.n_rows == outputDimensions() (the number of selected features), result.n_cols == features.n_cols
On failure: isTrained() unchanged, result is unmodified

Reimplements: MLCore::MLSupervisedDimReductionOperation::fitTransform
Binary (C=2): fits a single LARS model with binary response. Multi-class (C>=3): fits one-vs-all LARS models and takes the union of active feature sets.

isTrained() must be true (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features.n_rows must equal numFeatures() (enforcement: runtime_check)

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::Examples::TensorTemporalNeighborParams;
Parameters for temporal neighbor feature augmentation (reflect-cpp compatible).
Offsets are generated from separate lag and lead ranges:

Lags: {-lag_step, -2*lag_step, …, -lag_range} (negative offsets, past)
Leads: {+lead_step, +2*lead_step, …, +lead_range} (positive offsets, future)

Example: lag_range=3, lag_step=1, lead_range=2, lead_step=1 → offsets: {-3, -2, -1, +1, +2}





std::vector< int > buildOffsets() const
Build the sorted offset list from lag/lead range and step parameters.






int lag_range = 0;
Maximum lag (past) offset magnitude; 0 disables lags.



int lag_step = 1;
Step size for lag offsets (must be >= 1 when lag_range > 0).



int lead_range = 0;
Maximum lead (future) offset magnitude; 0 disables leads.



int lead_step = 1;
Step size for lead offsets (must be >= 1 when lead_range > 0).



BoundaryPolicy boundary_policy = BoundaryPolicy::NaN;
Boundary policy for rows where a neighbor offset is out-of-range.



bool include_original = true;
Whether to include the original (unshifted) columns in the output.

class DataViewer::DataViewerSelectionManager;
Manages entity selection state for the DataViewer widget.
Provides a clean API for selecting, deselecting, and querying entities. Supports both single-select and multi-select (Ctrl+click) modes.





void selectionChanged(
    EntityId id,
    bool selected
)
Emitted when an entity’s selection state changes.
Parameters:

id The EntityId that changed
selected true if now selected, false if now deselected




void selectionCleared()
Emitted when all selections are cleared.
This is emitted before individual selectionChanged signals for each previously selected entity.



void selectionModified()
Emitted when the selection set changes in any way.
This is a convenience signal for observers that just need to know that something changed, without caring about specifics.

)

id EntityId to select

Adds the entity to the selection set. If already selected, this is a no-op. Emits selectionChanged(id, true) if the entity was not previously selected.



void deselect(
    EntityId id
)
Deselect an entity.

id EntityId to deselect

Removes the entity from the selection set. If not selected, this is a no-op. Emits selectionChanged(id, false) if the entity was previously selected.

)

id EntityId to toggle

If the entity is selected, deselects it. If not selected, selects it. Emits selectionChanged with the new state.

Clear all selections.

class CorePlotting::SpatialLayoutStrategy;
Spatial layout strategy (SpatialOverlay style).
Computes coordinate transforms to fit spatial data (points, lines, masks) into a viewport. Unlike time-series layouts which only stack vertically, spatial layouts transform both X and Y coordinates.
LAYOUT MODES:

Fit: Scale uniformly to fit data bounds into viewport (preserves aspect ratio)
Fill: Scale non-uniformly to fill entire viewport (may distort aspect ratio)
Identity: No transform (1:1 mapping, useful when data is already in viewport coords)

COORDINATE SYSTEM:

Input coordinates are in data space (e.g., image pixels, sensor coordinates)
Output coordinates are in viewport space (typically -1 to +1 NDC or 0 to width/height)
Padding adds margin around data bounds

USE CASES:

SpatialOverlay: Whisker visualization, mask overlay
Image annotation: Points/lines over image coordinates
Direct spatial data: Sensor readings with X/Y positions

struct EventPlotOptions;
Options for plotting an event series in the raster plot.
Event key plus optional metadata. Glyph styling is stored separately in the per-key glyph style map (event_glyph_styles) so that GlyphStyleState objects can manage live state and serialization.
When the key refers to a DigitalIntervalSeries, [interval_edge](/api_generated/Classes/structEventPlotOptions.md#variable-interval-edge) specifies which edge (start or end) to extract as events for plotting.

template <typename T >
class ModificationHandle;
A RAII handle for modifying an object and notifying on completion.
This proxy object holds a reference to data (T&) and a callback. When this handle is destroyed (goes out of scope), the callback is automatically invoked, typically to notify observers of the change.
It is not copyable, but it is movable.

template <typename DataType >
class StateEstimation::MinCostFlowTracker;
A tracker that uses a global min-cost flow optimization to solve data association.
Template Parameters:

DataType raw observation type (e.g., Line2D)

This tracker formulates the tracking problem as a graph problem, finding the globally optimal set of tracks over an entire interval between anchors. It is more robust to ambiguities and identity swaps than iterative, frame-by-frame methods.





inline MinCostFlowTracker(
    std::unique_ptr< IFilter > filter_prototype,
    std::unique_ptr< IFeatureExtractor< DataType > > feature_extractor,
    CostFunction cost_function,
    double cost_scale_factor =100.0,
    double cheap_assignment_threshold =5.0,
    TrackerContractPolicy policy =TrackerContractPolicy::Throw,
    int n_scan_depth =3,
    bool enable_n_scan =true,
    int max_gap_frames =3
)
Construct a new MinCostFlowTracker.
Parameters:

filter_prototype Prototype filter (cloned for prediction and final smoothing). If nullptr, prediction is skipped in cost calculation (cost function must handle this) and no smoothing is performed. The filter’s uncertainty automatically scales with gap size through process noise accumulation.
feature_extractor Feature extractor for DataType
cost_function Function to compute cost between predicted state and observation
cost_scale_factor Multiplier to convert floating-point costs to integers for the solver.
cheap_assignment_threshold Threshold for greedy chaining
policy Contract violation policy
n_scan_depth Number of frames to look ahead when assignments are ambiguous (default 3)
enable_n_scan Enable N-scan lookahead for ambiguous assignments (default true)
max_gap_frames Maximum frames a chain can skip before terminating (default 3, set to -1 for unlimited)

)

chain_cost_function Cost for frame-to-frame greedy chaining (typically 1-step)
transition_cost_function Cost for meta-node transitions across k-step gaps
n_scan_depth Number of frames to look ahead when assignments are ambiguous (default 3)
enable_n_scan Enable N-scan lookahead for ambiguous assignments (default true)

    std::unique_ptr< IFilter > filter_prototype,

    Eigen::MatrixXd const & measurement_matrix,

    TrackerContractPolicy policy =TrackerContractPolicy::Throw,

)
Convenience constructor using default Mahalanobis distance cost function.
Parameters:

filter_prototype Prototype filter (cloned for prediction and final smoothing). If nullptr, Mahalanobis distance cannot be computed properly (requires filter state covariance). The filter’s uncertainty automatically scales with gap size.
feature_extractor Feature extractor for DataType
measurement_matrix H matrix for Mahalanobis distance calculation
measurement_noise_covariance R matrix for Mahalanobis distance calculation
cost_scale_factor Multiplier to convert floating-point costs to integers for the solver.
cheap_assignment_threshold Threshold for greedy chaining
policy Contract violation policy
n_scan_depth Number of frames to look ahead when assignments are ambiguous (default 3)
enable_n_scan Enable N-scan lookahead for ambiguous assignments (default true)




inline void setLookaheadCostFunction(
    CostFunction cost_fn
)
Set a dedicated cost function for N-scan lookahead scoring.
Precondition: cost_fn should be a valid callable; behavior is undefined if empty
Postcondition: Subsequent N-scan calls will use the provided function
This function is used exclusively inside the lookahead expansion and can differ from the greedy chaining or meta-node transition costs. It is useful to introduce dynamics-aware penalties (velocity/acceleration) only for ambiguity resolution while keeping cheaper costs elsewhere.



inline void setTransitionCostFunction(
    CostFunction cost_fn
)
Override the transition cost used between meta-nodes in the MCF graph.



inline void setLookaheadThreshold(
    double threshold
)
Set the acceptance threshold for N-scan lookahead costs.
Use a larger threshold for dynamics-aware costs whose scale exceeds the cheap chaining threshold. Set to infinity to disable pruning by threshold.



inline void setAmbiguityThreshold(
    double threshold
)
Set ambiguity threshold and optional margin to decide when to run N-scan. If the best cost < ambiguity_threshold and (second_best - best) >= ambiguity_margin, the chain is considered certain and N-scan is skipped.

    double margin

class StateEstimation::LineCentroidExtractor;
Feature extractor that computes line centroids on-demand.
This extractor computes the centroid (center of mass) of a Line2D object when features are requested, rather than pre-computing and caching. This approach is more memory-efficient and only computes features for lines that are actually used in tracking.
The centroid is computed as the mean of all points in the line: centroid = (sum of all points) / (number of points)
Features returned:

Filter features: [x_centroid, y_centroid] (2D position)
Initial state: [x, y, vx, vy] (position + zero velocity, high uncertainty)

class EntityGroupManager;
Manages user-defined groups of EntityIds for cross-data linking and visualization.
Note: Thread Safety: This class is not thread-safe. Callers must synchronize access when using from multiple threads. Consider wrapping operations in a mutex or using from a single thread (e.g., the Qt UI thread).
This class provides fast lookup and manipulation of entity groups to support linking data across different formats (e.g., from TableView rows back to raw LineData). Optimized for hundreds of thousands of entities with O(1) group operations.





GroupId createGroup(
    std::string const & name,
    std::string const & description =""
)
Create a new empty group with the given name.
Parameters:

name User-friendly name for the group (empty allowed).
description Optional description for the group (default ““).

Return: GroupId of the created group (never 0; 0 is reserved for invalid).
Note: Does not check for an existing group with the same name; each call creates a new group and returns a new id. Duplicate names are allowed.
No preconditions on name or description; both are stored as-is.



bool deleteGroup(
    GroupId group_id
)
Delete a group and all its entities.
Parameters:

group_id The group to delete (e.g. from createGroup or getAllGroupIds).

No preconditions on group_id; any GroupId is valid. Non-existent id returns false.

class EntityGroupManager;
Manages user-defined groups of EntityIds for cross-data linking and visualization.
Note: Thread Safety: This class is not thread-safe. Callers must synchronize access when using from multiple threads. Consider wrapping operations in a mutex or using from a single thread (e.g., the Qt UI thread).
This class provides fast lookup and manipulation of entity groups to support linking data across different formats (e.g., from TableView rows back to raw LineData). Optimized for hundreds of thousands of entities with O(1) group operations.

struct CorePlotting::ViewState;
Full runtime 2D camera / viewport state.
See:

ViewStateData — serializable subset
toRuntimeViewState() — ViewStateData → ViewState

Combines the serializable ViewStateData (zoom, pan, data bounds) with runtime-only information (viewport pixel dimensions, validity flag, padding factor).
This struct is used to generate View and Projection matrices for the RenderableScene. It is the primary input to calculateVisibleWorldBounds(), computeMatricesFromViewState(), screenToWorld(), worldToScreen(), etc.
Widget code should store ViewStateData for serialization and promote it to ViewState at render time via toRuntimeViewState().

class PlottingOpenGL::SceneRenderer;
Coordinates rendering of a complete RenderableScene.
See: CorePlotting::RenderableScene
SceneRenderer is the main entry point for rendering CorePlotting scenes using OpenGL. It manages the lifecycle of individual batch renderers and orchestrates the rendering of all primitives in a scene.
Usage:
// In initializeGL():
SceneRenderer renderer;
renderer.initialize();

// When scene data changes:
renderer.uploadScene(scene);

// In paintGL():
renderer.render();

// Before context destruction:
renderer.cleanup();
The SceneRenderer holds the View and Projection matrices from the scene and passes them to each batch renderer along with the batch’s Model matrix.

Set the rendering order for batch types.
By default, the order is: Rectangles -> PolyLines -> Glyphs (back to front, so rectangles are behind lines and points).

class MLCore::ICAOperation;
ICA via mlpack’s RADICAL algorithm.
Performs Independent Component Analysis using the RADICAL (Robust, Accurate, Direct ICA aLgorithm). Decomposes the input matrix X into independent components Y and a square unmixing matrix W such that Y = W * X.
Unlike PCA, ICA seeks statistical independence (not just uncorrelatedness). The number of output dimensions equals the number of input features (RADICAL does not reduce dimensionality).
Stores the fitted unmixing matrix for re-projection of new data via transform().

function fitTransform
virtual bool fitTransform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    MLModelParametersBase const * params,
    arma::mat & result
) override
Fit the ICA model to data and project in a single call.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (features × observations) in mlpack convention
params Algorithm-specific parameters (must be ICAParameters or null)
result Output: independent components matrix (features × observations)

Return: true on success, false on validation failure
Precondition:

features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must have at least 2 columns (observations) (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not contain NaN or Inf values — RADICAL produces garbage otherwise (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params, if non-null, must be dynamic_castable to ICAParameters (enforcement: runtime_check — falls back to defaults if cast fails)

Postcondition:

On success: isTrained() == true, result has features.n_rows rows and features.n_cols columns, numFeatures() == features.n_rows
On failure: isTrained() unchanged, result is unmodified

Reimplements: MLCore::MLDimReductionOperation::fitTransform

virtual bool transform(
    arma::mat const & features,
    arma::mat & result
) override
Project new data using the fitted unmixing matrix.
Parameters:

features Input matrix (features × observations) in mlpack convention
result Output: independent components (features × observations)

Return: true on success, false if untrained or dimension mismatch
Precondition:

isTrained() must be true (enforcement: runtime_check)
features must not be empty (enforcement: runtime_check)
features.n_rows must equal numFeatures() (enforcement: runtime_check)

Postcondition: result has outputDimensions() rows and features.n_cols columns
Reimplements: MLCore::MLDimReductionOperation::transform
Computes result = W * features, where W is the unmixing matrix learned during fitTransform().

class DataManagerExtension;
Extension to DataManager that provides the TableView factory interface.
This class extends the existing DataManager with the getAnalogSource factory method as described in the TableView design document. It can create and cache IAnalogSource adapters for both physical data (AnalogTimeSeries) and virtual data (PointData components).





using DataManagerExtension::SourceHandle =  std::variant<
            std::shared_ptr<IAnalogSource>,
            std::shared_ptr<DigitalEventSeries>,
            std::shared_ptr<DigitalIntervalSeries>,
            std::shared_ptr<LineData>,
            std::shared_ptr<PointData>>;

)

name The name of the analog data source.

Return: Shared pointer to IAnalogSource, or nullptr if not found.

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::ReductionStep;
Represents a reduction that computes a value for the store.
A ReductionStep encapsulates:

The name of the reduction to execute (from RangeReductionRegistry)
The key under which to store the result
Optional parameters for the reduction
Optional bindings for the reduction’s own parameters

The result of executing a ReductionStep is a scalar value that gets stored in the PipelineValueStore under [output_key](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Transforms_1_1V2_1_1ReductionStep.md#variable-output-key).

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::ReductionStep;
Represents a reduction that computes a value for the store.
A ReductionStep encapsulates:

The name of the reduction to execute (from RangeReductionRegistry)
The key under which to store the result
Optional parameters for the reduction
Optional bindings for the reduction’s own parameters

The result of executing a ReductionStep is a scalar value that gets stored in the PipelineValueStore under [output_key](/api_generated/Classes/structNeuralyzer_1_1Transforms_1_1V2_1_1ReductionStep.md#variable-output-key).

Remove all data objects from _data

Clear all data-to-timeframe mappings

) const
Get all TimeFrameIndex values in a group for a specific clock.
Parameters:

group_id The group to query
time_key The clock to filter by

Return: Vector of TimeFrameIndex values (unordered), empty if group doesn’t exist

std::vector< TimeFrameIndex > getTimeIndicesInGroupConverted(
    GroupId group_id,
    TimeKey const & target_key
) const
Get all TimeFrameIndex values in a group, converted to a target clock.
Parameters:

group_id The group to query
target_key The target clock to convert indices into

Return: Vector of converted TimeFrameIndex values (unordered), empty if group doesn’t exist or target TimeFrame is not registered
For each TimeEntity in the group (regardless of its source clock), converts its index to the target clock using convert_time_index(). TimeEntities already on the target clock are included without conversion. Non-TimeEntity members are skipped. Requires that both the source and target TimeFrames are registered.

class DigitalEventSeries;
A sorted collection of discrete time events with entity tracking.
DigitalEventSeries stores events as (TimeFrameIndex, EntityId) pairs, maintaining events in sorted order by time. Each event represents a discrete occurrence at a specific time point (compare to DigitalIntervalSeries for time ranges).

text:
Primary Interface

view(): Returns a lazy range of ClockTicksWithId objects for iteration
getStoredEvent(): Returns index-space event time at storage index (save/export)
viewInRange(): Returns events in a time range (requires TimeFrame for conversion)
addEvent()/removeEvent(): Modify events (owning storage only)
createView()/createFromView(): Create view/lazy backed series
materialize(): Convert any storage type to owning storage

title: DigitalEventSeries
text:
Storage Backends
The class supports three storage backends (Owning, View, Lazy) that provide different performance tradeoffs. See Digital_Event_Series.hpp for details.

class dl::GeneralEncoderModel;
General-purpose encoder model for extracting spatial feature tensors from images.
Precondition: Input resolution and output shape must have positive dimensions.
Maps a single input image to a feature tensor using any backbone (e.g. ConvNeXt, ViT, ResNet). The input resolution, number of input channels, and output feature shape are configurable at construction time.
Input slots:

“image” : [input_channels, height, width] — input image (RGB by default)

Output slots:

“features” : [output_shape…] — extracted feature tensor

Batch mode: DynamicBatch{1, max} (supports arbitrary batch sizes).
Usage:
// Default: 3-channel 224x224 input → 384x7x7 output
dl::GeneralEncoderModel model;

// Custom resolution:
dl::GeneralEncoderModel model(3, 512, 512, {768, 16, 16});

class RelativeTimeAxisWidget;
Widget that renders a horizontal time axis for relative time plots.
Shows:

Time range (e.g., -500 to +500 ms)
Tick marks at regular intervals
Center line at t=0 highlighted
Zoom/pan aware positioning

This widget is designed to work with CorePlotting::ViewState, making it reusable across EventPlotWidget, HeatmapWidget, PSTHWidget, and other relative time plots.

text:
Data Bounds
[x_min](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-x-min)/[x_max](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-x-max) and [y_min](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-y-min)/[y_max](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-y-max) define the world-coordinate extent of the data being visualised. Changing these typically triggers a scene rebuild (e.g. re-gathering trial data for a different time window).
For widgets whose bounds come from a separate AxisState (ScatterPlot, ACF, TemporalProjection), bounds can be left at their defaults and set at render time.

title: CorePlotting::ViewStateData
text:
View Transform
[x_zoom](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-x-zoom)/[y_zoom](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-y-zoom) scale the visible range (1.0 = fit-to-bounds). [x_pan](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-x-pan)/[y_pan](/api_generated/Classes/structCorePlotting_1_1ViewStateData.md#variable-y-pan) shift the view in world coordinates. Changing these only requires a projection matrix update, not a scene rebuild.

struct Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::DigitalIntervalBooleanParams;
Parameters for digital interval boolean operations.
This transform applies boolean logic between two DigitalIntervalSeries. Intervals are treated as boolean time series where presence in an interval means “true” at that timestamp.
Example JSON: ```json
{ “operation”: “and” }

Note: For the NOT operation, only the first input is used. The second input is ignored but must still be provided due to the binary transform signature. 

## Public Types Documentation

### enum Operation

| Enumerator | Value | Description |
| ---------- | ----- | ----------- |
| And | | Intersection of intervals (both must be true).   |
| Or | | Union of intervals (either can be true).   |
| Xor | | Exclusive or (exactly one must be true).   |
| Not | | Invert the first series (second series is ignored).   |
| and_not | | First AND (NOT second) - subtract second from first.   |



Boolean operation to perform. 

## Public Attributes Documentation

### variable operation

```cpp
Operation operation = Operation::And;

class OwningRaggedStorage;
Owning ragged storage using Structure of Arrays layout.

TData The data type stored (e.g., Mask2D, Line2D, Point2D)

_entity_ids[i] - EntityId for entry i

Maintains acceleration structures:

_entity_to_index: O(1) EntityId lookup
_time_ranges: O(log n) time range lookup

Describes the shape and named axes of a tensor.
A tensor has an ordered list of named axes. Each axis has a name and a size. The descriptor also supports optional named columns on one designated axis, useful for tabular / feature-matrix representations.
Axis names are freeform strings. Conventional names include:

“time” — row axis indexed by TimeIndexStorage
“channel” — named columns / features
“frequency” — frequency bins (spectrograms)
“batch” — batch dimension (model I/O)
“height”, “width” — spatial (image-like tensors)

Row-major strides are computed on construction for efficient flat-index calculations.

Feature conversion configuration.
Controls NaN dropping, z-score normalization, etc.

Where to assign clusters after fitting.

Configuration for writing clustering outputs.



std::string time_key_str = "time";
Time key string for time frame lookups.
Identifies which TimeFrame the feature tensor’s rows are indexed by. Used for output writing (intervals, groups).



bool defer_dm_writes = false;
If true, skip DataManager writes and store output in the result.
When running from a background thread, DataManager writes trigger observer callbacks that may manipulate Qt widgets, which is undefined behavior. Set this to true and perform the writes on the main thread instead.

class EditorState;
Base class for all editor/widget states.
EditorState is designed to separate widget visual components from their underlying state. This enables:

Multiple views of same state: Properties panels and main editors can both observe the same state object
Serialization: Complete application state can be saved/restored
Undo/Redo: Command pattern can operate on state objects
Testing: State logic can be tested without UI
