text:
std::shared_ptr< AnalogTimeSeries > analogDifference(
    AnalogTimeSeries const & input,
    AnalogDifferenceParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Compute backward, central, or forward difference on an AnalogTimeSeries.
Parameters:

input Input analog time series
params Differencing parameters
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation

Return: New AnalogTimeSeries with differenced values, or nullptr on validation failure or when Skip policy eliminates all samples
Precondition: params.window >= 1
Container signature: AnalogTimeSeries → AnalogTimeSeries
Each output sample is anchored at the same TimeFrameIndex as the corresponding input index. With Skip edge policy, boundary samples are omitted from output.



std::shared_ptr< DigitalEventSeries > analogEventThreshold(
    AnalogTimeSeries const & input,
    AnalogEventThresholdParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Detect threshold crossing events in an analog time series.
Parameters:

input Input analog time series
params Threshold parameters (value, direction, lockout)
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation

Return: Shared pointer to digital event series containing event times
This is a container-level transform because it has temporal dependencies: the lockout period requires looking at previous samples to determine if an event should be reported.
Container signature: AnalogTimeSeries → DigitalEventSeries
Algorithm:

Iterate through time series samples
Check if value crosses threshold (based on direction)
If crossed and outside lockout period from last event, record event
Report progress and check for cancellation




std::shared_ptr< AnalogTimeSeries > analogHilbertPhase(
    AnalogTimeSeries const & input,
    AnalogHilbertPhaseParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Calculate instantaneous phase or amplitude using Hilbert transform.
Parameters:

input Input analog time series
params Hilbert transform parameters
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation

Return: Shared pointer to analog time series containing phase (radians) or amplitude
This is a container-level transform because it operates on the entire time series and handles discontinuities, chunked processing, and FFT-based computation that requires global context.
Container signature: AnalogTimeSeries → AnalogTimeSeries
Algorithm:

Detect discontinuities and split into chunks
For each chunk: a. Optionally apply bandpass filter b. Compute FFT c. Create analytic signal by zeroing negative frequencies d. Compute inverse FFT e. Extract phase (atan2) or amplitude (magnitude)
Stitch chunks back together
Report progress and check for cancellation




std::shared_ptr< TensorData > analogToTensor(
    std::vector< std::shared_ptr< AnalogTimeSeries const > > const & channels,
    AnalogToTensorParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Pack multiple AnalogTimeSeries channels into a single 2D TensorData.
Parameters:

channels Non-empty vector of channels to pack
params Parameters (channel_keys used as column names if sizes match)
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation/logging

Return: 2D TensorData (time × channels), or nullptr on validation failure
Precondition:

channels must not be empty
All channels must have identical sample counts
All channels must share the same TimeFrame (pointer identity)

All channels must share the same TimeFrame (by pointer identity) and have the same sample count. Uses viewValues() for mmap-safe iteration.



std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries > eventToInterval(
    DigitalEventSeries const & input,
    EventToIntervalParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Expand each event in a DigitalEventSeries into a window interval.
Parameters:

input Input event series
params Pre/post expansion sizes in TimeFrameIndex units
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation

Return: Shared pointer to overlapping DigitalIntervalSeries
Precondition: params.pre_expansion and params.post_expansion must be non-negative
Container signature: DigitalEventSeries -> DigitalIntervalSeries
Each event at TimeFrameIndex T produces one interval: [T - pre_expansion, T + post_expansion]
The output uses IntervalLayout::Overlapping and preserves the input TimeFrame.



TimeFrameIndex eventTimeForInterval(
    TimeFrameInterval const & interval,

Resample or simplify a line based on the selected algorithm.
Parameters:

line The line to resample/simplify
params Parameters specifying algorithm and settings

Return: Line2D The resampled/simplified line
This is a unary element-level transform that takes a Line2D as input and returns a resampled/simplified Line2D.
Algorithm descriptions:
FixedSpacing: Iterates through the polyline, placing new points at target_spacing intervals. Interpolates between original points as needed. Preserves first and last points.
DouglasPeucker: Recursively simplifies a polyline by removing points that are within epsilon distance of the line segment between two endpoints. Preserves overall shape while reducing point count.
PolynomialSmooth: Fits parametric polynomials x(t), y(t) with arc-length parameterization, then generates evenly-spaced points along the fitted curve. Falls back to FixedSpacing resampling if fitting fails.
When applied to containers:

LineData → LineData (one resampled line per input line)

Edge cases:

Empty lines: Returned unchanged (empty)
Single-point lines: Returned unchanged (cannot resample)
Two-point lines: Returned unchanged (minimal representation)

std::shared_ptr< AnalogTimeSeries > sincInterpolation(
    AnalogTimeSeries const & input,
    SincInterpolationParams const & params,
    ComputeContext const & ctx
)
Apply band-limited sinc interpolation to upsample an AnalogTimeSeries.
Parameters:

input Input analog time series with N samples
params Interpolation parameters
ctx Compute context for progress/cancellation

Return: Shared pointer to a new AnalogTimeSeries with (N-1)*factor+1 samples, or nullptr if input is empty or params are invalid
Precondition: params.upsampling_factor >= 1
For each output sample position m in [0, M-1] where M = (N-1)*factor + 1:

Compute fractional input position: x = m / factor
For each input sample n in [floor(x) - K, floor(x) + K]: accumulate sinc(x - n) * window(x - n) * input[n]
Output sample = weighted sum

Where K = kernel_half_width and sinc(t) = sin(pit) / (pit), sinc(0) = 1.

std::vector< std::string > renderSceneToSVG(
    CorePlotting::RenderableScene const & scene,
    SVGExportParams const & params
)
Flatten scene batches to SVG element strings in fixed draw order.
Precondition:

params.canvas_width > 0 and params.canvas_height > 0 if coordinates should match OpenGL-style NDC→pixel mapping in the sub-renderers (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
Batch contents satisfy the preconditions of [SVGRectangleRenderer::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGRectangleRenderer.md#function-render), [SVGPolyLineRenderer::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGPolyLineRenderer.md#function-render), and [SVGGlyphRenderer::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGGlyphRenderer.md#function-render) respectively (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns the concatenation of per-batch renderer outputs in the order above (each batch may contribute zero or more strings).
Does not throw under normal allocator / string behavior.

Order: all rectangle_batches, then all poly_line_batches, then all glyph_batches. Uses scene.view_matrix and scene.projection_matrix for every batch. spatial_index, entity maps, selection, and preview fields are not read.



std::string buildSVGDocument(
    CorePlotting::RenderableScene const & scene,
    SVGExportParams const & params
)
Build a full SVG 1.1 document.
Precondition:

params.canvas_width and params.canvas_height should be positive for a conventional canvas (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
params.background_color must be safe inside fill="…" (no ", &, <, etc.) (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]

Postcondition:

Returns a document starting with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>, a root <svg> with viewBox="0 0 width height", a constant <desc>[Neuralyzer](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceNeuralyzer.md)[DataViewer](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespaceDataViewer.md) Export</desc>, a full-viewport background <rect>, then each string from [renderSceneToSVG](/api_generated/Namespaces/namespacePlottingSVG.md#function-renderscenetosvg) on its own line with leading indentation, and a closing </svg>.
Does not throw under normal stream behavior.

XML declaration, root <svg>, fixed <desc>, background <rect>, then scene elements.
Implementation is string-based (not [SVGDocument](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGDocument.md)); fragment strings are not XML-escaped.



std::vector< std::string > createScalebarSVG(
    int scalebar_length,
    ScalebarTimeRange time_range,
    SVGExportParams const & params
)
Bottom-right scalebar (default [SVGScalebar]() corner).
Precondition:

For non-empty output, time_range.end > time_range.start with a finite positive span, and params.canvas_width > 0, params.canvas_height > 0 (matches [SVGScalebar::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) early exit) (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
scalebar_length non-zero if the bar should have non-zero extent in typical ranges (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns an empty vector when [SVGScalebar::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) would return empty; otherwise the same four SVG fragments as that render (bar, ticks, label) for the default decoration configuration.
Does not throw under normal behavior of the callee.

horizontal bar, end ticks, numeric label.
Delegates to [SVGScalebar](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md)(scalebar_length, time_range.start, time_range.end) and render(canvas).



glm::vec2 transformVertexToSVG(
    glm::vec4 const & vertex,
    glm::mat4 const & mvp,
    int canvas_width,
    int canvas_height
)
Apply mvp to a homogeneous world-space vertex and map the result to SVG pixel coordinates.
Parameters:

vertex Typically (x, y, 0, 1) in the same space as mvp.
mvp Model–view–projection matrix (column-major, GL convention).
canvas_width Target width in pixels.
canvas_height Target height in pixels.

Precondition:

canvas_width > 0 and canvas_height > 0 if the mapping should match the usual OpenGL viewport convention (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
For finite pixel output, mvp * vertex and the post-divide NDC values should be finite; near-zero w skips the divide and can amplify coordinates (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns {svg_x, svg_y} with components computed from the formulas above (points may lie outside the [0, width] × [0, height] range when NDC is outside [-1, 1]).
Does not throw.

Performs ndc = mvp * vertex, then a perspective divide when std::abs(ndc.w) > 1e-6f (if w is smaller in magnitude, x/y are not divided). Maps NDC x from [-1, 1] to [0, canvas_width] and flips y so NDC +1 is the top of the canvas (svg_y = height * (1 - ndc.y) / 2).



std::string colorToSVGHex(
    glm::vec4 const & color
)
Convert linear RGB channels to an uppercase #RRGGBB string for SVG fill / stroke.
Precondition: For predictable channel bytes, color.r, color.g, and color.b should be finite (enforcement: none) [LOW]
Postcondition:

Returns exactly seven characters: '#' plus six uppercase hexadecimal digits.
Does not throw under normal std::ostringstream behavior.

Each channel is clamp(channel * 255, 0, 255); values outside [0, 1] are saturated. The alpha component is not encoded (callers must emit fill-opacity / stroke-opacity separately if needed).

For non-empty output, time_range.end > time_range.start with a finite positive span, and params.canvas_width > 0, params.canvas_height > 0 (matches [SVGScalebar::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) early exit) (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
scalebar_length non-zero if the bar should have non-zero extent in typical ranges (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns an empty vector when [SVGScalebar::render](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md#function-render) would return empty; otherwise the same four SVG fragments as that render (bar, ticks, label) for the default decoration configuration.
Does not throw under normal behavior of the callee.

horizontal bar, end ticks, numeric label.
Delegates to [SVGScalebar](/api_generated/Classes/classPlottingSVG_1_1SVGScalebar.md)(scalebar_length, time_range.start, time_range.end) and render(canvas).



glm::vec2 transformVertexToSVG(
    glm::vec4 const & vertex,
    glm::mat4 const & mvp,
    int canvas_width,
    int canvas_height
)
Apply mvp to a homogeneous world-space vertex and map the result to SVG pixel coordinates.
Parameters:

vertex Typically (x, y, 0, 1) in the same space as mvp.
mvp Model–view–projection matrix (column-major, GL convention).
canvas_width Target width in pixels.
canvas_height Target height in pixels.

Precondition:

canvas_width > 0 and canvas_height > 0 if the mapping should match the usual OpenGL viewport convention (enforcement: none) [IMPORTANT]
For finite pixel output, mvp * vertex and the post-divide NDC values should be finite; near-zero w skips the divide and can amplify coordinates (enforcement: none) [LOW]

Postcondition:

Returns {svg_x, svg_y} with components computed from the formulas above (points may lie outside the [0, width] × [0, height] range when NDC is outside [-1, 1]).
Does not throw.

Performs ndc = mvp * vertex, then a perspective divide when std::abs(ndc.w) > 1e-6f (if w is smaller in magnitude, x/y are not divided). Maps NDC x from [-1, 1] to [0, canvas_width] and flips y so NDC +1 is the top of the canvas (svg_y = height * (1 - ndc.y) / 2).



std::string colorToSVGHex(
    glm::vec4 const & color
)
Convert linear RGB channels to an uppercase #RRGGBB string for SVG fill / stroke.
Precondition: For predictable channel bytes, color.r, color.g, and color.b should be finite (enforcement: none) [LOW]
Postcondition:

Returns exactly seven characters: '#' plus six uppercase hexadecimal digits.
Does not throw under normal std::ostringstream behavior.

Each channel is clamp(channel * 255, 0, 255); values outside [0, 1] are saturated. The alpha component is not encoded (callers must emit fill-opacity / stroke-opacity separately if needed).

template <std::ranges::input_range R>
auto filterByTimeRange(
    R && range,
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end
)
Filter a range of time series elements by time range.
Parameters:

range The input range to filter
start Start of time range (inclusive)
end End of time range (inclusive)

Template Parameters:

R Range type (must be an input_range of TimeSeriesElement)

Return: A lazy view of elements in the time range
Note: The returned view holds a reference to start and end by value, so they are safely captured.
Par:

Example

auto series = createAnalogTimeSeries();
auto filtered = filterByTimeRange(series->elementsView(),
                                   TimeFrameIndex(100),
                                   TimeFrameIndex(200));
for (auto const& elem : filtered) {
    std::cout << elem.time().getValue() << ": " << elem.value() << "\n";
}

Complexity

O(1) to create the view. O(n) to fully iterate where n = input size.
Returns a lazy view containing only elements whose time() falls within the inclusive range [start, end]. The view does not copy data and evaluates lazily during iteration.

template <std::ranges::input_range R>
auto filterByEntityIds(
    R && range,
    std::unordered_set< EntityId > const & entity_ids
)
Filter a range of entity elements by EntityId set.
Parameters:

range The input range to filter
entity_ids Set of EntityIds to include

Template Parameters:

R Range type (must be an input_range of EntityElement)

Return: A lazy view of elements with matching EntityIds
Note: This function is only available for types satisfying EntityElement. Types like TimeValuePoint and FlatElement will fail at compile time.
Warning: The returned view holds a reference to entity_ids. The caller must ensure the set outlives the view’s usage.
Par:

Example

auto events = createDigitalEventSeries();
std::unordered_set<EntityId> selected{EntityId(1), EntityId(3), EntityId(5)};
auto filtered = filterByEntityIds(events->view(), selected);
for (auto const& event : filtered) {
    // Only events with EntityId 1, 3, or 5
}

Complexity

O(1) to create the view. O(n) to fully iterate where n = input size. Each element check is O(1) average due to hash set lookup.
Returns a lazy view containing only elements whose id() is present in the provided set of EntityIds. The view does not copy data and evaluates lazily during iteration.

    std::unordered_set< EntityId > const & entity_ids
)
Filter a range of entity elements by EntityId set.
Parameters:

range The input range to filter
entity_ids Set of EntityIds to include

Template Parameters:

R Range type (must be an input_range of EntityElement)

Return: A lazy view of elements with matching EntityIds
Note: This function is only available for types satisfying EntityElement. Types like TimeValuePoint and FlatElement will fail at compile time.
Warning: The returned view holds a reference to entity_ids. The caller must ensure the set outlives the view’s usage.
Par:

Example

auto events = createDigitalEventSeries();
std::unordered_set<EntityId> selected{EntityId(1), EntityId(3), EntityId(5)};
auto filtered = filterByEntityIds(events->view(), selected);
for (auto const& event : filtered) {
    // Only events with EntityId 1, 3, or 5
}

Complexity

O(1) to create the view. O(n) to fully iterate where n = input size. Each element check is O(1) average due to hash set lookup.
Returns a lazy view containing only elements whose id() is present in the provided set of EntityIds. The view does not copy data and evaluates lazily during iteration.



template <std::ranges::input_range R>
auto filterByEntityId(
    R && range,
    EntityId entity_id
)
Filter a range of entity elements by a single EntityId.
Parameters:

range The input range to filter
entity_id The EntityId to match

Template Parameters:

R Range type (must be an input_range of EntityElement)

Return: A lazy view of elements with the specified EntityId
Convenience overload for filtering by a single EntityId. More efficient than creating a set for single-ID queries.



template <std::ranges::input_range R>
auto filterByTimeRangeAndEntityIds(
    R && range,
    TimeFrameIndex start,
    TimeFrameIndex end,
    std::unordered_set< EntityId > const & entity_ids
)
Filter by both time range and EntityId set.
Parameters:

range The input range to filter
start Start of time range (inclusive)
end End of time range (inclusive)
entity_ids Set of EntityIds to include

Template Parameters:

R Range type (must be an input_range of EntityElement)

Return: A lazy view of elements matching both criteria
Warning: The returned view holds a reference to entity_ids. The caller must ensure the set outlives the view’s usage.
Convenience function that combines time range and EntityId filtering in a single pass. More efficient than chaining separate filters when both criteria are known upfront.



template <std::ranges::input_range R>
auto materializeToVector(
    R && range
)
Materialize a range into a vector.
Parameters:

range The input range to materialize

Template Parameters:

R Range type

Return: std::vector containing copies of all elements
Par: Example
auto filtered = filterByTimeRange(series->view(), start, end);
auto vec = materializeToVector(filtered);
// vec is now an independent std::vector

Pass filtered results to APIs expecting vectors
Iterate multiple times over filtered results
Ensure data lifetime beyond the source range

end_time End of range to generate (master [TimeFrameIndex](/api_generated/Classes/structTimeFrameIndex.md))

CorePlotting::RenderablePolyLineBatch buildAnalogSeriesBatchCached(
    AnalogTimeSeries const & series,
    std::shared_ptr< TimeFrame > const & master_time_frame,
    AnalogBatchParams const & params,
    glm::mat4 const & model_matrix,
    DataViewer::AnalogVertexCache & cache,
    std::vector< float > * scratch_buffer =nullptr
)
Build analog batch using vertex cache for efficient scrolling.
Parameters:

series The analog time series data
master_time_frame The master time frame for coordinate conversion
params Batch building parameters (time range, gap config, style)
model_matrix Pre-computed Model matrix
cache Vertex cache (will be updated with new data)

Return: A batch ready for upload to PolyLineRenderer
This function implements the ring buffer optimization strategy:

Check if cache covers the requested range
If not, generate only the missing edge data
Update the cache with new vertices
Return batch built from cached vertices

For typical scrolling (scroll by 10-100 points out of 100K visible), this is ~26-130x faster than regenerating all vertices.

std::size_t createTensorColumnViews(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & tensor_key,
    std::string const & prefix,
    std::vector< int > const & columns
)
Create AnalogTimeSeries column views from a TensorData in DataManager.
Parameters:

dm DataManager containing the tensor
tensor_key DataManager key of the source TensorData
prefix Prefix for generated AnalogTimeSeries keys
columns 0-based column indices to extract (empty = all columns)

Return: Number of views successfully created
Precondition:

dm must contain a TensorData at tensor_key
The TensorData must be 2D
All column indices must be in [0, numColumns())

For each selected column (or all columns if columns is empty), creates a zero-copy AnalogTimeSeries view backed by TensorColumnAnalogStorage and inserts it into the DataManager under “{prefix}/{column_name}”.



std::vector< AnalogKeyGroup > discoverAnalogKeyGroups(
    DataManager & dm
)
Discover groups of AnalogTimeSeries keys sharing a common prefix.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to scan for AnalogTimeSeries keys

Return: Vector of key groups, sorted by prefix
Scans all AnalogTimeSeries keys in the DataManager, extracts the prefix before the last ’_’ character, and groups keys by that prefix. Only groups with 2 or more keys are returned.



bool populateTensorFromAnalogKeys(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & tensor_key,
    std::vector< std::string > const & analog_keys
)
Populate an existing TensorData from AnalogTimeSeries channels.
Parameters:

dm DataManager containing the tensor and analog data
tensor_key Key of the TensorData to populate
analog_keys Ordered list of AnalogTimeSeries keys to pack as columns

Return: true if the tensor was successfully populated
Precondition:

dm must contain a TensorData at tensor_key
All analog_keys must exist and contain AnalogTimeSeries
All channels must share the same TimeFrame and sample count

Gathers the specified AnalogTimeSeries channels, packs them into a 2D TensorData via analogToTensor(), and replaces the data at tensor_key. The TimeKey is inherited from the first analog channel.

json JSON string with row_source and columns fields

spec Design specification to serialize

)
Build a lazy TensorData from a design spec without registering it.

dm DataManager containing row source and column source data
spec Design specification

std::optional< TimeKey > resolveOutputTimeKey(
    DataManager & dm,
    TensorDesignSpec const & spec
)
Resolve the TimeKey under which a designed tensor should be registered.
Parameters:

dm DataManager containing row source and timeframe registrations
spec Design specification

Return: Resolved TimeKey, or nullopt when no valid timeframe exists
Uses an explicit non-default spec.output_time_key when present and valid, otherwise the row source’s TimeKey, then "time" or "default" if registered.



bool populateDataManager(
    DataManager & dm,
    TensorDesignSpec const & spec
)
Build a tensor from a design spec and register it in DataManager.
Parameters:

dm DataManager to populate
spec Design specification (tensor_key required)

Return: true if the tensor was built and registered
Precondition: spec.tensor_key must not be empty



ColumnProviderFn buildIntervalPropertyProvider(
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    IntervalProperty property
)
Build a ColumnProviderFn that extracts a property (start, end, or duration) from the row intervals.
Parameters:

intervals Row intervals
property Which property to extract

Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per interval
This does NOT consult any DataManager source — the values come entirely from the interval endpoints.



InvalidationWiringFn buildInvalidationWiringFn(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::vector< std::string > const & source_keys
)
Build an InvalidationWiringFn that registers DataManager observers to invalidate tensor columns when source data changes.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns source data
source_keys Ordered list of DataManager keys, one per column. Empty strings mean “no source dependency” (e.g. interval property columns) and will be skipped.

Return: InvalidationWiringFn suitable for TensorData::createFromLazyColumns()
For each (column_index, source_key) pair, the wiring function registers an observer on the source data. When the source notifies, the wiring callback invalidates the corresponding column and notifies the tensor’s own observers.



ColumnProviderFn buildProviderFromRecipe(
    DataManager & dm,
    ColumnRecipe const & recipe,
    std::vector< TimeFrameIndex > const & row_times,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > const & intervals
)
Build a ColumnProviderFn from a ColumnRecipe.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns source data
recipe Column specification
row_times Row timestamps (for timestamp-row tensors; empty for interval-row)
intervals Row intervals (for interval-row tensors; nullptr for timestamp-row)

Return: ColumnProviderFn
This is the main entry point for building providers from serialized configurations. It dispatches to the appropriate builder based on the recipe’s fields.

Precondition: When params.bucket_count > 0, in.line_start_indices.size() == in.line_vertex_counts.size(). If sizes differ, in is returned unchanged.
Postcondition: Returned batch has the same number of logical lines as in when decimation runs.
For each logical line (parallel line_start_indices / line_vertex_counts), vertices are partitioned into bucket_count uniform buckets along x (or by sample index when x span is degenerate). Each non-empty bucket contributes up to two points: the point with minimum y and the point with maximum y (emit in increasing x order). The first and last vertices of each strip are always included (with consecutive duplicates removed).

Queries the layout response to find the series whose allocated region contains the specified world Y coordinate. Optionally allows a tolerance for selecting series near the boundary.
Example:
LayoutResponse layout = engine.compute(request);
float world_y = screenToWorld(mouse_pos, ...).y;

if (auto result = findSeriesAtWorldY(world_y, layout)) {
    std::cout << "Clicked on series: " << result->series_key << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Position within series: " << result->series_local_y << std::endl;
}



std::optional< SeriesQueryResult > findClosestSeriesAtWorldY(

    LayoutResponse const & layout_response
)

layout_response Layout containing all series positions

Return: SeriesQueryResult for the closest series, std::nullopt if layout is empty

Example:
// User clicked between two series - find the closest one

    highlightSeries(result->series_key);
}

RenderablePolyLineBatch decimatePolyLineBatchMinMax(
    RenderablePolyLineBatch const & in,
    MinMaxDecimationParams params
)
Apply min–max decimation to each line strip in in.
Parameters:

in Source batch (unchanged).
params bucket_count <= 0 returns a copy of in.

Return: Decimated batch; metadata (thickness, model_matrix, colors, entity ids) is copied from in.
Precondition: When params.bucket_count > 0, in.line_start_indices.size() == in.line_vertex_counts.size(). If sizes differ, in is returned unchanged.
Postcondition: Returned batch has the same number of logical lines as in when decimation runs.
For each logical line (parallel line_start_indices / line_vertex_counts), vertices are partitioned into bucket_count uniform buckets along x (or by sample index when x span is degenerate). Each non-empty bucket contributes up to two points: the point with minimum y and the point with maximum y (emit in increasing x order). The first and last vertices of each strip are always included (with consecutive duplicates removed).

Find first time when value crosses threshold.

params Threshold and direction parameters

Template Parameters:

Element Value element type (must have time() and value() accessors)

Return: Time of first crossing, or NaN if no crossing found

Rising: previous value < threshold AND current value >= threshold
Falling: previous value >= threshold AND current value < threshold

ColumnProviderFn buildAnalogSampleAtOffsetProvider(

)
Build a ColumnProviderFn that samples an AnalogTimeSeries at each row timestamp plus a fixed offset.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns the source data

row_times Ordered vector of TimeFrameIndex values (one per row)
offset Time offset to add to each row timestamp (may be negative)

Exceptions:

Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per row
For each row i the provider reads source.getAtTime(row_times[i] + offset). Returns NaN for any sample that falls outside the source range.
This replaces the old AnalogTimestampOffsetsMultiComputer — each offset produces one call to this function, yielding one column.



ColumnProviderFn buildPipelineColumnProvider(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & source_key,
    std::vector< TimeFrameIndex > const & row_times,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline pipeline
)
Build a generic ColumnProviderFn for timestamp-row tensors from any source type.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns the source data
source_key DataManager key for any supported source type
row_times Ordered vector of TimeFrameIndex values (one per row)
pipeline TransformPipeline (may be empty for passthrough)

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the pipeline does not produce float output, has a terminal range reduction, or the source is unavailable

See: buildIntervalPipelineProvider() for interval-row tensors with reductions
Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per row
Works with any DataManager source type (AnalogTimeSeries, MaskData, LineData, PointData, etc.) as long as the pipeline transforms the source into float output (AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries).
Empty pipeline (passthrough): The source must already be a float type (AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries). Samples the source directly at each row timestamp.
Non-empty pipeline: Calls executePipeline() on the full source DataTypeVariant, then samples the resulting AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries at each row timestamp.
Terminal range reductions are rejected — they collapse the entire series to a single scalar, which is not meaningful for timestamp-row columns. For interval-row columns that need range reductions, use buildIntervalPipelineProvider() instead.
Validation is performed at build time via pipelineProducesFloat().



ColumnProviderFn buildIntervalPipelineProvider(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & source_key,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline pipeline
)
Build a generic ColumnProviderFn for interval-row tensors from any source type.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns the source data
source_key DataManager key for any supported source type
intervals Shared pointer to the DigitalIntervalSeries defining rows
pipeline TransformPipeline that must end with a range reduction

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the pipeline does not produce float output, lacks a range reduction, or the source is unavailable

See: buildPipelineColumnProvider() for timestamp-row tensors without reductions
Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per interval
Note: RaggedAnalogTimeSeries sources are not supported (no GatherResult specialisation exists). Passing one will throw at materialization time.
Works with any DataManager source type that satisfies HasDataTraits (AnalogTimeSeries, MaskData, LineData, PointData, DigitalEventSeries, DigitalIntervalSeries) by delegating to gatherAndExecutePipeline().
For each interval row, the function:

Gathers a view/copy of the source data within the interval boundaries
Executes the pipeline on that gathered view
Extracts a single float from the pipeline output via extractSingleFloat()

The pipeline must contain a range reduction that collapses each gathered view to a single scalar. Pipelines without a range reduction are rejected at build time.
Validation is performed at build time via pipelineProducesFloat().

This is the main entry point for building providers from serialized configurations. It dispatches to the appropriate builder based on the recipe’s fields.



InvalidationWiringFn buildInvalidationWiringFn(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::vector< std::string > const & source_keys
)
Build an InvalidationWiringFn that registers DataManager observers to invalidate tensor columns when source data changes.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns source data
source_keys Ordered list of DataManager keys, one per column. Empty strings mean “no source dependency” (e.g. interval property columns) and will be skipped.

Return: InvalidationWiringFn suitable for TensorData::createFromLazyColumns()
For each (column_index, source_key) pair, the wiring function registers an observer on the source data. When the source notifies, the wiring callback invalidates the corresponding column and notifies the tensor’s own observers.

source_key DataManager key for any supported source type
row_times Ordered vector of TimeFrameIndex values (one per row)
pipeline TransformPipeline (may be empty for passthrough)

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the pipeline does not produce float output, has a terminal range reduction, or the source is unavailable

See: buildIntervalPipelineProvider() for interval-row tensors with reductions
Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per row
Works with any DataManager source type (AnalogTimeSeries, MaskData, LineData, PointData, etc.) as long as the pipeline transforms the source into float output (AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries).
Empty pipeline (passthrough): The source must already be a float type (AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries). Samples the source directly at each row timestamp.
Non-empty pipeline: Calls executePipeline() on the full source DataTypeVariant, then samples the resulting AnalogTimeSeries or RaggedAnalogTimeSeries at each row timestamp.
Terminal range reductions are rejected — they collapse the entire series to a single scalar, which is not meaningful for timestamp-row columns. For interval-row columns that need range reductions, use buildIntervalPipelineProvider() instead.
Validation is performed at build time via pipelineProducesFloat().



ColumnProviderFn buildIntervalPipelineProvider(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & source_key,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline pipeline
)
Build a generic ColumnProviderFn for interval-row tensors from any source type.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns the source data
source_key DataManager key for any supported source type
intervals Shared pointer to the DigitalIntervalSeries defining rows
pipeline TransformPipeline that must end with a range reduction

Exceptions:

std::runtime_error if the pipeline does not produce float output, lacks a range reduction, or the source is unavailable

See: buildPipelineColumnProvider() for timestamp-row tensors without reductions
Return: ColumnProviderFn producing one float per interval
Note: RaggedAnalogTimeSeries sources are not supported (no GatherResult specialisation exists). Passing one will throw at materialization time.
Works with any DataManager source type that satisfies HasDataTraits (AnalogTimeSeries, MaskData, LineData, PointData, DigitalEventSeries, DigitalIntervalSeries) by delegating to gatherAndExecutePipeline().
For each interval row, the function:

Gathers a view/copy of the source data within the interval boundaries
Executes the pipeline on that gathered view
Extracts a single float from the pipeline output via extractSingleFloat()

The pipeline must contain a range reduction that collapses each gathered view to a single scalar. Pipelines without a range reduction are rejected at build time.
Validation is performed at build time via pipelineProducesFloat().

    DataManager & dm,
    std::string const & source_key,
    std::shared_ptr< DigitalIntervalSeries const > intervals,
    Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::TransformPipeline pipeline,
    std::vector< Neuralyzer::Transforms::V2::PipelineValueStore > row_stores

    std::vector< TimeFrameIndex > const & row_times,

)

dm DataManager that owns source data
recipe Column specification
row_times Row timestamps (for timestamp-row tensors; empty for interval-row)
intervals Row intervals (for interval-row tensors; nullptr for timestamp-row)

This is the main entry point for building providers from serialized configurations. It dispatches to the appropriate builder based on the recipe’s fields.



InvalidationWiringFn buildInvalidationWiringFn(
    DataManager & dm,
    std::vector< std::string > const & source_keys
)
Build an InvalidationWiringFn that registers DataManager observers to invalidate tensor columns when source data changes.
Parameters:

dm DataManager that owns source data
source_keys Ordered list of DataManager keys, one per column. Empty strings mean “no source dependency” (e.g. interval property columns) and will be skipped.

Return: InvalidationWiringFn suitable for TensorData::createFromLazyColumns()
For each (column_index, source_key) pair, the wiring function registers an observer on the source data. When the source notifies, the wiring callback invalidates the corresponding column and notifies the tensor’s own observers.

title: Neuralyzer
text:
A powerful, cross-platform toolkit for visualizing and analyzing experimental data.
Get Started Download




Experience your data in perfect context. Neuralyzer provides temporally synchronized playback of high-speed video, analog traces, and spike data, reproducing the entire experiment. Navigate seamlessly between different levels of abstraction—from raw data points to complex analysis results—to verify every insight.



Access a comprehensive suite of built-in algorithms for tracking, signal processing, and behavioral quantification. For advanced needs, native Python support allows you to integrate custom analysis routines and instantly visualize the results within the application.



Tame your experimental data. Streamline your workflow from data ingestion to dataset generation. Visualize and create deep learning labels directly on your data, manage complex experimental hierarchies, and export labeled videos for training or presentation.








Master Neuralyzer with our comprehensive collection of tutorials and how-to guides. Explore Resources



Connect with other users, ask questions, and share your feedback on GitHub. GitHub Discussions



Interested in contributing? Dive into our technical guides and API reference. Developer Guide
